about: Reranker corpus: score (request, tool description) pairs. Generated by tools/build_reranker_corpus.py, seed 20261013. Negatives come from the selector's own top-12, not from uniform sampling - the tools that crowd out the answer are the ones it already rates highest.
limit: Evidence for tool RANKING, and for arguments on the 100 of 184 cases that carry them. `ascension_gate` scores right tool AND right arguments, so a run graded by it is answerable on 100 rows and NOT on the 84 with no arguments - a verdict drawn from those rows is a verdict about argument-bearing requests and says nothing about the rest.

train.say: Change one exact piece of text.
train.positives_desc: edit_file: Replace one exact piece of text in one named file. The text to replace must appear exactly once, or nothing is written - the count and line numbers are reported instead of a guess being made. Use this to change a specific line; use find_and_replace to change a string across many files. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, old_string, new_string, preview, replace_all)

negatives.desc: translate_text: Translate text into another language, with the local model when it is running and a web service otherwise. The reply says which was used, because one sends your text to a third party. (arguments: text, to_language, from_language)

undo_last_change: Put a file or a Chronoa setting back the way Chronoa last found it, by restoring the content or value recorded just before Chronoa's own last change to it. Undoes Chronoa's recent writes only - NOT git history, NOT changes you made in an editor or a shell, and only while a recorded pre-image is still held. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, list, setting, steps)

phone: The user's paired phone via GSConnect/KDE Connect: status (reachable, battery), ring it to find it, ping it, share a file or link to it; read text messages ('messages': latest, from a contact, or unread only); send a text message ('send': to a contact name or number, or omit contact to reply to the latest conversation) with exactly the text given - draft it first; or 'call' a contact or number (opens the phone's dialer). The user confirms every message and call before it goes. Requires the 'phone-control-enabled' consent key; reading needs 'phone-messages-read-enabled', sending and calling 'phone-messages-send-enabled'. (arguments: action, device, target, contact, text, unread_only, limit)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

calendar_edit: Change the user's calendar: 'create' adds an event to the default calendar (title, start, optional duration or end, location); 'move' reschedules an event found by its current time and/or title to new_start; 'cancel' deletes one. Times in words: 'tomorrow 3pm', 'friday 5 pm', '2026-10-09 14:00'. Move and cancel ask the person to confirm. Ambiguous matches are refused with the candidates. Requires the 'calendar-write-enabled' consent key (move/cancel also 'calendar-read-enabled'). No invitations are sent. (arguments: action, title, start, duration, end, new_start, location, notes)
encode_text: Encode or decode text: base64, url (percent-encoding), hex, binary, rot13, morse. (arguments: text, scheme, direction)
type_text: Type text at the currently focused window. Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key (separate from the vision sense) to be enabled. (arguments: text)

train.positives_desc: recording: Make subtitles or a transcript of a video or audio file, tell speakers apart, or remove background noise. Works on the sound, on this computer. text: what was said; subtitles: save an .srt beside it; speakers: who said what, turn by turn; clean: a copy with background noise removed; sounds: what can be heard in it (music, a dog, traffic...); listen: what can be heard around the computer right now (the microphone, a few seconds); streams: which applications are carrying audio right now, and the name to capture one by (a call in a browser is one); capture: record one of those for 5-600 seconds and transcribe it - which records the room, so it needs the sound consent like the microphone does. (arguments: action, path, range, language, people, seconds)

negatives.desc: convert_media: Convert an audio, video or image file to another format (mp3, ogg, opus, wav, flac, m4a, mp4, webm, gif, png, jpg, webp), optionally resizing to a width. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to, width)

media_control: Control music and video players: play, pause, toggle, next track, previous track, stop, restart (current track from the beginning), seek (skip ahead or go back by 'seconds'; negative goes back), or 'status' to say what is playing. (arguments: action, seconds)

meeting: Hold a meeting: record the microphone for as long as it takes, transcribe it with who said what, and write notes. 'record': start now and run for the given number of minutes (default 120, the ceiling). 'notes': write notes from a recording that already exists. 'status': what a meeting would do on this machine. The recording, the transcript and the notes are all written on this computer and nothing leaves it. Needs the 'meeting-enabled' consent key, which is off by default - this holds the microphone for possibly hours, with other people speaking. (arguments: action, minutes, path)

speaker_id: Opt-in voice identity using the local speaker model. enrol: remember a person's voice from a 16 kHz mono WAV, with their name and the basis on which they agreed; identify: say which enrolled voice a WAV sounds like; list: names already enrolled; forget: remove one. Needs the hearing consent and an explicit yes for enrol and forget. Nothing about the voice leaves this machine. (arguments: action, name, clip, basis)

edit_audio: Edit a sound file and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, raise or lower the volume, normalize loudness, change speed, or convert to an audio format. End times accept seconds or 'MM:SS'/'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, volume, normalize, speed, to)

open_application: Open or launch an installed application by name or by kind, e.g. 'firefox', 'files', 'settings', 'music player', 'text editor'. Not for websites: use browse to open a site and work on it. (arguments: name)

read_video: Read a video's basics out loud (for subtitles or what was said use recording): how long it is, its resolution, its video codec, whether it has audio, and its bitrate. Add keyframes=true to also save the moments the image changes. The original is never modified. (arguments: path, keyframes)

train.say: Mute or unmute the microphone input.
train.positives_desc: set_mic_mute: Mute or unmute the default microphone input, or report whether it is currently muted. Output volume is a separate skill. Requires the 'mic-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)

negatives.desc: set_privacy: Control the machine's privacy: mute or unmute the microphone, enable or disable a camera, or blank the screen. Muting the microphone is a user-level stream mute that any new application can override, and the reply says so rather than implying the hardware is off. Disabling a camera needs root and is only possible on drivers that expose a disable control, so a device with no such control is reported as unsupported rather than disabled. Blanking works on X11; under Wayland it would need a permission prompt, so the idle timeout is offered instead. Every action says how to undo it. (arguments: action, device)
set_mute: Mute or unmute the sound from the speakers or headphones ('mute the sound', 'unmute'). The microphone is set_mic_mute. (arguments: mute, device)

audio_output: List the speakers/headphones (outputs) and microphones (inputs) and which one is the default, or switch the default output or input - 'play through my headphones', 'use the USB microphone', 'send sound to the HDMI monitor'. Pick a device by its number or part of its name. (arguments: action, device, kind)

phone_remote: Press keys on the paired phone as a Bluetooth keyboard: 'press' the camera 'shutter' (takes a photo in the camera app), play_pause, next, previous, volume_up/down, mute; or 'type' text into whatever field is focused on the phone. The phone must have paired 'Chronoa Remote'. Requires the 'phone-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, key, text)

edit_video: Edit a video and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, resize to a width, rotate, mute or keep only the audio, or change the speed. End times accept seconds ('95'), or 'MM:SS' / 'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, width, rotate, mute, audio_only, speed, output)

get_volume: Get the current volume and mute state of an audio output, or the default one. On a machine with more than one output - several monitors, headphones and a dock - 'the volume' is ambiguous, so pass the device exactly as `wpctl status` prints it to ask about a specific one. (arguments: device)

bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)

train.say: Keep your own notes: add, list, search and remove.
train.positives_desc: notes: Keep your own notes in a plain list stored on this machine: 'add' one from 'text', 'list' them, 'search' by text or id, 'remove' one by 'id'. Never sent to a model. For what the assistant itself believes and uses in its replies, use remember_fact instead. (arguments: action, text, query, id)

negatives.desc: shopping_list: Keep your own shopping list in a plain local file: 'add' an item from 'text', 'list' what is on it, 'check' or 'uncheck' one by 'id', 'remove' one, or 'clear' the list. Checked items stay on the list so you can see what is already in the basket. This is the user's own list and is never sent to a model or a server. (arguments: action, text, id)

search_my_files: Search your own files by their contents - documents, notes, code - either in a directory you choose with Chronoa's own index, or through the desktop's index (LocalSearch on GNOME, Baloo on Plasma). 'search' (default): what matches a few words. 'desktop': ask the desktop's index instead, needing 'document-search-enabled'. 'reindex': read the directory and build or refresh Chronoa's index (needed before the first search). 'status': what would be indexed and whether this machine can search by meaning. Needs the 'file-index-enabled' consent key for its own index. (arguments: action, query, kind, path, limit)

todo_list: Keep a list of tasks that survives between turns and restarts: add an item, change its status, mark what it is blocked by, or list what is outstanding. Use this to track a multi-step job rather than holding it in the conversation. Requires the 'todo-list-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, id, content, status, blocked_by)

reminders: A dated list of reminders you can keep coming back to: add one, list what is still due, mark one done, or remove one. Optionally with a due time in words, e.g. 'tomorrow 9am' or 'in 3 hours'. (arguments: action, number, text, due)

conversations: The user's saved Chronoa conversations. list: recent ones; search: find what was said in earlier conversations (query); open: continue one (which = title or id); new: start a fresh one; rename (which, title); copy: duplicate one to try another way, optionally keeping only its first keep_turns user messages; export: save one as Markdown (path); delete: remove one permanently (needs 'file-delete-enabled'). (arguments: action, which, query, title, path, keep_turns)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Use 'setpoints' to list built-in off-by-default proposals, 'describe-setpoint' to explain one, and 'arm-setpoint' to arm one whose own switch is already on; arming never switches one on. Listing and describing need no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds, setpoint)

search_file_contents: Search inside text files under a directory for a literal string, and report which files contain it and on which lines. Skips binary files and very large files, and says how many it skipped. (arguments: text, path, file_pattern, case_sensitive, max_matches)

train.positives_desc: list_directory: List the files and folders in a directory, with each one's type and size. Use this to see what is in a folder before opening, moving or deleting anything in it. (arguments: path, include_hidden)

negatives.desc: download_file: Download a file from a web address and save it to disk, reporting the size and how long it took. Use for 'download that file', 'get this installer', 'save that page'. Only http and https; a site that answers with an error page reports that rather than saving the error as if it were the file. (arguments: url, destination, engine)

directory_tree: Show the shape of a directory as a nested tree, with each entry's type. Use this to understand how a project or folder is laid out before opening files in it. Reports what it skipped and when it stopped early. (arguments: path, max_depth, include_hidden)

sync_folder: Sync one folder to another, sending only what changed - and show the plan first, before anything is copied. Use for 'copy my files to the server', 'sync these folders', 'what would change if I synced'. Does not delete anything at the destination unless you ask it to, and asks first even then. (arguments: source, destination, apply, delete)

'reindex': read the directory and build or refresh Chronoa's index (needed before the first search). 'status': what would be indexed and whether this machine can search by meaning. Needs the 'file-index-enabled' consent key for its own index. (arguments: action, query, kind, path, limit)
create_directory: Create a directory, and any missing parent directories. Succeeds without complaint if it already exists. (arguments: path)

find_files: Find files and folders by name under a directory, using a wildcard pattern such as '*.log' or 'report*'. Matches on the name only and never opens the files. To see what is in one folder, use list_directory. (arguments: pattern, path, include_hidden, max_results, details)

chart: Make an SVG file from data, drawn on this computer with no install. chart: kind=bar|line|pie with data (bar/pie: [[label, number], ...]; line: [[x, y], ...], or several lines as series {name: [[x, y], ...]}), plus title, x_label, y_label. icon: a stroke icon by name (arrow-right, bell, calendar, check, clock, close, download, folder, heart, home, mail, search, settings, star, user). diagram: a top-to-bottom flow, steps=["Read", "Edit", "Test"] with optional arrows [[from, to, label], ...]. output is the .svg path, e.g. '~/Pictures/sales.svg'. (arguments: action, output, kind, data, series, steps, arrows, name, title, x_label, y_label)

train.positives_desc: read_text_file: Read a text file and return its contents, optionally a range of lines. Use this to see what a file actually says. (arguments: path, start_line, max_lines)

negatives.desc: todo_list: Keep a list of tasks that survives between turns and restarts: add an item, change its status, mark what it is blocked by, or list what is outstanding. Use this to track a multi-step job rather than holding it in the conversation. Requires the 'todo-list-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, id, content, status, blocked_by)
convert_document: Convert a document between markdown, plain text, and HTML. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to)
create_document: Create a document from a title and body: a markdown file, a plain text file, or an HTML page. Writes a new file; never overwrites. (arguments: title, body, format, path)

notes: Keep your own notes in a plain list stored on this machine: 'add' one from 'text', 'list' them, 'search' by text or id, 'remove' one by 'id'. Never sent to a model. For what the assistant itself believes and uses in its replies, use remember_fact instead. (arguments: action, text, query, id)

'record': start now and run for the given number of minutes (default 120, the ceiling). 'notes': write notes from a recording that already exists. 'status': what a meeting would do on this machine. get_file_info: Report one file's type, size, when it was last modified, and who can read it. Use this to answer 'when did I last edit this' or 'who else can read this file' - no other skill reports timestamps or permissions. (arguments: path)

train.positives_desc: compute_hash: Compute a checksum of a file, and optionally compare it with an expected value. Defaults to SHA-256, which is what package managers and download sites publish. (arguments: path, algorithm, expected)

negatives.desc: delete_file: Delete a file or folder by moving it to the desktop trash, where it stays recoverable. This is how you clear something out. The whole folder goes as one item and can be restored from the trash - nothing in this project is deleted permanently, so there is no faster or 'real' delete to reach for instead. Requires the 'file-delete-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path)

Only http and https; a site that answers with an error page reports that rather than saving the error as if it were the file. (arguments: url, destination, engine)

identify_file: Identify a file by reading its first bytes rather than trusting its name. Use for 'why won't this open', 'what is this file', 'is this really a PNG', 'this file has no extension'. Reports the detected format and whether the filename agrees with it, which is the usual cause of a file refusing to open in the program its name implies. Says plainly when a signature is unrecognised. Read-only. (arguments: path)

move_or_copy_file: Move or copy a file or directory to a new path. Moving a directory into itself is refused, and an existing destination is not overwritten unless asked. (arguments: source, destination, mode, overwrite)

open_file: Open one specific file or folder (by its path) using the desktop's default application for it - the same thing double-clicking it would do. To launch an app such as the file manager, use open_application. (arguments: path)

train.positives_desc: find_and_replace: Find a string across files under a directory and optionally replace it. Reports what it would change without changing anything unless dry_run is explicitly false. Requires the 'bulk-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: find, replace, path, file_pattern, dry_run, case_sensitive)

negatives.desc: office_document: Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx) and PowerPoint (.pptx) files; also reads .odt/.ods/.odp. read: text with headings, tables, one section per sheet or slide (sheet, cell_range like A1:D20, formulas=true to see formulas). create: a new file from content - for .docx Markdown-style text (# headings, - bullets, 1. lists, | tables |, **bold**); for .xlsx rows (list of lists), or sheets {name: rows}, or CSV/Markdown-table text in content, '=...' cells are formulas; for .pptx slides [{title, bullets[], subtitle}]. set_cells: values {'B12': 42, 'C1': 'Total'} in a sheet. replace_text / append: change a .docx. pdf_images: save a PDF's embedded pictures to a folder. Changing an existing file needs 'file-edit-enabled' and can be undone with undo_last_change. (arguments: action, path, content, rows, sheets, chart, slides, values, sheet, cell_range, formulas, find, replace, title, overwrite, output_dir)

find_device: Make a paired Bluetooth watch, band or tag buzz or ring so the person can find it - 'where is my watch', 'find my band'. Works on devices with the standard Immediate Alert service and on MoYoung (Da Fit) watches; anything else is refused rather than sent an unknown command. The device must be in range. Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: device)
find_emoji: Find an emoji or symbol by name (heart, thumbs up, rupee sign, arrow) and copy the best match to the clipboard. (arguments: name)

find_files: Find files and folders by name under a directory, using a wildcard pattern such as '*.log' or 'report*'. Matches on the name only and never opens the files. To see what is in one folder, use list_directory. (arguments: pattern, path, include_hidden, max_results, details)

find_recently_modified: List files under a directory whose recorded modification time is within the last N days, newest first. Use this to answer 'what did I change today'. This is a timestamp, so a tool that preserves or sets times (tar, rsync, cp -p) can move an entry without the content changing. (arguments: path, within_days, pattern, limit)

edit_file: Replace one exact piece of text in one named file. Use this to change a specific line; use find_and_replace to change a string across many files. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, old_string, new_string, preview, replace_all)

list_shortcuts: List this machine's keyboard shortcuts, or find what one key does. Reads GNOME's two keybinding schemas, so it covers both window management and the hardware media keys, and reports that the scheme does not apply on a desktop that does not use it rather than listing defaults for a desktop that is not running. Reading a shortcut is not a change and needs no permission. (arguments: action, keys)

train.say: Commit notes.txt with the message 'update the notes'.

Requires the 'git-write-enabled' consent key. Pushing is a separate skill: that publishes. (arguments: files, message, path)

photos: Find the user's photos by what is in them or written on them, or when they were taken. search: query like 'receipt hardware shop', 'dog on the beach', 'december 2025'; index: update the index of the Pictures folder (a batch at a time); status: how much is indexed. (arguments: action, query, captions)

snapshot_status: Whether this Shanios machine can roll back: the OS version, which blue/green slot was booted, which slot boots next, the previous slot a rollback would return to, any recorded boot failure or pending reboot, and the btrfs snapshots on disk. Use for 'can I undo the update', 'which slot am I on', 'is an update waiting'. The snapshot list uses the 'snapshots-sense-enabled' switch. Read-only.

focus_window: Bring a window to the front and give it keyboard focus, by window id from list_windows or by matching part of its title. Works on X11 and Plasma; on GNOME it needs Chronoa's window control extension and says so. (arguments: window_id, title_contains)

open_settings: Open the system Settings app at a specific page, e.g. 'wifi', 'bluetooth', 'display', 'sound', 'power', 'privacy', 'keyboard', 'mouse', 'touchpad', 'printers', 'users', 'about', 'date_time', 'region', 'notifications', 'background', 'accessibility'. GNOME and KDE Plasma. Use open_application for Settings without a page. (arguments: page)

train.say: Openblaze demo.com and find the cheapest flight from Boston to London.
train.positives_desc: browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

negatives.desc: web_search: Look something up on the web and return what the pages actually say: facts, prices, how-tos, anything no more specific tool covers. Give a search query, a specific URL, or both. For a scholarly question - a paper, a preprint, prior work, 'what does the research say' - set source=arxiv and it searches the arXiv preprint archive instead of the web. For news headlines use news; to click, fill in or book something on a site use browse. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: query, url, source)

find_and_replace: Find a string across files under a directory and optionally replace it. Reports what it would change without changing anything unless dry_run is explicitly false. Requires the 'bulk-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: find, replace, path, file_pattern, dry_run, case_sensitive)

find_files: Find files and folders by name under a directory, using a wildcard pattern such as '*.log' or 'report*'. Matches on the name only and never opens the files. To see what is in one folder, use list_directory. (arguments: pattern, path, include_hidden, max_results, details)

search_file_contents: Search inside text files under a directory for a literal string, and report which files contain it and on which lines. Skips binary files and very large files, and says how many it skipped. (arguments: text, path, file_pattern, case_sensitive, max_matches)

search_my_files: Search your own files by their contents - documents, notes, code - either in a directory you choose with Chronoa's own index, or through the desktop's index (LocalSearch on GNOME, Baloo on Plasma). 'search' (default): what matches a few words. 'desktop': ask the desktop's index instead, needing 'document-search-enabled'. 'reindex': read the directory and build or refresh Chronoa's index (needed before the first search). 'status': what would be indexed and whether this machine can search by meaning. Needs the 'file-index-enabled' consent key for its own index. (arguments: action, query, kind, path, limit)

maps: OpenStreetMap maps: find where a place is ('find'), driving/walking/cycling directions ('directions') or just distance and time ('travel_time') between places, the nearest kind of place such as petrol pump, hotel, ATM or hospital ('nearby'), or open a place or route on the map in the browser ('open'). Times are typical, without live traffic. With no origin, 'here' is this computer's location. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off; 'here' also needs the location sense. (arguments: action, place, destination, origin, mode, what, near, limit)

find_device: Make a paired Bluetooth watch, band or tag buzz or ring so the person can find it - 'where is my watch', 'find my band'. Works on devices with the standard Immediate Alert service and on MoYoung (Da Fit) watches; anything else is refused rather than sent an unknown command. The device must be in range. Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: device)
find_emoji: Find an emoji or symbol by name (heart, thumbs up, rupee sign, arrow) and copy the best match to the clipboard. (arguments: name)

train.positives_desc: install_app: Search Flathub for an app, or install / remove one for this user by its app ID (e.g. org.videolan.VLC, from a search). Installing and removing need the 'app-install-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, query, app_id)

negatives.desc: list_apps: List the applications installed on this machine, optionally filtered by a search term, so a request to open something can be answered with what actually exists rather than a guess. (arguments: search)

install_model: Download a named model into the local Ollama. Takes an explicit model name and never picks one by itself - call recommend_model first and install only what the user agreed to. Warns rather than refuses when the model looks larger than available memory. This downloads gigabytes and needs the network. (arguments: name)

android_device: An Android phone connected with USB debugging (adb). devices: which are connected; info: model, Android version, battery, storage; screenshot: save the phone's screen as a PNG; apps: installed apps (query filters); push: copy a file to the phone (to, default /sdcard/Download); pull: copy a file from the phone; open_url: open a web link on the phone. Requires 'phone-control-enabled'. (arguments: action, serial, path, to, url, query, output)

default_apps: Show or change which application opens a kind of file - by MIME type ('application/pdf'), extension ('.pdf', 'mp4') or an example file - or the default web browser (target 'browser'). Use for 'what opens PDFs', 'make VLC open my videos', 'set Firefox as my default browser'. Changing a default requires the 'default-apps-enabled' consent key; showing one does not. (arguments: target, action, app)

lan_phone: Find phones on the SAME Wi-Fi network, using the KDE Connect protocol directly - so it works without KDE Connect or GSConnect installed. 'devices': what announced itself on this network in the last few seconds (phones, tablets, other computers). 'announce': make this computer findable by a phone's KDE Connect app. 'status': what this computer can and cannot do on the LAN. 'pair': pair with the device 'devices' found (the phone asks its owner). Needs the 'lan-phone-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, seconds)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Use 'setpoints' to list built-in off-by-default proposals, 'describe-setpoint' to explain one, and 'arm-setpoint' to arm one whose own switch is already on; arming never switches one on. Listing and describing need no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds, setpoint)

ui_elements: Use another app's controls by what they are, through the accessibility tree. apps: which apps are reachable. inspect: list a window's buttons, fields, menus and labels with ids (app = its name; query narrows by text). press: activate an element by id (a button, checkbox, link, menu item). set_text: put text in a field by id. read: an element's text or value. menu: open a menu path like 'File > Export'. drive: one turn of driving - give an action and a control number and the reply is the app's new state in the same short numbered form, which is what a small model can act on. act: click, type or key an app by name or position, with a visible cursor. state: the numbered controls an app is showing. Works on a container's app and on this desktop's own apps alike. Requires 'input-control-enabled'; drive start also runs a container, so it needs 'container-control-enabled' as well. (arguments: action, app, id, text, query, path, do, how, number, image, keys, x, y)

train.say: What is plugged in, and Thunderbolt docks.
train.positives_desc: usb_devices: What is plugged into this machine's USB ports (mice, phones, webcams, sticks, with their speed), and every Thunderbolt/USB4 device with whether it is authorised to work. Use for 'what's plugged in', 'why doesn't my dock work', 'is my webcam connected'. The USB list uses the 'usb-sense-enabled' switch. Read-only.

negatives.desc: charger_info: Report what is powering this machine: on battery or plugged in, AC adapter or USB-C, whether USB Power Delivery is in use, and the charger's wattage when the firmware reports it, plus battery charge and rate.

firmware_updates: List firmware updates fwupd knows for this machine's devices (BIOS, SSD, dock, touchpad...) and what each fixes, plus the firmware versions this machine is running. Read-only; nothing is installed.

get_volume: Get the current volume and mute state of an audio output, or the default one. On a machine with more than one output - several monitors, headphones and a dock - 'the volume' is ambiguous, so pass the device exactly as `wpctl status` prints it to ask about a specific one. (arguments: device)

train.positives_desc: spell_word: Check how a word is spelled, offline, and suggest the closest correct spellings - 'how do you spell necessary', 'is it recieve or receive'. (arguments: word)

negatives.desc: define_word: What a word means, from Wiktionary. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off. (arguments: word)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

ask_user: Ask the user a clarifying question and wait for their answer, with 2 to 4 short options they can pick. Use this whenever a request is genuinely ambiguous - especially when several files or devices could match. Do not guess instead, and do not ask when one option is obviously right. In a headless session there is nobody to answer and this will say so. (arguments: question, options)

calendar_edit: Change the user's calendar: 'create' adds an event to the default calendar (title, start, optional duration or end, location); 'move' reschedules an event found by its current time and/or title to new_start; 'cancel' deletes one. Times in words: 'tomorrow 3pm', 'friday 5 pm', '2026-10-09 14:00'. Move and cancel ask the person to confirm. Ambiguous matches are refused with the candidates. Requires the 'calendar-write-enabled' consent key (move/cancel also 'calendar-read-enabled'). No invitations are sent. (arguments: action, title, start, duration, end, new_start, location, notes)

conversations: The user's saved Chronoa conversations. list: recent ones; search: find what was said in earlier conversations (query); open: continue one (which = title or id); new: start a fresh one; rename (which, title); copy: duplicate one to try another way, optionally keeping only its first keep_turns user messages; export: save one as Markdown (path); delete: remove one permanently (needs 'file-delete-enabled'). (arguments: action, which, query, title, path, keep_turns)
generate_password: Generate a strong random password, or a passphrase of random words, and copy it to the clipboard (it is never said or shown in the reply). (arguments: kind, length, symbols)

look_at_image: Look at a picture file and say what it shows, with the local vision model: objects, scenes, charts, screenshots, UI, handwriting. Use a prompt to ask something specific about it. For the exact words printed in a picture, use read_document. Needs the vision sense. (arguments: path, prompt)

train.positives_desc: create_directory: Create a directory, and any missing parent directories. Succeeds without complaint if it already exists. (arguments: path)

negatives.desc: list_directory: List the files and folders in a directory, with each one's type and size. Use this to see what is in a folder before opening, moving or deleting anything in it. (arguments: path, include_hidden)

create_archive: Create a zip or tar.gz archive from files or folders, or list or safely extract an existing one. Refuses archives whose entries would escape the destination. (arguments: action, source, destination, format)

create_video: Create a video: a slideshow from a list of pictures (each shown for a few seconds), or a simple clip of a colour for a duration. Writes a new .mp4 next to the inputs; never overwrites. (arguments: images, seconds, color, duration, width)

directory_tree: Show the shape of a directory as a nested tree, with each entry's type. Use this to understand how a project or folder is laid out before opening files in it. Reports what it skipped and when it stopped early. (arguments: path, max_depth, include_hidden)
create_document: Create a document from a title and body: a markdown file, a plain text file, or an HTML page. Writes a new file; never overwrites. (arguments: title, body, format, path)

sync_folder: Sync one folder to another, sending only what changed - and show the plan first, before anything is copied. Use for 'copy my files to the server', 'sync these folders', 'what would change if I synced'. Does not delete anything at the destination unless you ask it to, and asks first even then. (arguments: source, destination, apply, delete)

'search' (default): what matches a few words. 'desktop': ask the desktop's index instead, needing 'document-search-enabled'. 'reindex': read the directory and build or refresh Chronoa's index (needed before the first search). 'status': what would be indexed and whether this machine can search by meaning. Needs the 'file-index-enabled' consent key for its own index. (arguments: action, query, kind, path, limit)

train.positives_desc: manage_mount: Mount an unmounted filesystem or drive, or unmount one, through the desktop's own disk service so its authorisation rules apply. Verifies the result against the mount table. Requires the 'mount-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, device)

negatives.desc: disk_health: Health of this machine's drives (SMART/NVMe status and wear where it can be read) and whether each mounted filesystem - /, /home and the rest - sits on an encrypted (LUKS) volume. Use for 'is my SSD healthy', 'is my disk encrypted', 'how worn is my drive'. Drive health uses the 'storage-sense-enabled' switch. Read-only.

train.positives_desc: calculate: Evaluate arithmetic and percentages ('15% of 2400'), or convert between units. Handles the four operations, powers, parentheses, factorial, permutations and combinations (perm/nPr, comb/nCr), gcd, lcm, sqrt, exp, log, ln, trig and inverse trig, and pi/e/tau - exact for whole numbers. For algebra with variables, derivatives, integrals, limits or equations, use solve_math. Converts length, mass, volume, time, data, pressure, frequency, power, energy and temperature, in the units a person actually meets - say '200 km to miles' or '70kg in lb'. Runs entirely on this machine with no network call. Refuses to guess: a percentage needs a number to apply to, and converting between quantities that measure different things is an error rather than a number. (arguments: expression)

edit_audio: Edit a sound file and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, raise or lower the volume, normalize loudness, change speed, or convert to an audio format. End times accept seconds or 'MM:SS'/'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, volume, normalize, speed, to)

edit_video: Edit a video and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, resize to a width, rotate, mute or keep only the audio, or change the speed. End times accept seconds ('95'), or 'MM:SS' / 'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, width, rotate, mute, audio_only, speed, output)

find_recently_modified: List files under a directory whose recorded modification time is within the last N days, newest first. Use this to answer 'what did I change today'. This is a timestamp, so a tool that preserves or sets times (tar, rsync, cp -p) can move an entry without the content changing. (arguments: path, within_days, pattern, limit)

(arguments: action, place, destination, origin, mode, what, near, limit)

train.say: Steps, sleep, stress, heart rate, SpO2 and settings on your watch.
train.positives_desc: watch: Your MoYoung/Da Fit smartwatch: 'summary' (steps, distance, calories for 3 days, last night's sleep stages, today's stress, workouts), 'measure' a heart rate, blood oxygen or blood pressure on the wrist (takes up to a minute), read 'settings', 'set' one (step_goal, time_format 12h/24h, units metric/imperial, raise_to_wake, sedentary_reminder, other_app_notifications, power_saving, heart_rate_auto_interval, do_not_disturb '22:00-07:00'), 'sync_time', 'find' (make the watch ring), 'notify' (show a message on the watch), or set the 'profile' (height, weight, age, gender - weight is never measured by the watch). Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, device, what, setting, value, sender, text, kind, height_cm, weight_kg, age, gender)

negatives.desc: power_action: Suspend (sleep), hibernate, restart or shut down this computer, or cancel a scheduled restart/shutdown. Restart and shutdown happen after one minute and can be cancelled. Requires the 'power-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

open_settings: Open the system Settings app at a specific page, e.g. 'wifi', 'bluetooth', 'display', 'sound', 'power', 'privacy', 'keyboard', 'mouse', 'touchpad', 'printers', 'users', 'about', 'date_time', 'region', 'notifications', 'background', 'accessibility'. GNOME and KDE Plasma. Use open_application for Settings without a page. (arguments: page)

bluetooth_gatt: Read what a paired Bluetooth Low Energy device says about itself - a watch's or headset's battery, a heart-rate strap's live reading, which services a band offers. 'list': every paired device and whether it speaks this protocol. 'services': what one exposes. 'read': one stored value. 'listen': a live reading of something the device only pushes, e.g. heart rate - 'nothing arrived' is the truthful answer when the device is not measuring. Speakers, headphones and car stereios are older Bluetooth and expose nothing here, which is a true answer, not a failure; wearables, bands, straps, smart tags and thermometers answer. Needs 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' and the device must be connected. (arguments: action, device, seconds, characteristic)

chart: Make an SVG file from data, drawn on this computer with no install. chart: kind=bar|line|pie with data (bar/pie: [[label, number], ...]; line: [[x, y], ...], or several lines as series {name: [[x, y], ...]}), plus title, x_label, y_label. icon: a stroke icon by name (arrow-right, bell, calendar, check, clock, close, download, folder, heart, home, mail, search, settings, star, user). diagram: a top-to-bottom flow, steps=["Read", "Edit", "Test"] with optional arrows [[from, to, label], ...]. output is the .svg path, e.g. '~/Pictures/sales.svg'. (arguments: action, output, kind, data, series, steps, arrows, name, title, x_label, y_label)

set_power_profile: Switch the machine between its power profiles - typically power-saver, balanced and performance - and report which one is active now. The profile list is read from the machine rather than assumed, because which profiles exist depends on the CPU driver: switching to one the machine does not have is refused with the valid names listed. Changes the CPU and platform power behaviour, not a per-application setting. (arguments: profile)

For algebra with variables, derivatives, integrals, limits or equations, use solve_math. train.positives_desc: lock_screen: Lock this session so a password is needed to come back to it. Uses the session's own mechanism so the same thing happens as the desktop's Lock button. Requires the 'screen-lock-enabled' consent key.

negatives.desc: screen_to_phone: Show this computer's screen on a paired phone, over the Bluetooth network. 'status': could this be shared here at all, and what is missing if not. 'start': ask the desktop to share the screen and serve it to the phone - the desktop shows its own 'Share screen' dialog, which only the person can answer. 'stop': end it and close the portal session. The picture goes over Bluetooth, so it is not on Wi-Fi, but it is the whole screen - which is why this needs the 'screen-share-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

set_screensaver: Report or change how long the machine waits before the screen blanks, and whether it then demands a password. The two are reported separately, because blanking without locking leaves anyone who walks up to the machine able to use it. Requires the 'idle-timeout-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, blank_after_minutes, lock)

accessibility: Turn an accessibility feature on or off, or report them all: screen reader, on-screen keyboard, magnifier (zoom), large text, high contrast, reduce motion (animations), sticky keys. (arguments: feature, enabled)

set_privacy: Control the machine's privacy: mute or unmute the microphone, enable or disable a camera, or blank the screen. Muting the microphone is a user-level stream mute that any new application can override, and the reply says so rather than implying the hardware is off. Disabling a camera needs root and is only possible on drivers that expose a disable control, so a device with no such control is reported as unsupported rather than disabled. Blanking works on X11; under Wayland it would need a permission prompt, so the idle timeout is offered instead. Every action says how to undo it. (arguments: action, device)

Requires 'phone-control-enabled'. (arguments: action, serial, path, to, url, query, output)

arrange_window: Arrange a window: tile (snap it to the left, right, top or bottom half of the screen - 'put it on the left half', side by side), minimize, maximize, unmaximize, make fullscreen, leave fullscreen, move, resize, or send it to another workspace - by window id from list_windows or by part of its title. tile takes side; move takes x and y, resize width and height (pixels), set_workspace a 0-based workspace. Nothing is closed; close_window does that. (arguments: action, window_id, title_contains, x, y, width, height, workspace, side)

train.say: Call through a paired phone, on this computer's speakers.
train.positives_desc: bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)

negatives.desc: landline_call: Place and answer calls on the JioFiber broadband landline over Wi-Fi, through the router - the same line the JioJoin app uses, the house's own landline number. 'status' says whether the line is connected and what call is on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+911234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' picks up a ringing call; 'hangup' ends, cancels or declines the current call. The voice is on this computer's speaker and microphone, nothing is recorded, and the landline handset keeps working. Needs this computer added to the line on the Shani Link app's Phone page and the 'landline-enabled' consent key. This is the landline, not a mobile over Bluetooth - that is 'bluetooth_call'. (arguments: action, number, name)

phone: The user's paired phone via GSConnect/KDE Connect: status (reachable, battery), ring it to find it, ping it, share a file or link to it; read text messages ('messages': latest, from a contact, or unread only); send a text message ('send': to a contact name or number, or omit contact to reply to the latest conversation) with exactly the text given - draft it first; or 'call' a contact or number (opens the phone's dialer). The user confirms every message and call before it goes. Requires the 'phone-control-enabled' consent key; reading needs 'phone-messages-read-enabled', sending and calling 'phone-messages-send-enabled'. (arguments: action, device, target, contact, text, unread_only, limit)

lan_phone: Find phones on the SAME Wi-Fi network, using the KDE Connect protocol directly - so it works without KDE Connect or GSConnect installed. 'devices': what announced itself on this network in the last few seconds (phones, tablets, other computers). 'announce': make this computer findable by a phone's KDE Connect app. 'status': what this computer can and cannot do on the LAN. 'pair': pair with the device 'devices' found (the phone asks its owner). Needs the 'lan-phone-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, seconds)

screen_to_phone: Show this computer's screen on a paired phone, over the Bluetooth network. 'status': could this be shared here at all, and what is missing if not. The phone must have paired 'Chronoa Remote'. Requires the 'phone-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, key, text)

recording: Make subtitles or a transcript of a video or audio file, tell speakers apart, or remove background noise. Works on the sound, on this computer. text: what was said; subtitles: save an .srt beside it; speakers: who said what, turn by turn; clean: a copy with background noise removed; sounds: what can be heard in it (music, a dog, traffic...); listen: what can be heard around the computer right now (the microphone, a few seconds); streams: which applications are carrying audio right now, and the name to capture one by (a call in a browser is one); capture: record one of those for 5-600 seconds and transcribe it - which records the room, so it needs the sound consent like the microphone does. (arguments: action, path, range, language, people, seconds)

adb_workflow: A small Android Debug Bridge workflow. status: connected devices and their state; pair: the steps to authorise this computer; push and pull: copy one file between this computer and the phone. Needs 'phone-control-enabled' and a yes for each copy. Local paths stay inside your home; remote paths must be under /sdcard/. (arguments: action, serial, local, remote)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Use 'setpoints' to list built-in off-by-default proposals, 'describe-setpoint' to explain one, and 'arm-setpoint' to arm one whose own switch is already on; arming never switches one on. Listing and describing need no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds, setpoint)

bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)
screenshot: Capture the screen to a PNG file and return the path it was saved to. Refuses when there is no display.

train.positives_desc: convert_media: Convert an audio, video or image file to another format (mp3, ogg, opus, wav, flac, m4a, mp4, webm, gif, png, jpg, webp), optionally resizing to a width. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to, width)

negatives.desc: photo_video: Blur or pixelate faces, blur or remove the background, or find people and objects in a photo or video. Works by what is in it, on this computer. identify: find faces and everyday objects (people, cars, dogs, cups...); effect: blur_faces, pixelate_faces, blur_background or remove_background, saved as a new file (videos keep their sound); keyframes: save the moments a video changes; describe: say what happens in a video. For a look like sepia or sketch, or resizing and converting, use edit_image or convert_media. (arguments: action, path, effect, subject, labelled_copy)

media_control: Control music and video players: play, pause, toggle, next track, previous track, stop, restart (current track from the beginning), seek (skip ahead or go back by 'seconds'; negative goes back), or 'status' to say what is playing. (arguments: action, seconds)

create_video: Create a video: a slideshow from a list of pictures (each shown for a few seconds), or a simple clip of a colour for a duration. Writes a new .mp4 next to the inputs; never overwrites. (arguments: images, seconds, color, duration, width)

edit_video: Edit a video and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, resize to a width, rotate, mute or keep only the audio, or change the speed. End times accept seconds ('95'), or 'MM:SS' / 'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, width, rotate, mute, audio_only, speed, output)

read_video: Read a video's basics out loud (for subtitles or what was said use recording): how long it is, its resolution, its video codec, whether it has audio, and its bitrate. Add keyframes=true to also save the moments the image changes. The original is never modified. (arguments: path, keyframes)

edit_audio: Edit a sound file and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, raise or lower the volume, normalize loudness, change speed, or convert to an audio format. End times accept seconds or 'MM:SS'/'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, volume, normalize, speed, to)

search_my_files: Search your own files by their contents - documents, notes, code - either in a directory you choose with Chronoa's own index, or through the desktop's index (LocalSearch on GNOME, Baloo on Plasma). 'search' (default): what matches a few words. 'desktop': ask the desktop's index instead, needing 'document-search-enabled'. 'reindex': read the directory and build or refresh Chronoa's index (needed before the first search). 'status': what would be indexed and whether this machine can search by meaning. Needs the 'file-index-enabled' consent key for its own index. (arguments: action, query, kind, path, limit)

train.positives_desc: screenshot: Capture the screen to a PNG file and return the path it was saved to. Refuses when there is no display.

negatives.desc: take_photo: Take a photo or selfie with the webcam and save it to the Pictures folder, optionally after a countdown in seconds (0-30). Requires the vision/camera consent. Not for screenshots (use screenshot) or video (use capture_video). (arguments: countdown, path, device, infrared)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

android_device: An Android phone connected with USB debugging (adb). devices: which are connected; info: model, Android version, battery, storage; screenshot: save the phone's screen as a PNG; apps: installed apps (query filters); push: copy a file to the phone (to, default /sdcard/Download); pull: copy a file from the phone; open_url: open a web link on the phone. Requires 'phone-control-enabled'. (arguments: action, serial, path, to, url, query, output)

json_query: Ask questions about the shape of a JSON document: what keys it has, what a field contains, how many entries an array has, or the sum/unique/sorted values of an array. Give either a file path or paste the document itself. (arguments: path, document, field, operation, of)

look_at_image: Look at a picture file and say what it shows, with the local vision model: objects, scenes, charts, screenshots, UI, handwriting. Use a prompt to ask something specific about it. For the exact words printed in a picture, use read_document. Needs the vision sense. (arguments: path, prompt)

resolve_conflict: Work out what is conflicting in a git repository and resolve it. 'show' lists every unmerged file and prints all three sides git holds - the common ancestor, your side and theirs - so there is no guessing about which is which; 'ours' and 'theirs' take a whole side of the named files and mark them resolved; 'mark' marks files you have edited by hand; 'abort' abandons the merge, rebase or cherry-pick and leaves the commits to try again. There is no automatic merge, because deciding which line is right is a judgement about the code and only you can make it. Reading needs 'git-sense-enabled'; changing the working tree needs 'git-write-enabled'. (arguments: action, path, paths)

set_timer: Set a countdown timer that sends a desktop notification when it finishes; list pending timers, say how much time is left, add or take off time, pause, resume, reset to the original length, and cancel. With one timer pending, 'my timer' needs no id. The countdown is owned by systemd, so it fires even if the assistant is closed. It is refused rather than silently accepted when systemd is unavailable, because a timer recorded as pending that will never fire is the same lie as a camera reported as disabled when it is not. (arguments: action, seconds, label, id)

train.say: What is conflicting in a git repository, and resolve it.
train.positives_desc: resolve_conflict: Work out what is conflicting in a git repository and resolve it. Reading needs 'git-sense-enabled'; changing the working tree needs 'git-write-enabled'. (arguments: action, path, paths)

negatives.desc: git_inspect: Report a git working tree: what has changed and is not committed, the diff of those changes, recent commits, or the current branch and how far it is from its upstream; also the stashed work and the reflog (the record that survives rebases and amends). Reports UNKNOWN - never 'clean tree' - when git is missing, the folder is not a repository, or git fails. Requires the 'git-sense-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, subcommand, revision, since, context_lines)

git_push: Push a branch to a named remote. Requires the 'git-push-enabled' consent key, and asks before every push. The remote must be one the repository already has, and must be named - there is no default and no 'push everything'. Force-pushing is refused. (arguments: remote, branch, set_upstream, path)

git_commit: Commit the files you name in a git repository, with a message. Only the paths given are staged - nothing is swept up from the rest of the tree. Requires the 'git-write-enabled' consent key. Pushing is a separate skill: that publishes. (arguments: files, message, path)
git_branch: Create a branch in a git repository and switch to it, or switch to a branch that already exists. Requires the 'git-write-enabled' consent key. (arguments: name, path)

vcs_status: What state a checkout is in, for git, subversion or mercurial: which version control system it belongs to, the branch or revision, the repository it points at, and what has changed. Use when the answer might not be git - 'what is this folder's state', 'which repository is this', 'what changed in my checkout'. Read-only; runs nothing that modifies a repository. (arguments: path)

list_fonts: List the font families installed on this machine (optionally only those whose name contains some text), and which real font the generic names - sans-serif, serif, monospace, emoji - or a font you name actually resolve to. Use for 'what fonts do I have', 'is Fira Code installed', 'which font is used for monospace'. Read-only. (arguments: query)

backup_adapters: A small uniform view of local backup tools. list: which of restic, borg and rsync are installed; check: read a repository's own history (read-only); plan: print the exact backup command for a repository and paths, after asking. plan never runs the command. (arguments: action, backend, repository, paths, name)

negatives.desc: watch: Your MoYoung/Da Fit smartwatch: 'summary' (steps, distance, calories for 3 days, last night's sleep stages, today's stress, workouts), 'measure' a heart rate, blood oxygen or blood pressure on the wrist (takes up to a minute), read 'settings', 'set' one (step_goal, time_format 12h/24h, units metric/imperial, raise_to_wake, sedentary_reminder, other_app_notifications, power_saving, heart_rate_auto_interval, do_not_disturb '22:00-07:00'), 'sync_time', 'find' (make the watch ring), 'notify' (show a message on the watch), or set the 'profile' (height, weight, age, gender - weight is never measured by the watch). Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, device, what, setting, value, sender, text, kind, height_cm, weight_kg, age, gender)

(arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)

landline_call: Place and answer calls on the JioFiber broadband landline over Wi-Fi, through the router - the same line the JioJoin app uses, the house's own landline number. 'status' says whether the line is connected and what call is on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+911234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' picks up a ringing call; 'hangup' ends, cancels or declines the current call. (arguments: action, number, name)

Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

Times in words: 'tomorrow 3pm', 'friday 5 pm', '2026-10-09 14:00'. Move and cancel ask the person to confirm. Ambiguous matches are refused with the candidates. Requires the 'calendar-write-enabled' consent key (move/cancel also 'calendar-read-enabled'). No invitations are sent. (arguments: action, title, start, duration, end, new_start, location, notes)

calendar_events: List events on the user's calendars (GNOME calendars and online accounts): today, tomorrow, this week, or the next few hours. Requires the 'calendar-read-enabled' consent key. (arguments: range, hours)

phone: The user's paired phone via GSConnect/KDE Connect: status (reachable, battery), ring it to find it, ping it, share a file or link to it; read text messages ('messages': latest, from a contact, or unread only); send a text message ('send': to a contact name or number, or omit contact to reply to the latest conversation) with exactly the text given - draft it first; or 'call' a contact or number (opens the phone's dialer). train.say: Can this machine roll back, and which slot is it on.
train.positives_desc: snapshot_status: Whether this Shanios machine can roll back: the OS version, which blue/green slot was booted, which slot boots next, the previous slot a rollback would return to, any recorded boot failure or pending reboot, and the btrfs snapshots on disk. Use for 'can I undo the update', 'which slot am I on', 'is an update waiting'. The snapshot list uses the 'snapshots-sense-enabled' switch. Read-only.

negatives.desc: random_pick: Flip a coin, roll dice ('2d6'), pick a random number in a range, or choose one of a list of options. (arguments: kind, dice, low, high, options)

backup_status: Whether this machine's files are actually backed up off it: how many restic snapshots exist, when the most recent was taken, what it covered, and whether the repository still passes restic's own integrity check. Use for 'is my backup working', 'when did I last back up', 'do I have a copy of my files'. A machine with no repository configured says so plainly, because that means there is no backup. Read-only: it never writes to the repository. (arguments: repository)

process_cost: What each running program is COSTING this machine right now, measured over the last second rather than as a snapshot: percent CPU split into user and system time, how much memory it holds, page faults (including the major ones that mean it is thrashing), and how many kB a second it is reading and writing. Answers 'what is using my CPU', 'what is making my computer slow', 'what is writing to my disk all the time', 'which program is swapping', 'why did everything freeze'. Use this when the machine feels slow; use list_processes to see what is running and disk_activity to see whether the disk itself is busy. Read-only; nothing is started, stopped or changed.

machine_capabilities: Report what this machine can actually do: which of the commands Chronoa knows how to use are really present, which Python modules import here, and which services are enabled. Asks the live machine rather than reading the shipped inventory, which describes the image it was built from and not necessarily this one. Use it before offering to convert a file, edit an image, read a document or capture audio, to find out whether that is even possible here.
