photo_metadata: Read a photo's embedded EXIF metadata: the camera and lens, the date and time it was taken, exposure, aperture, ISO, focal length, and the GPS location if one is recorded. Use for 'when was this photo taken', 'does this picture contain my location', 'which camera took it'. JPEG and TIFF. Read-only; the file is not changed. (arguments: path)

photos: Find the user's photos by what is in them or written on them, or when they were taken. search: query like 'receipt hardware shop', 'dog on the beach', 'december 2025'; index: update the index of the Pictures folder (a batch at a time); status: how much is indexed. (arguments: action, query, captions)

capture_video: Record a short video from the camera (webcam), e.g. '/dev/video0', for a few seconds. Requires the vision/camera consent. Writes a new .mp4; no camera means a clear refusal. (arguments: device, seconds, infrared)

edit_video: Edit a video and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, resize to a width, rotate, mute or keep only the audio, or change the speed. End times accept seconds ('95'), or 'MM:SS' / 'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, width, rotate, mute, audio_only, speed, output)

read_video: Read a video's basics out loud (for subtitles or what was said use recording): how long it is, its resolution, its video codec, whether it has audio, and its bitrate. Add keyframes=true to also save the moments the image changes. The original is never modified. (arguments: path, keyframes)

train.say: search the web for the latest news about ISRO
train.positives_desc: web_search: Look something up on the web and return what the pages actually say: facts, prices, how-tos, anything no more specific tool covers. Give a search query, a specific URL, or both. For a scholarly question - a paper, a preprint, prior work, 'what does the research say' - set source=arxiv and it searches the arXiv preprint archive instead of the web. For news headlines use news; to click, fill in or book something on a site use browse. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: query, url, source)

negatives.desc: news: News headlines only (title, source, age), from Google News (or BBC) RSS feeds - not facts or what a page says, which is web_search. With no topic: the top stories. A topic can be a section - world, business, tech, science, health, sports, entertainment - or anything to search for, e.g. 'ISRO'. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: topic, source, limit)

search_my_files: Search your own files by their contents - documents, notes, code - either in a directory you choose with Chronoa's own index, or through the desktop's index (LocalSearch on GNOME, Baloo on Plasma). 'search' (default): what matches a few words. 'desktop': ask the desktop's index instead, needing 'document-search-enabled'. 'reindex': read the directory and build or refresh Chronoa's index (needed before the first search). 'status': what would be indexed and whether this machine can search by meaning. Needs the 'file-index-enabled' consent key for its own index. (arguments: action, query, kind, path, limit)

search_file_contents: Search inside text files under a directory for a literal string, and report which files contain it and on which lines. Skips binary files and very large files, and says how many it skipped. (arguments: text, path, file_pattern, case_sensitive, max_matches)

conversations: The user's saved Chronoa conversations. list: recent ones; search: find what was said in earlier conversations (query); open: continue one (which = title or id); new: start a fresh one; rename (which, title); copy: duplicate one to try another way, optionally keeping only its first keep_turns user messages; export: save one as Markdown (path); delete: remove one permanently (needs 'file-delete-enabled'). (arguments: action, which, query, title, path, keep_turns)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

phone: The user's paired phone via GSConnect/KDE Connect: status (reachable, battery), ring it to find it, ping it, share a file or link to it; read text messages ('messages': latest, from a contact, or unread only); send a text message ('send': to a contact name or number, or omit contact to reply to the latest conversation) with exactly the text given - draft it first; or 'call' a contact or number (opens the phone's dialer). The user confirms every message and call before it goes. Requires the 'phone-control-enabled' consent key; reading needs 'phone-messages-read-enabled', sending and calling 'phone-messages-send-enabled'. (arguments: action, device, target, contact, text, unread_only, limit)

calendar_edit: Change the user's calendar: 'create' adds an event to the default calendar (title, start, optional duration or end, location); 'move' reschedules an event found by its current time and/or title to new_start; 'cancel' deletes one. Times in words: 'tomorrow 3pm', 'friday 5 pm', '2026-10-09 14:00'. Move and cancel ask the person to confirm. Ambiguous matches are refused with the candidates. Requires the 'calendar-write-enabled' consent key (move/cancel also 'calendar-read-enabled'). No invitations are sent. (arguments: action, title, start, duration, end, new_start, location, notes)

train.positives_desc: convert_color: Convert a colour between hex (#ff8800), rgb(255, 136, 0), hsl and its CSS name. (arguments: color)

negatives.desc: ir_remote: Send and receive infrared remote-control codes, and build or read the pulse-space timings themselves. 'devices': is there IR hardware here (most machines have none, and that is a true answer). 'encode': turn an address and command into the NEC or RC-6 timings that would carry them. 'decode': turn timings into a code. 'send': transmit a code through an IR device. 'receive': capture a button press and decode it. Needs the 'ir-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, protocol, address, command, timings, seconds)

create_video: Create a video: a slideshow from a list of pictures (each shown for a few seconds), or a simple clip of a colour for a duration. Writes a new .mp4 next to the inputs; never overwrites. (arguments: images, seconds, color, duration, width)

read_image: Read a picture's basics out loud: width by height, format, and colour type, plus file size. For what the picture says, use read_document on it. The original is never modified. (arguments: path)

train.say: Read a video's length, size, and format.
train.positives_desc: read_video: Read a video's basics out loud (for subtitles or what was said use recording): how long it is, its resolution, its video codec, whether it has audio, and its bitrate. Add keyframes=true to also save the moments the image changes. The original is never modified. (arguments: path, keyframes)

negatives.desc: convert_media: Convert an audio, video or image file to another format (mp3, ogg, opus, wav, flac, m4a, mp4, webm, gif, png, jpg, webp), optionally resizing to a width. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to, width)

photo_video: Blur or pixelate faces, blur or remove the background, or find people and objects in a photo or video. Works by what is in it, on this computer. identify: find faces and everyday objects (people, cars, dogs, cups...); effect: blur_faces, pixelate_faces, blur_background or remove_background, saved as a new file (videos keep their sound); keyframes: save the moments a video changes; describe: say what happens in a video. For a look like sepia or sketch, or resizing and converting, use edit_image or convert_media. (arguments: action, path, effect, subject, labelled_copy)

media_control: Control music and video players: play, pause, toggle, next track, previous track, stop, restart (current track from the beginning), seek (skip ahead or go back by 'seconds'; negative goes back), or 'status' to say what is playing. (arguments: action, seconds)

create_video: Create a video: a slideshow from a list of pictures (each shown for a few seconds), or a simple clip of a colour for a duration. Writes a new .mp4 next to the inputs; never overwrites. (arguments: images, seconds, color, duration, width)

edit_image: Edit a picture (for faces or backgrounds use photo_video) and save the result as a new file next to it: resize (width and/or height, or percent), compress (quality, or to under a size in KB), crop, upscale (2-4x), rotate, flip, grayscale, a look (sepia, vignette, sketch, paint, enhance), strip metadata (location/camera), or convert format. Several edits can be combined in one call. For effects that depend on what is in the picture (blur faces, blur the background) use photo_video. (arguments: path, width, height, percent, upscale, quality, max_kb, crop, rotate, flip, grayscale, look, strip_metadata, format)
convert_document: Convert a document between markdown, plain text, and HTML. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to)

desktop_setting: Read or change one desktop setting from a fixed list: animations (window and menu animations); cursor_size (mouse pointer size in pixels (24 is normal; 32, 48, 64 are larger)); single_click (open files and folders with a single click); clock_24h (show the top-bar clock in 24-hour format); clock_seconds (show seconds in the top-bar clock); battery_percentage (show the battery percentage in the top bar); hot_corner (open the overview when the pointer hits the top-left corner); natural_scroll (touchpad natural (reverse) scrolling); tap_to_click (tap the touchpad to click). Changing requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: setting, value)

train.positives_desc: create_archive: Create a zip or tar.gz archive from files or folders, or list or safely extract an existing one. Refuses archives whose entries would escape the destination. (arguments: action, source, destination, format)

negatives.desc: extract_archive: Unpack a .tar/.tar.gz/.tgz/.zip archive, or any format 7z reads (.7z, .rar, .cab ...), into a directory. Every member is checked first and the archive is refused whole if any entry would be written outside the destination or is a link, a device or a FIFO. Will not overwrite existing files unless asked. (arguments: archive, destination, overwrite)

list_archive: List what is inside an archive - .tar, .tar.gz, .zip, .7z, .rar or .cab - without extracting anything. Use for 'what's in this archive', 'does this tarball contain what I need'. Names any member that extraction would refuse because it points outside the destination, which is how a malicious archive is recognised before it is opened. Reads only; writes nothing. (arguments: path)

pdf_pages: Work with PDF pages without re-rendering them: 'info' (page count), 'merge' several PDFs into one (paths, in order), 'split' a PDF into one file per page (into a folder), or 'extract' some pages (e.g. '1-3,7') into a new PDF. Always writes new files; never overwrites an existing one or changes the originals. No rotation. (arguments: action, path, paths, pages, output)

backup_adapters: A small uniform view of local backup tools. list: which of restic, borg and rsync are installed; check: read a repository's own history (read-only); plan: print the exact backup command for a repository and paths, after asking. plan never runs the command. (arguments: action, backend, repository, paths, name)

web_search: Look something up on the web and return what the pages actually say: facts, prices, how-tos, anything no more specific tool covers. Give a search query, a specific URL, or both. For a scholarly question - a paper, a preprint, prior work, 'what does the research say' - set source=arxiv and it searches the arXiv preprint archive instead of the web. For news headlines use news; to click, fill in or book something on a site use browse. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: query, url, source)

train.positives_desc: search_file_contents: Search inside text files under a directory for a literal string, and report which files contain it and on which lines. Skips binary files and very large files, and says how many it skipped. (arguments: text, path, file_pattern, case_sensitive, max_matches)

negatives.desc: search_my_files: Search your own files by their contents - documents, notes, code - either in a directory you choose with Chronoa's own index, or through the desktop's index (LocalSearch on GNOME, Baloo on Plasma). 'search' (default): what matches a few words. 'desktop': ask the desktop's index instead, needing 'document-search-enabled'. 'reindex': read the directory and build or refresh Chronoa's index (needed before the first search). 'status': what would be indexed and whether this machine can search by meaning. Needs the 'file-index-enabled' consent key for its own index. (arguments: action, query, kind, path, limit)

find_files: Find files and folders by name under a directory, using a wildcard pattern such as '*.log' or 'report*'. Matches on the name only and never opens the files. To see what is in one folder, use list_directory. (arguments: pattern, path, include_hidden, max_results, details)

content_discovery: Enumerate which paths exist on a web server on the local network, using gobuster with a wordlist the person supplies. Use for 'what endpoints does my server expose', 'is /admin public on my site'. Private, loopback and local targets only, behind the network consent. Reports the paths that answered; changes nothing on the server. (arguments: url, wordlist)

cloud_files: See what is in this machine's configured cloud storage remotes - which remotes rclone knows, how many objects and bytes each holds, and what is at the top level of one. Use for 'what is in my cloud drive', 'is anything in the bucket', 'how big is my remote'. Read-only: it never copies, syncs or deletes anything. A machine with no remotes says so, because that means there is nowhere off-machine for anything to go. (arguments: remote, path)

web_search: Look something up on the web and return what the pages actually say: facts, prices, how-tos, anything no more specific tool covers. Give a search query, a specific URL, or both. For a scholarly question - a paper, a preprint, prior work, 'what does the research say' - set source=arxiv and it searches the arXiv preprint archive instead of the web. For news headlines use news; to click, fill in or book something on a site use browse. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: query, url, source)

compare_files: Show what is different between two text files, as a unified diff. Reports 'identical' when they match. Use this to compare two versions of a config, or to see what a change actually did. (arguments: path_a, path_b, context_lines)
read_text_file: Read a text file and return its contents, optionally a range of lines. Use this to see what a file actually says. (arguments: path, start_line, max_lines)

train.say: Read or change a desktop setting (animations, clock, cursor, touchpad...).
train.positives_desc: desktop_setting: Read or change one desktop setting from a fixed list: animations (window and menu animations); cursor_size (mouse pointer size in pixels (24 is normal; 32, 48, 64 are larger)); single_click (open files and folders with a single click); clock_24h (show the top-bar clock in 24-hour format); clock_seconds (show seconds in the top-bar clock); battery_percentage (show the battery percentage in the top bar); hot_corner (open the overview when the pointer hits the top-left corner); natural_scroll (touchpad natural (reverse) scrolling); tap_to_click (tap the touchpad to click). Changing requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: setting, value)

negatives.desc: set_scaling: Report or change the desktop's text scaling factor (1.0 is normal, 1.5 is 150%). Text scaling only - display-resolution and HiDPI scaling are not changed by this, because driving those black-screens sessions. Requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, factor)

set_theme: Report or change whether the desktop uses a light or dark appearance, on GNOME or KDE. Reports the applied theme separately from the preference, because setting the preference does not make every application follow it. Requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)

set_wallpaper: Report or change the GNOME desktop wallpaper, setting the light and dark variants together. Refuses a path that does not exist, rather than leaving a blank desktop with no error. KDE is not supported and will say so. Requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, image)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

ui_elements: Use another app's controls by what they are, through the accessibility tree. apps: which apps are reachable. inspect: list a window's buttons, fields, menus and labels with ids (app = its name; query narrows by text). press: activate an element by id (a button, checkbox, link, menu item). set_text: put text in a field by id. read: an element's text or value. menu: open a menu path like 'File > Export'. drive: one turn of driving - give an action and a control number and the reply is the app's new state in the same short numbered form, which is what a small model can act on. act: click, type or key an app by name or position, with a visible cursor. state: the numbered controls an app is showing. Works on a container's app and on this desktop's own apps alike. Requires 'input-control-enabled'; drive start also runs a container, so it needs 'container-control-enabled' as well. (arguments: action, app, id, text, query, path, do, how, number, image, keys, x, y)

undo_last_change: Put a file or a Chronoa setting back the way Chronoa last found it, by restoring the content or value recorded just before Chronoa's own last change to it. Undoes Chronoa's recent writes only - NOT git history, NOT changes you made in an editor or a shell, and only while a recorded pre-image is still held. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, list, setting, steps)

set_timer: Set a countdown timer that sends a desktop notification when it finishes; list pending timers, say how much time is left, add or take off time, pause, resume, reset to the original length, and cancel. With one timer pending, 'my timer' needs no id. The countdown is owned by systemd, so it fires even if the assistant is closed. It is refused rather than silently accepted when systemd is unavailable, because a timer recorded as pending that will never fire is the same lie as a camera reported as disabled when it is not. (arguments: action, seconds, label, id)

train.positives_desc: set_volume: Set the system output volume to an exact percentage. (arguments: percent, device)

negatives.desc: calculate: Evaluate arithmetic and percentages ('15% of 2400'), or convert between units. Handles the four operations, powers, parentheses, factorial, permutations and combinations (perm/nPr, comb/nCr), gcd, lcm, sqrt, exp, log, ln, trig and inverse trig, and pi/e/tau - exact for whole numbers. For algebra with variables, derivatives, integrals, limits or equations, use solve_math. Converts length, mass, volume, time, data, pressure, frequency, power, energy and temperature, in the units a person actually meets - say '200 km to miles' or '70kg in lb'. Runs entirely on this machine with no network call. Refuses to guess: a percentage needs a number to apply to, and converting between quantities that measure different things is an error rather than a number. (arguments: expression)

get_volume: Get the current volume and mute state of an audio output, or the default one. On a machine with more than one output - several monitors, headphones and a dock - 'the volume' is ambiguous, so pass the device exactly as `wpctl status` prints it to ask about a specific one. (arguments: device)

set_mic_mute: Mute or unmute the default microphone input, or report whether it is currently muted. Output volume is a separate skill. Requires the 'mic-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)

fm_radio: FM and AM broadcast radio. Five actions: 'hardware' for whether this computer can receive anything at all (a laptop usually cannot, and that is a true answer rather than a failure - it needs an RTL2832U USB dongle), 'bands' for the coverage, 'tune' to a frequency, 'decode' to demodulate a recorded IQ capture, and 'scan' to look for carriers in one. A frequency is given in MHz, e.g. 98.6. rtl_fm is narrowband and retunes per channel, so it cannot scan - scanning needs a wideband recording. No station names are guessed: a carrier gives a frequency, and naming it would need a table for your region. Requires the 'fm-radio-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, frequency, seconds, file, centre_mhz, out, deemphasis_us)

phone_remote: Press keys on the paired phone as a Bluetooth keyboard: 'press' the camera 'shutter' (takes a photo in the camera app), play_pause, next, previous, volume_up/down, mute; or 'type' text into whatever field is focused on the phone. The phone must have paired 'Chronoa Remote'. Requires the 'phone-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, key, text)

set_brightness: Get or set screen brightness as a percentage. With no level, reports the current brightness of each panel. With a level, sets it. Writing needs root - the backlight node is root-owned - and a permission failure is reported as such rather than as success. (arguments: level)
set_clipboard: Write text to the system clipboard. (arguments: text)

train.positives_desc: translate_text: Translate text into another language, with the local model when it is running and a web service otherwise. The reply says which was used, because one sends your text to a third party. (arguments: text, to_language, from_language)

negatives.desc: routines: Save a routine: a short phrase (e.g. 'good morning', 'leaving work') that later runs a whole request, e.g. 'tell me the weather, my calendar today and the top news'. Also list or delete routines. Saving runs nothing; saying the phrase later runs the request. (arguments: action, name, request, phrases)

review_proposals: Facts Chronoa noticed in a finished conversation and has NOT saved, listed for the user to keep or discard. Nothing here is remembered until it is kept, and a discarded fact is never offered again. Use this when the user asks what Chronoa thinks it learned, or asks to remember or forget something it noticed last night. (arguments: action, session_id, number)

train.say: Save a phrase that runs a whole request.
train.positives_desc: routines: Save a routine: a short phrase (e.g. 'good morning', 'leaving work') that later runs a whole request, e.g. 'tell me the weather, my calendar today and the top news'. Also list or delete routines. Saving runs nothing; saying the phrase later runs the request. (arguments: action, name, request, phrases)

negatives.desc: git_commit: Commit the files you name in a git repository, with a message. Only the paths given are staged - nothing is swept up from the rest of the tree. Requires the 'git-write-enabled' consent key. Pushing is a separate skill: that publishes. (arguments: files, message, path)

run_command: Run one program in the project folder and get its exit code and output - the project's tests (pytest, npm test, cargo test), its build or linter - to check that a change works. One program per call: no pipes, redirections or shell syntax. Requires the 'run-command-enabled' consent key; asks each time. (arguments: command, cwd, timeout_seconds, where, image, machine, network)

recording: Make subtitles or a transcript of a video or audio file, tell speakers apart, or remove background noise. Works on the sound, on this computer. text: what was said; subtitles: save an .srt beside it; speakers: who said what, turn by turn; clean: a copy with background noise removed; sounds: what can be heard in it (music, a dog, traffic...); listen: what can be heard around the computer right now (the microphone, a few seconds); streams: which applications are carrying audio right now, and the name to capture one by (a call in a browser is one); capture: record one of those for 5-600 seconds and transcribe it - which records the room, so it needs the sound consent like the microphone does. (arguments: action, path, range, language, people, seconds)

calculate: Evaluate arithmetic and percentages ('15% of 2400'), or convert between units. Handles the four operations, powers, parentheses, factorial, permutations and combinations (perm/nPr, comb/nCr), gcd, lcm, sqrt, exp, log, ln, trig and inverse trig, and pi/e/tau - exact for whole numbers. For algebra with variables, derivatives, integrals, limits or equations, use solve_math. Converts length, mass, volume, time, data, pressure, frequency, power, energy and temperature, in the units a person actually meets - say '200 km to miles' or '70kg in lb'. Runs entirely on this machine with no network call. Refuses to guess: a percentage needs a number to apply to, and converting between quantities that measure different things is an error rather than a number. (arguments: expression)

analyze_table: Ask questions of a .csv, .tsv, .xlsx or .json (list of records) file with read-only SQLite SQL. describe: the tables, columns, types, row counts and a sample - do this first. query: run one SELECT (the table is `data`, or one table per sheet name for a workbook); save_as='~/x.csv' or .xlsx keeps the full result. chart: bar, line or pie chart saved as .svg from a SELECT returning (label, value) columns. (arguments: action, path, sql, save_as, kind, title, output)
kill_process: Stop a running process by pid, asking it to exit cleanly. Use list_processes to find the pid first. Requires the 'process-kill-enabled' consent key. (arguments: pid, signal_name)

manage_goals: Save a multi-step goal as a plan of tool steps that can be run later from the Goals panel, list saved goals, answer one that is waiting for you, or remove one. Saving runs nothing. Each step names a tool, its arguments, and a name for its result; a later step can use an earlier result as $name in a string argument, and lists the names it depends_on. A depends_on name that no earlier step produces is a question for the user: the goal waits there until they answer it. Requires the 'goals-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, goal, steps, id, answer)

train.positives_desc: bluetooth_devices: List paired Bluetooth devices (and which are connected), or connect / disconnect one by its name, e.g. 'connect my headphones'. (arguments: action, name)

negatives.desc: toggle_bluetooth: Turn the Bluetooth adapter on or off, or report its state and the paired devices. Requires the 'bluetooth-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)

usb_devices: What is plugged into this machine's USB ports (mice, phones, webcams, sticks, with their speed), and every Thunderbolt/USB4 device with whether it is authorised to work. Use for 'what's plugged in', 'why doesn't my dock work', 'is my webcam connected'. The USB list uses the 'usb-sense-enabled' switch. Read-only.

bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)

bluetooth_gatt: Read what a paired Bluetooth Low Energy device says about itself - a watch's or headset's battery, a heart-rate strap's live reading, which services a band offers. 'list': every paired device and whether it speaks this protocol. 'services': what one exposes. 'read': one stored value. 'listen': a live reading of something the device only pushes, e.g. heart rate - 'nothing arrived' is the truthful answer when the device is not measuring. Speakers, headphones and car stereios are older Bluetooth and expose nothing here, which is a true answer, not a failure; wearables, bands, straps, smart tags and thermometers answer. Needs 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' and the device must be connected. (arguments: action, device, seconds, characteristic)

android_device: An Android phone connected with USB debugging (adb). devices: which are connected; info: model, Android version, battery, storage; screenshot: save the phone's screen as a PNG; apps: installed apps (query filters); push: copy a file to the phone (to, default /sdcard/Download); pull: copy a file from the phone; open_url: open a web link on the phone. Requires 'phone-control-enabled'. (arguments: action, serial, path, to, url, query, output)

ir_remote: Send and receive infrared remote-control codes, and build or read the pulse-space timings themselves. 'devices': is there IR hardware here (most machines have none, and that is a true answer). 'encode': turn an address and command into the NEC or RC-6 timings that would carry them. 'decode': turn timings into a code. 'send': transmit a code through an IR device. 'receive': capture a button press and decode it. Needs the 'ir-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, protocol, address, command, timings, seconds)

lan_phone: Find phones on the SAME Wi-Fi network, using the KDE Connect protocol directly - so it works without KDE Connect or GSConnect installed. 'devices': what announced itself on this network in the last few seconds (phones, tablets, other computers). 'announce': make this computer findable by a phone's KDE Connect app. 'status': what this computer can and cannot do on the LAN. 'pair': pair with the device 'devices' found (the phone asks its owner). Needs the 'lan-phone-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, seconds)

train.positives_desc: lookup_wikipedia: Who or what something is - a person, place, thing or event - from Wikipedia's summary. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off. (arguments: topic)
set_mute: Mute or unmute the sound from the speakers or headphones ('mute the sound', 'unmute'). The microphone is set_mic_mute. (arguments: mute, device)

negatives.desc: set_mic_mute: Mute or unmute the default microphone input, or report whether it is currently muted. Output volume is a separate skill. Requires the 'mic-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)

get_volume: Get the current volume and mute state of an audio output, or the default one. On a machine with more than one output - several monitors, headphones and a dock - 'the volume' is ambiguous, so pass the device exactly as `wpctl status` prints it to ask about a specific one. (arguments: device)

edit_audio: Edit a sound file and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, raise or lower the volume, normalize loudness, change speed, or convert to an audio format. End times accept seconds or 'MM:SS'/'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, volume, normalize, speed, to)

audio_output: List the speakers/headphones (outputs) and microphones (inputs) and which one is the default, or switch the default output or input - 'play through my headphones', 'use the USB microphone', 'send sound to the HDMI monitor'. Pick a device by its number or part of its name. (arguments: action, device, kind)

speaker_id: Opt-in voice identity using the local speaker model. enrol: remember a person's voice from a 16 kHz mono WAV, with their name and the basis on which they agreed; identify: say which enrolled voice a WAV sounds like; list: names already enrolled; forget: remove one. Needs the hearing consent and an explicit yes for enrol and forget. Nothing about the voice leaves this machine. (arguments: action, name, clip, basis)

recording: Make subtitles or a transcript of a video or audio file, tell speakers apart, or remove background noise. Works on the sound, on this computer. text: what was said; subtitles: save an .srt beside it; speakers: who said what, turn by turn; clean: a copy with background noise removed; sounds: what can be heard in it (music, a dog, traffic...); listen: what can be heard around the computer right now (the microphone, a few seconds); streams: which applications are carrying audio right now, and the name to capture one by (a call in a browser is one); capture: record one of those for 5-600 seconds and transcribe it - which records the room, so it needs the sound consent like the microphone does. (arguments: action, path, range, language, people, seconds)

set_privacy: Control the machine's privacy: mute or unmute the microphone, enable or disable a camera, or blank the screen. Muting the microphone is a user-level stream mute that any new application can override, and the reply says so rather than implying the hardware is off. Disabling a camera needs root and is only possible on drivers that expose a disable control, so a device with no such control is reported as unsupported rather than disabled. Blanking works on X11; under Wayland it would need a permission prompt, so the idle timeout is offered instead. Every action says how to undo it. (arguments: action, device)

train.positives_desc: connect_wifi: Join a WiFi network by name, or leave the current one. Open networks only - this never handles a password, because a password passed through a chat or an MCP client is in a transcript. Requires the 'wifi-connect-enabled' consent key. (arguments: ssid)

negatives.desc: list_wifi_networks: Scan for and list the WiFi networks in range, with signal strength and whether this machine is joined to one. Scans the radio, so it requires the 'network-sense-enabled' consent. (arguments: rescan)

toggle_wifi: Turn the Wi-Fi radio on or off (only Wi-Fi - airplane_mode switches every radio, connect_wifi joins a network), or report whether Wi-Fi is on. Changing requires the 'radio-control-enabled' consent key; status needs no permission. (arguments: action)

solve_math: Maths: derivative, series (Taylor), expansion, factor, numeric integral (definite, or numeric for indefinite), numeric limit (at a point or oo), linear and quadratic solve, numeric sum of a series, evaluation to N digits, prime_factors / is_prime. Write maths plainly: 'x^2 + 3x', 'sin(x)/x', 'x^2 - 4 = 0'. (arguments: operation, expression, variable, point, lower, upper, order, digits, other)
vpn_control: List saved VPN connections and which is active, or connect / disconnect one by name. Connecting needs the 'wifi-connect-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name)

lan_phone: Find phones on the SAME Wi-Fi network, using the KDE Connect protocol directly - so it works without KDE Connect or GSConnect installed. open_settings: Open the system Settings app at a specific page, e.g. 'wifi', 'bluetooth', 'display', 'sound', 'power', 'privacy', 'keyboard', 'mouse', 'touchpad', 'printers', 'users', 'about', 'date_time', 'region', 'notifications', 'background', 'accessibility'. GNOME and KDE Plasma. Use open_application for Settings without a page. (arguments: page)

qr_code: read: decode every QR code and barcode in a picture (path) or on the screen (screen=true, needs the vision consent). create: make a QR code PNG of text (a URL, Wi-Fi details, a note) at output. (arguments: action, path, screen, text, output)

train.positives_desc: open_file: Open one specific file or folder (by its path) using the desktop's default application for it - the same thing double-clicking it would do. To launch an app such as the file manager, use open_application. (arguments: path)

negatives.desc: open_application: Open or launch an installed application by name or by kind, e.g. 'firefox', 'files', 'settings', 'music player', 'text editor'. Not for websites: use browse to open a site and work on it. (arguments: name)

GNOME and KDE Plasma. Use open_application for Settings without a page. (arguments: page)

identify_file: Identify a file by reading its first bytes rather than trusting its name. Use for 'why won't this open', 'what is this file', 'is this really a PNG', 'this file has no extension'. Reports the detected format and whether the filename agrees with it, which is the usual cause of a file refusing to open in the program its name implies. Says plainly when a signature is unrecognised. Read-only. (arguments: path)

Requires 'phone-control-enabled'. (arguments: action, serial, path, to, url, query, output)

conversations: The user's saved Chronoa conversations. list: recent ones; search: find what was said in earlier conversations (query); open: continue one (which = title or id); new: start a fresh one; rename (which, title); copy: duplicate one to try another way, optionally keeping only its first keep_turns user messages; export: save one as Markdown (path); delete: remove one permanently (needs 'file-delete-enabled'). (arguments: action, which, query, title, path, keep_turns)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

maps: OpenStreetMap maps: find where a place is ('find'), driving/walking/cycling directions ('directions') or just distance and time ('travel_time') between places, the nearest kind of place such as petrol pump, hotel, ATM or hospital ('nearby'), or open a place or route on the map in the browser ('open'). Times are typical, without live traffic. With no origin, 'here' is this computer's location. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off; 'here' also needs the location sense. (arguments: action, place, destination, origin, mode, what, near, limit)

train.positives_desc: list_services: List system services with their load and active state, optionally filtered by name, newest state first for anything running. Reports UNKNOWN on a machine that is not systemd-managed. (arguments: name_filter, failed_only)

negatives.desc: system_info: Describe the machine Chronoa is running on: distribution, kernel, architecture, uptime, load, memory, CPU count, whether this is a desktop session or a container, and the hardware identity (make, model, board, BIOS version).

'list': every paired device and whether it speaks this protocol. 'services': what one exposes. 'read': one stored value. 'listen': a live reading of something the device only pushes, e.g. heart rate - 'nothing arrived' is the truthful answer when the device is not measuring. Speakers, headphones and car stereios are older Bluetooth and expose nothing here, which is a true answer, not a failure; wearables, bands, straps, smart tags and thermometers answer. machine_capabilities: Report what this machine can actually do: which of the commands Chronoa knows how to use are really present, which Python modules import here, and which services are enabled. Asks the live machine rather than reading the shipped inventory, which describes the image it was built from and not necessarily this one. Use it before offering to convert a file, edit an image, read a document or capture audio, to find out whether that is even possible here.
check_updates: Check whether this machine has package updates waiting, without installing anything and without needing root. Works on Arch and other pacman systems.
get_clipboard: Read the current contents of the system clipboard.
set_clipboard: Write text to the system clipboard. (arguments: text)

control_service: Start, stop, restart, reload, enable or disable a system service, then read its state back so the reply says whether it actually came up. Requires the 'service-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: unit, action)

train.positives_desc: toggle_night_light: Report or turn on/off the blue-light filter (GNOME night light), reporting the schedule separately from the on/off state, because a filter that is enabled with its schedule off is not currently doing anything. KDE is not supported and will say so. Requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)

negatives.desc: set_theme: Report or change whether the desktop uses a light or dark appearance, on GNOME or KDE. Reports the applied theme separately from the preference, because setting the preference does not make every application follow it. Requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)

Nothing here is remembered until it is kept, and a discarded fact is never offered again. Use this when the user asks what Chronoa thinks it learned, or asks to remember or forget something it noticed last night. (arguments: action, session_id, number)

watch: Your MoYoung/Da Fit smartwatch: 'summary' (steps, distance, calories for 3 days, last night's sleep stages, today's stress, workouts), 'measure' a heart rate, blood oxygen or blood pressure on the wrist (takes up to a minute), read 'settings', 'set' one (step_goal, time_format 12h/24h, units metric/imperial, raise_to_wake, sedentary_reminder, other_app_notifications, power_saving, heart_rate_auto_interval, do_not_disturb '22:00-07:00'), 'sync_time', 'find' (make the watch ring), 'notify' (show a message on the watch), or set the 'profile' (height, weight, age, gender - weight is never measured by the watch). edit_image: Edit a picture (for faces or backgrounds use photo_video) and save the result as a new file next to it: resize (width and/or height, or percent), compress (quality, or to under a size in KB), crop, upscale (2-4x), rotate, flip, grayscale, a look (sepia, vignette, sketch, paint, enhance), strip metadata (location/camera), or convert format. (arguments: path, width, height, percent, upscale, quality, max_kb, crop, rotate, flip, grayscale, look, strip_metadata, format)

set_wallpaper: Report or change the GNOME desktop wallpaper, setting the light and dark variants together. Refuses a path that does not exist, rather than leaving a blank desktop with no error. KDE is not supported and will say so. Requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, image)

(arguments: action, date, datetime, latitude, longitude, planet, sign, year, month, day, hour)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, device, what, setting, value, sender, text, kind, height_cm, weight_kg, age, gender)

chart: Make an SVG file from data, drawn on this computer with no install. chart: kind=bar|line|pie with data (bar/pie: [[label, number], ...]; line: [[x, y], ...], or several lines as series {name: [[x, y], ...]}), plus title, x_label, y_label. icon: a stroke icon by name (arrow-right, bell, calendar, check, clock, close, download, folder, heart, home, mail, search, settings, star, user). diagram: a top-to-bottom flow, steps=["Read", "Edit", "Test"] with optional arrows [[from, to, label], ...]. output is the .svg path, e.g. '~/Pictures/sales.svg'. (arguments: action, output, kind, data, series, steps, arrows, name, title, x_label, y_label)

desktop_setting: Read or change one desktop setting from a fixed list: animations (window and menu animations); cursor_size (mouse pointer size in pixels (24 is normal; 32, 48, 64 are larger)); single_click (open files and folders with a single click); clock_24h (show the top-bar clock in 24-hour format); clock_seconds (show seconds in the top-bar clock); battery_percentage (show the battery percentage in the top bar); hot_corner (open the overview when the pointer hits the top-left corner); natural_scroll (touchpad natural (reverse) scrolling); tap_to_click (tap the touchpad to click). Changing requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: setting, value)

Disabling a camera needs root and is only possible on drivers that expose a disable control, so a device with no such control is reported as unsupported rather than disabled. Blanking works on X11; under Wayland it would need a permission prompt, so the idle timeout is offered instead. Every action says how to undo it. (arguments: action, device)

negatives.desc: set_mic_mute: Mute or unmute the default microphone input, or report whether it is currently muted. Output volume is a separate skill. Requires the 'mic-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)
set_mute: Mute or unmute the sound from the speakers or headphones ('mute the sound', 'unmute'). The microphone is set_mic_mute. (arguments: mute, device)

phone_remote: Press keys on the paired phone as a Bluetooth keyboard: 'press' the camera 'shutter' (takes a photo in the camera app), play_pause, next, previous, volume_up/down, mute; or 'type' text into whatever field is focused on the phone. The phone must have paired 'Chronoa Remote'. Requires the 'phone-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, key, text)

lock_screen: Lock this session so a password is needed to come back to it. Uses the session's own mechanism so the same thing happens as the desktop's Lock button. Requires the 'screen-lock-enabled' consent key.

screen_to_phone: Show this computer's screen on a paired phone, over the Bluetooth network. 'status': could this be shared here at all, and what is missing if not. 'start': ask the desktop to share the screen and serve it to the phone - the desktop shows its own 'Share screen' dialog, which only the person can answer. 'stop': end it and close the portal session. The picture goes over Bluetooth, so it is not on Wi-Fi, but it is the whole screen - which is why this needs the 'screen-share-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

set_screensaver: Report or change how long the machine waits before the screen blanks, and whether it then demands a password. The two are reported separately, because blanking without locking leaves anyone who walks up to the machine able to use it. Requires the 'idle-timeout-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, blank_after_minutes, lock)

scan_document: Scan a page and return its text (OCR), keeping the image in ~/Documents/Scans. source: 'scanner' (default; list_only lists them), 'camera' (hold the page up to the webcam; it is found and straightened), or 'photo' (straighten and read a picture of a page at path). 'Scan this letter and read it to me.' (arguments: source, path, list_only, device)

train.say: What changed in a git repository.
train.positives_desc: git_inspect: Report a git working tree: what has changed and is not committed, the diff of those changes, recent commits, or the current branch and how far it is from its upstream; also the stashed work and the reflog (the record that survives rebases and amends). Reports UNKNOWN - never 'clean tree' - when git is missing, the folder is not a repository, or git fails. Requires the 'git-sense-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, subcommand, revision, since, context_lines)

negatives.desc: git_push: Push a branch to a named remote. Requires the 'git-push-enabled' consent key, and asks before every push. The remote must be one the repository already has, and must be named - there is no default and no 'push everything'. Force-pushing is refused. (arguments: remote, branch, set_upstream, path)

git_commit: Commit the files you name in a git repository, with a message. Only the paths given are staged - nothing is swept up from the rest of the tree. Requires the 'git-write-enabled' consent key. Pushing is a separate skill: that publishes. (arguments: files, message, path)
git_branch: Create a branch in a git repository and switch to it, or switch to a branch that already exists. Requires the 'git-write-enabled' consent key. (arguments: name, path)

resolve_conflict: Work out what is conflicting in a git repository and resolve it. 'show' lists every unmerged file and prints all three sides git holds - the common ancestor, your side and theirs - so there is no guessing about which is which; 'ours' and 'theirs' take a whole side of the named files and mark them resolved; 'mark' marks files you have edited by hand; 'abort' abandons the merge, rebase or cherry-pick and leaves the commits to try again. There is no automatic merge, because deciding which line is right is a judgement about the code and only you can make it. Reading needs 'git-sense-enabled'; changing the working tree needs 'git-write-enabled'. (arguments: action, path, paths)

vcs_status: What state a checkout is in, for git, subversion or mercurial: which version control system it belongs to, the branch or revision, the repository it points at, and what has changed. Use when the answer might not be git - 'what is this folder's state', 'which repository is this', 'what changed in my checkout'. Read-only; runs nothing that modifies a repository. (arguments: path)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Use 'setpoints' to list built-in off-by-default proposals, 'describe-setpoint' to explain one, and 'arm-setpoint' to arm one whose own switch is already on; arming never switches one on. Listing and describing need no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds, setpoint)

undo_last_change: Put a file or a Chronoa setting back the way Chronoa last found it, by restoring the content or value recorded just before Chronoa's own last change to it. Undoes Chronoa's recent writes only - NOT git history, NOT changes you made in an editor or a shell, and only while a recorded pre-image is still held. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, list, setting, steps)

train.positives_desc: stopwatch: A stopwatch: start, lap, read the time so far, or stop. (arguments: action)
my_ip_address: This computer's IP addresses: local (LAN) addresses per network interface, and the public internet address when the web sense is on.

negatives.desc: content_discovery: Enumerate which paths exist on a web server on the local network, using gobuster with a wordlist the person supplies. Use for 'what endpoints does my server expose', 'is /admin public on my site'. Private, loopback and local targets only, behind the network consent. Reports the paths that answered; changes nothing on the server. (arguments: url, wordlist)

download_file: Download a file from a web address and save it to disk, reporting the size and how long it took. Use for 'download that file', 'get this installer', 'save that page'. Only http and https; a site that answers with an error page reports that rather than saving the error as if it were the file. (arguments: url, destination, engine)

ir_remote: Send and receive infrared remote-control codes, and build or read the pulse-space timings themselves. 'devices': is there IR hardware here (most machines have none, and that is a true answer). 'encode': turn an address and command into the NEC or RC-6 timings that would carry them. 'decode': turn timings into a code. 'send': transmit a code through an IR device. 'receive': capture a button press and decode it. Needs the 'ir-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, protocol, address, command, timings, seconds)

login_history: Recent logins to this machine: which user, from which terminal or remote address, when they started and how long they lasted, and recent reboots. Use for 'who logged in', 'has anyone used my computer'. Requires the 'sessions-sense-enabled' consent key, because it reports other people's presence. Read-only. (arguments: limit)

train.positives_desc: speak: Speak text aloud using the local text-to-speech engine. Reuses the app's own Piper/RHVoice/espeak-ng fallback chain and its own audio playback path. The engine actually used is named in the result. (arguments: text)

negatives.desc: browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

email_read: Read a locally configured IMAP mailbox: 'list' recent messages (or 'unseen'), or 'get' one by 'uid'. Needs the 'email-read-enabled' consent key. There is no built-in account or cloud credential - the account must be configured locally. (arguments: action, uid, unseen)
read_audio: Read an audio file's basics out loud: how long it is, its codec, sample rate, channels, and bitrate. The original is never modified. (arguments: path)

read_document: Read the text of a PDF (optionally a page range) or of an image (OCR), e.g. to summarise it or read it out. For a PDF it also reports whether the document embeds its fonts, since one that does not prints wrong elsewhere. (arguments: path, first_page, last_page)

read_image: Read a picture's basics out loud: width by height, format, and colour type, plus file size. For what the picture says, use read_document on it. The original is never modified. (arguments: path)

read_logs: Read recent log output from a named system service, or from the kernel when no service is named. Returns the most recent lines first-context-last, and says how much it did not show. (arguments: unit, lines, priority, since)
read_text_file: Read a text file and return its contents, optionally a range of lines. Use this to see what a file actually says. (arguments: path, start_line, max_lines)

read_video: Read a video's basics out loud (for subtitles or what was said use recording): how long it is, its resolution, its video codec, whether it has audio, and its bitrate. Add keyframes=true to also save the moments the image changes. The original is never modified. (arguments: path, keyframes)

train.positives_desc: get_datetime: Current date and time here or in a named place. (arguments: place)

negatives.desc: date_math: Date arithmetic: days until a date ('how many days until 25 December'), the date N days/weeks/months from a date ('what date is 45 days from now'), days between two dates, or the weekday of a date. (arguments: operation, date, other_date, amount, unit)

kundali: Compute Vedic Kundali (birth chart), Panchang (daily almanac), transits, aspects, dignities, BaZi (Chinese Four Pillars), and Nakshatra details. Offline, no API keys, no external dependencies. panchang: Tithi, Vara, Nakshatra, Yoga, Karana. kundali: sidereal birth chart with planets, houses, Navamsha, Dasha, aspects, dignities. transit: transit positions and cross-aspects. aspects: planetary aspects. dignity: planet dignity in a sign. bazi: Chinese Four Pillars. nakshatra: nakshatra details. timelords: profections and firdaria. arabicparts: Arabic parts (lots). temperament: elemental temperament. lunarmansion: lunar mansion. charakarakas: Jaimini karakas. shadbala: planetary strength. combustion: combust planets. horary: horary chart. upagrahas: all upagrahas. arudha: Arudha padas. drishti: Vedic aspects. vishesha: special lagnas. muhurta: electional scoring. vimshopaka: Vimshopaka bala. cheshta: motion states. grahayuddha: planetary wars. upagrahas_full: all upagrahas. fullchart: complete chart JSON. ashtakavarga: Bhinna + Sarva ashtakavarga. gochara: transit analysis. bhava: house analysis. kalamana: time measurement. chinese: Chinese calendar. grahana: eclipse check. shadbala_full: complete shadbala. karakas_full: chara karakas with Rahu reflection. yogas: Vishesha yogas. nodes: lunar nodes. eclipse: eclipse details. charadasha: Chara dasha. yoginidasha: Yogini dasha. ashtottaridasha: Ashtottari dasha. (arguments: action, date, datetime, latitude, longitude, planet, sign, year, month, day, hour)

git_inspect: Report a git working tree: what has changed and is not committed, the diff of those changes, recent commits, or the current branch and how far it is from its upstream; also the stashed work and the reflog (the record that survives rebases and amends). Reports UNKNOWN - never 'clean tree' - when git is missing, the folder is not a repository, or git fails. Requires the 'git-sense-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, subcommand, revision, since, context_lines)

get_weather: Current weather and today's forecast - temperature, feels-like, rain, wind - for a named place, or for where this computer is if no place is given; with `when`, the forecast for tomorrow, a weekday, this week or the weekend instead. Use for weather, temperature outside, rain, forecast. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: place, when)

calendar_events: List events on the user's calendars (GNOME calendars and online accounts): today, tomorrow, this week, or the next few hours. Requires the 'calendar-read-enabled' consent key. (arguments: range, hours)

open_settings: Open the system Settings app at a specific page, e.g. 'wifi', 'bluetooth', 'display', 'sound', 'power', 'privacy', 'keyboard', 'mouse', 'touchpad', 'printers', 'users', 'about', 'date_time', 'region', 'notifications', 'background', 'accessibility'. GNOME and KDE Plasma. Use open_application for Settings without a page. (arguments: page)

photo_metadata: Read a photo's embedded EXIF metadata: the camera and lens, the date and time it was taken, exposure, aperture, ISO, focal length, and the GPS location if one is recorded. Use for 'when was this photo taken', 'does this picture contain my location', 'which camera took it'. JPEG and TIFF. Read-only; the file is not changed. (arguments: path)

train.positives_desc: set_power_profile: Switch the machine between its power profiles - typically power-saver, balanced and performance - and report which one is active now. The profile list is read from the machine rather than assumed, because which profiles exist depends on the CPU driver: switching to one the machine does not have is refused with the valid names listed. Changes the CPU and platform power behaviour, not a per-application setting. (arguments: profile)

negatives.desc: watch: Your MoYoung/Da Fit smartwatch: 'summary' (steps, distance, calories for 3 days, last night's sleep stages, today's stress, workouts), 'measure' a heart rate, blood oxygen or blood pressure on the wrist (takes up to a minute), read 'settings', 'set' one (step_goal, time_format 12h/24h, units metric/imperial, raise_to_wake, sedentary_reminder, other_app_notifications, power_saving, heart_rate_auto_interval, do_not_disturb '22:00-07:00'), 'sync_time', 'find' (make the watch ring), 'notify' (show a message on the watch), or set the 'profile' (height, weight, age, gender - weight is never measured by the watch). Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, device, what, setting, value, sender, text, kind, height_cm, weight_kg, age, gender)

power_action: Suspend (sleep), hibernate, restart or shut down this computer, or cancel a scheduled restart/shutdown. Restart and shutdown happen after one minute and can be cancelled. Requires the 'power-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)

solve_math: Maths: derivative, series (Taylor), expansion, factor, numeric integral (definite, or numeric for indefinite), numeric limit (at a point or oo), linear and quadratic solve, numeric sum of a series, evaluation to N digits, prime_factors / is_prime. Write maths plainly: 'x^2 + 3x', 'sin(x)/x', 'x^2 - 4 = 0'. (arguments: operation, expression, variable, point, lower, upper, order, digits, other)

calculate: Evaluate arithmetic and percentages ('15% of 2400'), or convert between units. Handles the four operations, powers, parentheses, factorial, permutations and combinations (perm/nPr, comb/nCr), gcd, lcm, sqrt, exp, log, ln, trig and inverse trig, and pi/e/tau - exact for whole numbers. For algebra with variables, derivatives, integrals, limits or equations, use solve_math. Converts length, mass, volume, time, data, pressure, frequency, power, energy and temperature, in the units a person actually meets - say '200 km to miles' or '70kg in lb'. Runs entirely on this machine with no network call. Refuses to guess: a percentage needs a number to apply to, and converting between quantities that measure different things is an error rather than a number. (arguments: expression)

charger_info: Report what is powering this machine: on battery or plugged in, AC adapter or USB-C, whether USB Power Delivery is in use, and the charger's wattage when the firmware reports it, plus battery charge and rate.

list_percepts: Show what Chronoa is currently perceiving - every fact held about this machine and the user right now, with its age, what expires it, and whether it would be included in the next reply. Use this to check what the assistant actually knows rather than what it says. (arguments: sense_filter, include_expired)

train.positives_desc: set_hostname: Report this computer's name (hostname), or rename it - the name other devices on the network and in Bluetooth see. The name must be letters, digits and hyphens only. Renaming requires the 'hostname-control-enabled' consent key and the administrator password; reporting needs neither. (arguments: action, name)

negatives.desc: chart: Make an SVG file from data, drawn on this computer with no install. chart: kind=bar|line|pie with data (bar/pie: [[label, number], ...]; line: [[x, y], ...], or several lines as series {name: [[x, y], ...]}), plus title, x_label, y_label. icon: a stroke icon by name (arrow-right, bell, calendar, check, clock, close, download, folder, heart, home, mail, search, settings, star, user). diagram: a top-to-bottom flow, steps=["Read", "Edit", "Test"] with optional arrows [[from, to, label], ...]. output is the .svg path, e.g. '~/Pictures/sales.svg'. (arguments: action, output, kind, data, series, steps, arrows, name, title, x_label, y_label)

landline_call: Place and answer calls on the JioFiber broadband landline over Wi-Fi, through the router - the same line the JioJoin app uses, the house's own landline number. 'status' says whether the line is connected and what call is on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+911234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' picks up a ringing call; 'hangup' ends, cancels or declines the current call. The voice is on this computer's speaker and microphone, nothing is recorded, and the landline handset keeps working. Needs this computer added to the line on the Shani Link app's Phone page and the 'landline-enabled' consent key. This is the landline, not a mobile over Bluetooth - that is 'bluetooth_call'. (arguments: action, number, name)

recording: Make subtitles or a transcript of a video or audio file, tell speakers apart, or remove background noise. Works on the sound, on this computer. text: what was said; subtitles: save an .srt beside it; speakers: who said what, turn by turn; clean: a copy with background noise removed; sounds: what can be heard in it (music, a dog, traffic...); listen: what can be heard around the computer right now (the microphone, a few seconds); streams: which applications are carrying audio right now, and the name to capture one by (a call in a browser is one); capture: record one of those for 5-600 seconds and transcribe it - which records the room, so it needs the sound consent like the microphone does. (arguments: action, path, range, language, people, seconds)

adb_workflow: A small Android Debug Bridge workflow. status: connected devices and their state; pair: the steps to authorise this computer; push and pull: copy one file between this computer and the phone. Needs 'phone-control-enabled' and a yes for each copy. Local paths stay inside your home; remote paths must be under /sdcard/. (arguments: action, serial, local, remote)

bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)

dashboard: Build a dashboard as one self-contained HTML page (headline numbers, charts and tables), drawn on this computer with no install, no network and no scripts. Give any of: cards [{label, value, sub}], charts [{type: bar|line|pie, title, data: [[label, number], ...]}], tables [{title, rows: [[header...], [row...]]}], plus title and when (a 'as of ...' line). output is the .html path, e.g. '~/Documents/sales-dashboard.html'. Static: run again to refresh it. (arguments: output, title, when, cards, charts, tables)
data_usage: How much internet data this computer has used today and this month, per network interface (from vnStat).

train.say: Press the phone camera shutter, media keys, or type on the phone.
train.positives_desc: phone_remote: Press keys on the paired phone as a Bluetooth keyboard: 'press' the camera 'shutter' (takes a photo in the camera app), play_pause, next, previous, volume_up/down, mute; or 'type' text into whatever field is focused on the phone. The phone must have paired 'Chronoa Remote'. Requires the 'phone-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, key, text)

negatives.desc: press_key: Press a key or key combination in the focused window, e.g. 'Return', 'Escape', 'Tab' or 'ctrl+shift+t'. This sends a key, not text - use type_text to type a string. Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key. X11 only. (arguments: key, repeat)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

ui_elements: Use another app's controls by what they are, through the accessibility tree. apps: which apps are reachable. inspect: list a window's buttons, fields, menus and labels with ids (app = its name; query narrows by text). press: activate an element by id (a button, checkbox, link, menu item). set_text: put text in a field by id. read: an element's text or value. menu: open a menu path like 'File > Export'. drive: one turn of driving - give an action and a control number and the reply is the app's new state in the same short numbered form, which is what a small model can act on. act: click, type or key an app by name or position, with a visible cursor. state: the numbered controls an app is showing. Works on a container's app and on this desktop's own apps alike. Requires 'input-control-enabled'; drive start also runs a container, so it needs 'container-control-enabled' as well. (arguments: action, app, id, text, query, path, do, how, number, image, keys, x, y)

convert_media: Convert an audio, video or image file to another format (mp3, ogg, opus, wav, flac, m4a, mp4, webm, gif, png, jpg, webp), optionally resizing to a width. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to, width)

media_control: Control music and video players: play, pause, toggle, next track, previous track, stop, restart (current track from the beginning), seek (skip ahead or go back by 'seconds'; negative goes back), or 'status' to say what is playing. (arguments: action, seconds)

lan_phone: Find phones on the SAME Wi-Fi network, using the KDE Connect protocol directly - so it works without KDE Connect or GSConnect installed. 'devices': what announced itself on this network in the last few seconds (phones, tablets, other computers). 'announce': make this computer findable by a phone's KDE Connect app. 'status': what this computer can and cannot do on the LAN. 'pair': pair with the device 'devices' found (the phone asks its owner). Needs the 'lan-phone-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, seconds)

phone: The user's paired phone via GSConnect/KDE Connect: status (reachable, battery), ring it to find it, ping it, share a file or link to it; read text messages ('messages': latest, from a contact, or unread only); send a text message ('send': to a contact name or number, or omit contact to reply to the latest conversation) with exactly the text given - draft it first; or 'call' a contact or number (opens the phone's dialer). The user confirms every message and call before it goes. Requires the 'phone-control-enabled' consent key; reading needs 'phone-messages-read-enabled', sending and calling 'phone-messages-send-enabled'. (arguments: action, device, target, contact, text, unread_only, limit)

train.say: Listen to FM radio through a USB receiver.
train.positives_desc: fm_radio: FM and AM broadcast radio. Five actions: 'hardware' for whether this computer can receive anything at all (a laptop usually cannot, and that is a true answer rather than a failure - it needs an RTL2832U USB dongle), 'bands' for the coverage, 'tune' to a frequency, 'decode' to demodulate a recorded IQ capture, and 'scan' to look for carriers in one. A frequency is given in MHz, e.g. 98.6. rtl_fm is narrowband and retunes per channel, so it cannot scan - scanning needs a wideband recording. No station names are guessed: a carrier gives a frequency, and naming it would need a table for your region. Requires the 'fm-radio-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, frequency, seconds, file, centre_mhz, out, deemphasis_us)

negatives.desc: usb_devices: What is plugged into this machine's USB ports (mice, phones, webcams, sticks, with their speed), and every Thunderbolt/USB4 device with whether it is authorised to work. Use for 'what's plugged in', 'why doesn't my dock work', 'is my webcam connected'. The USB list uses the 'usb-sense-enabled' switch. Read-only.

bluetooth_gatt: Read what a paired Bluetooth Low Energy device says about itself - a watch's or headset's battery, a heart-rate strap's live reading, which services a band offers. 'list': every paired device and whether it speaks this protocol. 'services': what one exposes. 'read': one stored value. 'listen': a live reading of something the device only pushes, e.g. heart rate - 'nothing arrived' is the truthful answer when the device is not measuring. Speakers, headphones and car stereios are older Bluetooth and expose nothing here, which is a true answer, not a failure; wearables, bands, straps, smart tags and thermometers answer. Needs 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' and the device must be connected. (arguments: action, device, seconds, characteristic)

recording: Make subtitles or a transcript of a video or audio file, tell speakers apart, or remove background noise. Works on the sound, on this computer. text: what was said; subtitles: save an .srt beside it; speakers: who said what, turn by turn; clean: a copy with background noise removed; sounds: what can be heard in it (music, a dog, traffic...); listen: what can be heard around the computer right now (the microphone, a few seconds); streams: which applications are carrying audio right now, and the name to capture one by (a call in a browser is one); capture: record one of those for 5-600 seconds and transcribe it - which records the room, so it needs the sound consent like the microphone does. (arguments: action, path, range, language, people, seconds)

audio_output: List the speakers/headphones (outputs) and microphones (inputs) and which one is the default, or switch the default output or input - 'play through my headphones', 'use the USB microphone', 'send sound to the HDMI monitor'. Pick a device by its number or part of its name. (arguments: action, device, kind)

get_location: Where this computer is right now - latitude, longitude and accuracy - from a GPS receiver or GNOME's location service. Use for 'where am I'. Requires the location sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off.

lan_phone: Find phones on the SAME Wi-Fi network, using the KDE Connect protocol directly - so it works without KDE Connect or GSConnect installed. 'devices': what announced itself on this network in the last few seconds (phones, tablets, other computers). 'announce': make this computer findable by a phone's KDE Connect app. 'status': what this computer can and cannot do on the LAN. 'pair': pair with the device 'devices' found (the phone asks its owner). Needs the 'lan-phone-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, seconds)

airplane_mode: Report which radios (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile broadband) are on, or turn airplane mode on (all radios off) or off. Changing requires the 'radio-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

train.say: search the web for how much the Chandrayaan-3 mission cost
train.positives_desc: web_search: Look something up on the web and return what the pages actually say: facts, prices, how-tos, anything no more specific tool covers. Give a search query, a specific URL, or both. For a scholarly question - a paper, a preprint, prior work, 'what does the research say' - set source=arxiv and it searches the arXiv preprint archive instead of the web. For news headlines use news; to click, fill in or book something on a site use browse. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: query, url, source)

negatives.desc: process_cost: What each running program is COSTING this machine right now, measured over the last second rather than as a snapshot: percent CPU split into user and system time, how much memory it holds, page faults (including the major ones that mean it is thrashing), and how many kB a second it is reading and writing. Answers 'what is using my CPU', 'what is making my computer slow', 'what is writing to my disk all the time', 'which program is swapping', 'why did everything freeze'. Use this when the machine feels slow; use list_processes to see what is running and disk_activity to see whether the disk itself is busy. Read-only; nothing is started, stopped or changed.

search_file_contents: Search inside text files under a directory for a literal string, and report which files contain it and on which lines. Skips binary files and very large files, and says how many it skipped. (arguments: text, path, file_pattern, case_sensitive, max_matches)

search_my_files: Search your own files by their contents - documents, notes, code - either in a directory you choose with Chronoa's own index, or through the desktop's index (LocalSearch on GNOME, Baloo on Plasma).
