'search' (default): what matches a few words. 'desktop': ask the desktop's index instead, needing 'document-search-enabled'. 'reindex': read the directory and build or refresh Chronoa's index (needed before the first search). 'status': what would be indexed and whether this machine can search by meaning. Needs the 'file-index-enabled' consent key for its own index. (arguments: action, query, kind, path, limit)

news: News headlines only (title, source, age), from Google News (or BBC) RSS feeds - not facts or what a page says, which is web_search. With no topic: the top stories. A topic can be a section - world, business, tech, science, health, sports, entertainment - or anything to search for, e.g. 'ISRO'. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: topic, source, limit)

chart: Make an SVG file from data, drawn on this computer with no install. chart: kind=bar|line|pie with data (bar/pie: [[label, number], ...]; line: [[x, y], ...], or several lines as series {name: [[x, y], ...]}), plus title, x_label, y_label. icon: a stroke icon by name (arrow-right, bell, calendar, check, clock, close, download, folder, heart, home, mail, search, settings, star, user). diagram: a top-to-bottom flow, steps=["Read", "Edit", "Test"] with optional arrows [[from, to, label], ...]. output is the .svg path, e.g. '~/Pictures/sales.svg'. (arguments: action, output, kind, data, series, steps, arrows, name, title, x_label, y_label)

conversations: The user's saved Chronoa conversations. list: recent ones; search: find what was said in earlier conversations (query); open: continue one (which = title or id); new: start a fresh one; rename (which, title); copy: duplicate one to try another way, optionally keeping only its first keep_turns user messages; export: save one as Markdown (path); delete: remove one permanently (needs 'file-delete-enabled'). (arguments: action, which, query, title, path, keep_turns)

find_and_replace: Find a string across files under a directory and optionally replace it. Reports what it would change without changing anything unless dry_run is explicitly false. Requires the 'bulk-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: find, replace, path, file_pattern, dry_run, case_sensitive)

train.say: Remind me tomorrow at 9 to pack my bags.
train.positives_desc: reminders: A dated list of reminders you can keep coming back to: add one, list what is still due, mark one done, or remove one. Optionally with a due time in words, e.g. 'tomorrow 9am' or 'in 3 hours'. (arguments: action, number, text, due)

negatives.desc: calendar_events: List events on the user's calendars (GNOME calendars and online accounts): today, tomorrow, this week, or the next few hours. Requires the 'calendar-read-enabled' consent key. (arguments: range, hours)

watch: Your MoYoung/Da Fit smartwatch: 'summary' (steps, distance, calories for 3 days, last night's sleep stages, today's stress, workouts), 'measure' a heart rate, blood oxygen or blood pressure on the wrist (takes up to a minute), read 'settings', 'set' one (step_goal, time_format 12h/24h, units metric/imperial, raise_to_wake, sedentary_reminder, other_app_notifications, power_saving, heart_rate_auto_interval, do_not_disturb '22:00-07:00'), 'sync_time', 'find' (make the watch ring), 'notify' (show a message on the watch), or set the 'profile' (height, weight, age, gender - weight is never measured by the watch). Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, device, what, setting, value, sender, text, kind, height_cm, weight_kg, age, gender)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

calendar_edit: Change the user's calendar: 'create' adds an event to the default calendar (title, start, optional duration or end, location); 'move' reschedules an event found by its current time and/or title to new_start; 'cancel' deletes one. Times in words: 'tomorrow 3pm', 'friday 5 pm', '2026-10-09 14:00'. Move and cancel ask the person to confirm. Ambiguous matches are refused with the candidates. Requires the 'calendar-write-enabled' consent key (move/cancel also 'calendar-read-enabled'). No invitations are sent. (arguments: action, title, start, duration, end, new_start, location, notes)

date_math: Date arithmetic: days until a date ('how many days until 25 December'), the date N days/weeks/months from a date ('what date is 45 days from now'), days between two dates, or the weekday of a date. (arguments: operation, date, other_date, amount, unit)

get_weather: Current weather and today's forecast - temperature, feels-like, rain, wind - for a named place, or for where this computer is if no place is given; with `when`, the forecast for tomorrow, a weekday, this week or the weekend instead. Use for weather, temperature outside, rain, forecast. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: place, when)

train.positives_desc: edit_image: Edit a picture (for faces or backgrounds use photo_video) and save the result as a new file next to it: resize (width and/or height, or percent), compress (quality, or to under a size in KB), crop, upscale (2-4x), rotate, flip, grayscale, a look (sepia, vignette, sketch, paint, enhance), strip metadata (location/camera), or convert format. Several edits can be combined in one call. For effects that depend on what is in the picture (blur faces, blur the background) use photo_video. (arguments: path, width, height, percent, upscale, quality, max_kb, crop, rotate, flip, grayscale, look, strip_metadata, format)

negatives.desc: photo_video: Blur or pixelate faces, blur or remove the background, or find people and objects in a photo or video. Works by what is in it, on this computer. identify: find faces and everyday objects (people, cars, dogs, cups...); effect: blur_faces, pixelate_faces, blur_background or remove_background, saved as a new file (videos keep their sound); keyframes: save the moments a video changes; describe: say what happens in a video. For a look like sepia or sketch, or resizing and converting, use edit_image or convert_media. (arguments: action, path, effect, subject, labelled_copy)

photos: Find the user's photos by what is in them or written on them, or when they were taken. search: query like 'receipt hardware shop', 'dog on the beach', 'december 2025'; index: update the index of the Pictures folder (a batch at a time); status: how much is indexed. (arguments: action, query, captions)

take_photo: Take a photo or selfie with the webcam and save it to the Pictures folder, optionally after a countdown in seconds (0-30). Requires the vision/camera consent. Not for screenshots (use screenshot) or video (use capture_video). (arguments: countdown, path, device, infrared)

create_video: Create a video: a slideshow from a list of pictures (each shown for a few seconds), or a simple clip of a colour for a duration. Writes a new .mp4 next to the inputs; never overwrites. (arguments: images, seconds, color, duration, width)

photo_metadata: Read a photo's embedded EXIF metadata: the camera and lens, the date and time it was taken, exposure, aperture, ISO, focal length, and the GPS location if one is recorded. Use for 'when was this photo taken', 'does this picture contain my location', 'which camera took it'. JPEG and TIFF. Read-only; the file is not changed. (arguments: path)

generate_image: Make a new picture from a text description, or change a photo the way a description says (from_photo, e.g. 'make it snowy', 'as a watercolour'), drawn locally by stable-diffusion.cpp. Describe it in English. Saves a PNG and returns its path. (arguments: prompt, avoid, size, steps, seed, output, from_photo, strength)

search_file_contents: Search inside text files under a directory for a literal string, and report which files contain it and on which lines. Skips binary files and very large files, and says how many it skipped. (arguments: text, path, file_pattern, case_sensitive, max_matches)

train.positives_desc: recording: Make subtitles or a transcript of a video or audio file, tell speakers apart, or remove background noise. Works on the sound, on this computer. text: what was said; subtitles: save an .srt beside it; speakers: who said what, turn by turn; clean: a copy with background noise removed; sounds: what can be heard in it (music, a dog, traffic...); listen: what can be heard around the computer right now (the microphone, a few seconds); streams: which applications are carrying audio right now, and the name to capture one by (a call in a browser is one); capture: record one of those for 5-600 seconds and transcribe it - which records the room, so it needs the sound consent like the microphone does. (arguments: action, path, range, language, people, seconds)

negatives.desc: read_video: Read a video's basics out loud (for subtitles or what was said use recording): how long it is, its resolution, its video codec, whether it has audio, and its bitrate. Add keyframes=true to also save the moments the image changes. The original is never modified. (arguments: path, keyframes)

capture_video: Record a short video from the camera (webcam), e.g. '/dev/video0', for a few seconds. Requires the vision/camera consent. Writes a new .mp4; no camera means a clear refusal. (arguments: device, seconds, infrared)

create_video: Create a video: a slideshow from a list of pictures (each shown for a few seconds), or a simple clip of a colour for a duration. Writes a new .mp4 next to the inputs; never overwrites. (arguments: images, seconds, color, duration, width)

edit_video: Edit a video and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, resize to a width, rotate, mute or keep only the audio, or change the speed. End times accept seconds ('95'), or 'MM:SS' / 'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, width, rotate, mute, audio_only, speed, output)

convert_media: Convert an audio, video or image file to another format (mp3, ogg, opus, wav, flac, m4a, mp4, webm, gif, png, jpg, webp), optionally resizing to a width. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to, width)

photo_video: Blur or pixelate faces, blur or remove the background, or find people and objects in a photo or video. Works by what is in it, on this computer. identify: find faces and everyday objects (people, cars, dogs, cups...); effect: blur_faces, pixelate_faces, blur_background or remove_background, saved as a new file (videos keep their sound); keyframes: save the moments a video changes; describe: say what happens in a video. For a look like sepia or sketch, or resizing and converting, use edit_image or convert_media. (arguments: action, path, effect, subject, labelled_copy)

default_apps: Show or change which application opens a kind of file - by MIME type ('application/pdf'), extension ('.pdf', 'mp4') or an example file - or the default web browser (target 'browser'). Use for 'what opens PDFs', 'make VLC open my videos', 'set Firefox as my default browser'. Changing a default requires the 'default-apps-enabled' consent key; showing one does not. (arguments: target, action, app)

train.say: Read an audio file's length, format, and bitrate.
train.positives_desc: read_audio: Read an audio file's basics out loud: how long it is, its codec, sample rate, channels, and bitrate. The original is never modified. (arguments: path)

negatives.desc: edit_audio: Edit a sound file and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, raise or lower the volume, normalize loudness, change speed, or convert to an audio format. End times accept seconds or 'MM:SS'/'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, volume, normalize, speed, to)

read_video: Read a video's basics out loud (for subtitles or what was said use recording): how long it is, its resolution, its video codec, whether it has audio, and its bitrate. Add keyframes=true to also save the moments the image changes. The original is never modified. (arguments: path, keyframes)

identify_file: Identify a file by reading its first bytes rather than trusting its name. Use for 'why won't this open', 'what is this file', 'is this really a PNG', 'this file has no extension'. Reports the detected format and whether the filename agrees with it, which is the usual cause of a file refusing to open in the program its name implies. Says plainly when a signature is unrecognised. Read-only. (arguments: path)
read_text_file: Read a text file and return its contents, optionally a range of lines. Use this to see what a file actually says. (arguments: path, start_line, max_lines)

read_image: Read a picture's basics out loud: width by height, format, and colour type, plus file size. For what the picture says, use read_document on it. The original is never modified. (arguments: path)

search_my_files: Search your own files by their contents - documents, notes, code - either in a directory you choose with Chronoa's own index, or through the desktop's index (LocalSearch on GNOME, Baloo on Plasma). 'search' (default): what matches a few words. 'desktop': ask the desktop's index instead, needing 'document-search-enabled'. 'reindex': read the directory and build or refresh Chronoa's index (needed before the first search). 'status': what would be indexed and whether this machine can search by meaning. Needs the 'file-index-enabled' consent key for its own index. (arguments: action, query, kind, path, limit)

audio_output: List the speakers/headphones (outputs) and microphones (inputs) and which one is the default, or switch the default output or input - 'play through my headphones', 'use the USB microphone', 'send sound to the HDMI monitor'. Pick a device by its number or part of its name. (arguments: action, device, kind)

train.say: Read an NFC tag, or write a link to a sticker.
train.positives_desc: nfc: Read and write NFC tags. 'scan': is there a reader here (most laptops have none, and that is a true answer). 'read': tap a tag and be told what is written on it. 'write': put a link on an Ultralight/NTAG sticker - a bank card, transit pass or hotel key is refused, not rewritten. 'emulate': present a tag to a phone. Needs the 'nfc-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, url, text, seconds, target)

negatives.desc: write_text_file: Write text to a file, creating it or replacing its contents. Refuses to replace a non-empty file unless asked to overwrite, and refuses binary data. (arguments: path, content, overwrite, append)

barcode: Make a Code 128 barcode PNG from short text, or read every QR code and barcode in a local image and say what kind of payload it holds. Both ask first. Nothing a code contains is opened or connected to. (arguments: action, text, path, output)

bluetooth_gatt: Read what a paired Bluetooth Low Energy device says about itself - a watch's or headset's battery, a heart-rate strap's live reading, which services a band offers. 'list': every paired device and whether it speaks this protocol. 'services': what one exposes. 'read': one stored value. 'listen': a live reading of something the device only pushes, e.g. heart rate - 'nothing arrived' is the truthful answer when the device is not measuring. Speakers, headphones and car stereios are older Bluetooth and expose nothing here, which is a true answer, not a failure; wearables, bands, straps, smart tags and thermometers answer. Needs 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' and the device must be connected. (arguments: action, device, seconds, characteristic)

extract_archive: Unpack a .tar/.tar.gz/.tgz/.zip archive, or any format 7z reads (.7z, .rar, .cab ...), into a directory. Every member is checked first and the archive is refused whole if any entry would be written outside the destination or is a link, a device or a FIFO. Will not overwrite existing files unless asked. (arguments: archive, destination, overwrite)

landline_call: Place and answer calls on the JioFiber broadband landline over Wi-Fi, through the router - the same line the JioJoin app uses, the house's own landline number. 'status' says whether the line is connected and what call is on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+911234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' picks up a ringing call; 'hangup' ends, cancels or declines the current call. The voice is on this computer's speaker and microphone, nothing is recorded, and the landline handset keeps working. Needs this computer added to the line on the Shani Link app's Phone page and the 'landline-enabled' consent key. This is the landline, not a mobile over Bluetooth - that is 'bluetooth_call'. (arguments: action, number, name)

phone: The user's paired phone via GSConnect/KDE Connect: status (reachable, battery), ring it to find it, ping it, share a file or link to it; read text messages ('messages': latest, from a contact, or unread only); send a text message ('send': to a contact name or number, or omit contact to reply to the latest conversation) with exactly the text given - draft it first; or 'call' a contact or number (opens the phone's dialer). The user confirms every message and call before it goes. Requires the 'phone-control-enabled' consent key; reading needs 'phone-messages-read-enabled', sending and calling 'phone-messages-send-enabled'. (arguments: action, device, target, contact, text, unread_only, limit)

ui_elements: Use another app's controls by what they are, through the accessibility tree. apps: which apps are reachable. inspect: list a window's buttons, fields, menus and labels with ids (app = its name; query narrows by text). press: activate an element by id (a button, checkbox, link, menu item). set_text: put text in a field by id. read: an element's text or value. menu: open a menu path like 'File > Export'. drive: one turn of driving - give an action and a control number and the reply is the app's new state in the same short numbered form, which is what a small model can act on. act: click, type or key an app by name or position, with a visible cursor. state: the numbered controls an app is showing. Works on a container's app and on this desktop's own apps alike. Requires 'input-control-enabled'; drive start also runs a container, so it needs 'container-control-enabled' as well. (arguments: action, app, id, text, query, path, do, how, number, image, keys, x, y)

train.say: Turn the Bluetooth adapter on or off.
train.positives_desc: toggle_bluetooth: Turn the Bluetooth adapter on or off, or report its state and the paired devices. Requires the 'bluetooth-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)

negatives.desc: backup_adapters: A small uniform view of local backup tools. list: which of restic, borg and rsync are installed; check: read a repository's own history (read-only); plan: print the exact backup command for a repository and paths, after asking. plan never runs the command. (arguments: action, backend, repository, paths, name)

airplane_mode: Report which radios (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile broadband) are on, or turn airplane mode on (all radios off) or off. Changing requires the 'radio-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)
bluetooth_devices: List paired Bluetooth devices (and which are connected), or connect / disconnect one by its name, e.g. 'connect my headphones'. (arguments: action, name)

bluetooth_gatt: Read what a paired Bluetooth Low Energy device says about itself - a watch's or headset's battery, a heart-rate strap's live reading, which services a band offers. 'list': every paired device and whether it speaks this protocol. 'services': what one exposes. 'read': one stored value. 'listen': a live reading of something the device only pushes, e.g. heart rate - 'nothing arrived' is the truthful answer when the device is not measuring. Speakers, headphones and car stereios are older Bluetooth and expose nothing here, which is a true answer, not a failure; wearables, bands, straps, smart tags and thermometers answer. Needs 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' and the device must be connected. (arguments: action, device, seconds, characteristic)

toggle_wifi: Turn the Wi-Fi radio on or off (only Wi-Fi - airplane_mode switches every radio, connect_wifi joins a network), or report whether Wi-Fi is on. Changing requires the 'radio-control-enabled' consent key; status needs no permission. (arguments: action)

accessibility: Turn an accessibility feature on or off, or report them all: screen reader, on-screen keyboard, magnifier (zoom), large text, high contrast, reduce motion (animations), sticky keys. (arguments: feature, enabled)

train.positives_desc: compare_files: Show what is different between two text files, as a unified diff. Reports 'identical' when they match. Use this to compare two versions of a config, or to see what a change actually did. (arguments: path_a, path_b, context_lines)

negatives.desc: solve_math: Maths: derivative, series (Taylor), expansion, factor, numeric integral (definite, or numeric for indefinite), numeric limit (at a point or oo), linear and quadratic solve, numeric sum of a series, evaluation to N digits, prime_factors / is_prime. Write maths plainly: 'x^2 + 3x', 'sin(x)/x', 'x^2 - 4 = 0'. (arguments: operation, expression, variable, point, lower, upper, order, digits, other)

cloud_files: See what is in this machine's configured cloud storage remotes - which remotes rclone knows, how many objects and bytes each holds, and what is at the top level of one. Use for 'what is in my cloud drive', 'is anything in the bucket', 'how big is my remote'. Read-only: it never copies, syncs or deletes anything. A machine with no remotes says so, because that means there is nowhere off-machine for anything to go. (arguments: remote, path)

find_files: Find files and folders by name under a directory, using a wildcard pattern such as '*.log' or 'report*'. Matches on the name only and never opens the files. To see what is in one folder, use list_directory. (arguments: pattern, path, include_hidden, max_results, details)

search_my_files: Search your own files by their contents - documents, notes, code - either in a directory you choose with Chronoa's own index, or through the desktop's index (LocalSearch on GNOME, Baloo on Plasma). 'search' (default): what matches a few words. 'desktop': ask the desktop's index instead, needing 'document-search-enabled'. 'reindex': read the directory and build or refresh Chronoa's index (needed before the first search). 'status': what would be indexed and whether this machine can search by meaning. Needs the 'file-index-enabled' consent key for its own index. (arguments: action, query, kind, path, limit)

compute_hash: Compute a checksum of a file, and optionally compare it with an expected value. Defaults to SHA-256, which is what package managers and download sites publish. (arguments: path, algorithm, expected)

date_math: Date arithmetic: days until a date ('how many days until 25 December'), the date N days/weeks/months from a date ('what date is 45 days from now'), days between two dates, or the weekday of a date. (arguments: operation, date, other_date, amount, unit)

fingerprint_status: Whether fingerprint login is set up on this machine, and which fingers are enrolled. Says which of the four real states it is in: no reader attached, reader present but nothing enrolled, fingers enrolled, or the daemon not running and the question unanswerable. Reading only - it never enrolls or deletes a fingerprint, because 'which fingers are enrolled' is a question and the other two are not. Needs no permission: it reports a machine's own login configuration, and the answer is about hardware and a per-user setting rather than anything private. (arguments: user)

train.say: Set, change, snooze or delete an alarm.
train.positives_desc: alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

negatives.desc: set_timer: Set a countdown timer that sends a desktop notification when it finishes; list pending timers, say how much time is left, add or take off time, pause, resume, reset to the original length, and cancel. With one timer pending, 'my timer' needs no id. The countdown is owned by systemd, so it fires even if the assistant is closed. It is refused rather than silently accepted when systemd is unavailable, because a timer recorded as pending that will never fire is the same lie as a camera reported as disabled when it is not. (arguments: action, seconds, label, id)

delete_file: Delete a file or folder by moving it to the desktop trash, where it stays recoverable. This is how you clear something out. The whole folder goes as one item and can be restored from the trash - nothing in this project is deleted permanently, so there is no faster or 'real' delete to reach for instead. Requires the 'file-delete-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path)

undo_last_change: Put a file or a Chronoa setting back the way Chronoa last found it, by restoring the content or value recorded just before Chronoa's own last change to it. Undoes Chronoa's recent writes only - NOT git history, NOT changes you made in an editor or a shell, and only while a recorded pre-image is still held. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, list, setting, steps)

desktop_setting: Read or change one desktop setting from a fixed list: animations (window and menu animations); cursor_size (mouse pointer size in pixels (24 is normal; 32, 48, 64 are larger)); single_click (open files and folders with a single click); clock_24h (show the top-bar clock in 24-hour format); clock_seconds (show seconds in the top-bar clock); battery_percentage (show the battery percentage in the top bar); hot_corner (open the overview when the pointer hits the top-left corner); natural_scroll (touchpad natural (reverse) scrolling); tap_to_click (tap the touchpad to click). Changing requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: setting, value)

set_locale: Report the system language and regional formats, list the locales available on this machine, or change one: the system language, or the date format (British day/month or American month/day order), number format (decimal comma or point), money, measurement or paper size (e.g. what='dates', locale='en_GB.UTF-8'). Takes effect at the next login. Changing requires the 'locale-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, locale, what)

set_scaling: Report or change the desktop's text scaling factor (1.0 is normal, 1.5 is 150%). Text scaling only - display-resolution and HiDPI scaling are not changed by this, because driving those black-screens sessions. Requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, factor)

set_screensaver: Report or change how long the machine waits before the screen blanks, and whether it then demands a password. The two are reported separately, because blanking without locking leaves anyone who walks up to the machine able to use it. Requires the 'idle-timeout-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, blank_after_minutes, lock)

train.say: The print queue, and cancelling a job.
train.positives_desc: print_queue: Show the printers, which one is the default, the print jobs still waiting, and what this machine can print to even when nothing is configured; or cancel a waiting job by its id. Use for 'what's printing', 'why isn't my printer there', 'what can I print to', 'cancel that print'. Cancelling requires the 'print-control-enabled' consent key; listing does not. (arguments: action, job, printer, option)

negatives.desc: print_file: Print a document file on the default printer, or on a named one. Refuses directories and non-document files. Reports the job as queued, since whether it actually printed is not observable from here. (arguments: path, printer)

power_action: Suspend (sleep), hibernate, restart or shut down this computer, or cancel a scheduled restart/shutdown. Restart and shutdown happen after one minute and can be cancelled. Requires the 'power-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

todo_list: Keep a list of tasks that survives between turns and restarts: add an item, change its status, mark what it is blocked by, or list what is outstanding. Use this to track a multi-step job rather than holding it in the conversation. Requires the 'todo-list-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, id, content, status, blocked_by)

backup_adapters: A small uniform view of local backup tools. list: which of restic, borg and rsync are installed; check: read a repository's own history (read-only); plan: print the exact backup command for a repository and paths, after asking. plan never runs the command. (arguments: action, backend, repository, paths, name)

compute_hash: Compute a checksum of a file, and optionally compare it with an expected value. Defaults to SHA-256, which is what package managers and download sites publish. (arguments: path, algorithm, expected)

ir_remote: Send and receive infrared remote-control codes, and build or read the pulse-space timings themselves. 'devices': is there IR hardware here (most machines have none, and that is a true answer). 'encode': turn an address and command into the NEC or RC-6 timings that would carry them. 'decode': turn timings into a code. 'send': transmit a code through an IR device. 'receive': capture a button press and decode it. Needs the 'ir-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, protocol, address, command, timings, seconds)

json_query: Ask questions about the shape of a JSON document: what keys it has, what a field contains, how many entries an array has, or the sum/unique/sorted values of an array. Give either a file path or paste the document itself. (arguments: path, document, field, operation, of)

train.positives_desc: generate_image: Make a new picture from a text description, or change a photo the way a description says (from_photo, e.g. 'make it snowy', 'as a watercolour'), drawn locally by stable-diffusion.cpp. Describe it in English. Saves a PNG and returns its path. (arguments: prompt, avoid, size, steps, seed, output, from_photo, strength)

negatives.desc: generate_password: Generate a strong random password, or a passphrase of random words, and copy it to the clipboard (it is never said or shown in the reply). (arguments: kind, length, symbols)

get_weather: Current weather and today's forecast - temperature, feels-like, rain, wind - for a named place, or for where this computer is if no place is given; with `when`, the forecast for tomorrow, a weekday, this week or the weekend instead. Use for weather, temperature outside, rain, forecast. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: place, when)

edit_image: Edit a picture (for faces or backgrounds use photo_video) and save the result as a new file next to it: resize (width and/or height, or percent), compress (quality, or to under a size in KB), crop, upscale (2-4x), rotate, flip, grayscale, a look (sepia, vignette, sketch, paint, enhance), strip metadata (location/camera), or convert format. Several edits can be combined in one call. For effects that depend on what is in the picture (blur faces, blur the background) use photo_video. (arguments: path, width, height, percent, upscale, quality, max_kb, crop, rotate, flip, grayscale, look, strip_metadata, format)

look_at_image: Look at a picture file and say what it shows, with the local vision model: objects, scenes, charts, screenshots, UI, handwriting. Use a prompt to ask something specific about it. For the exact words printed in a picture, use read_document. Needs the vision sense. (arguments: path, prompt)

read_image: Read a picture's basics out loud: width by height, format, and colour type, plus file size. For what the picture says, use read_document on it. The original is never modified. (arguments: path)

routines: Save a routine: a short phrase (e.g. 'good morning', 'leaving work') that later runs a whole request, e.g. 'tell me the weather, my calendar today and the top news'. Also list or delete routines. Saving runs nothing; saying the phrase later runs the request. (arguments: action, name, request, phrases)

barcode: Make a Code 128 barcode PNG from short text, or read every QR code and barcode in a local image and say what kind of payload it holds. Both ask first. Nothing a code contains is opened or connected to. (arguments: action, text, path, output)

train.positives_desc: find_recently_modified: List files under a directory whose recorded modification time is within the last N days, newest first. Use this to answer 'what did I change today'. This is a timestamp, so a tool that preserves or sets times (tar, rsync, cp -p) can move an entry without the content changing. (arguments: path, within_days, pattern, limit)

negatives.desc: get_datetime: Current date and time here or in a named place. (arguments: place)

calendar_events: List events on the user's calendars (GNOME calendars and online accounts): today, tomorrow, this week, or the next few hours. Requires the 'calendar-read-enabled' consent key. (arguments: range, hours)

git_inspect: Report a git working tree: what has changed and is not committed, the diff of those changes, recent commits, or the current branch and how far it is from its upstream; also the stashed work and the reflog (the record that survives rebases and amends). Reports UNKNOWN - never 'clean tree' - when git is missing, the folder is not a repository, or git fails. Requires the 'git-sense-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, subcommand, revision, since, context_lines)

kundali: Compute Vedic Kundali (birth chart), Panchang (daily almanac), transits, aspects, dignities, BaZi (Chinese Four Pillars), and Nakshatra details. Offline, no API keys, no external dependencies. panchang: Tithi, Vara, Nakshatra, Yoga, Karana. kundali: sidereal birth chart with planets, houses, Navamsha, Dasha, aspects, dignities. transit: transit positions and cross-aspects. aspects: planetary aspects. dignity: planet dignity in a sign. bazi: Chinese Four Pillars. nakshatra: nakshatra details. timelords: profections and firdaria. arabicparts: Arabic parts (lots). temperament: elemental temperament. lunarmansion: lunar mansion. charakarakas: Jaimini karakas. shadbala: planetary strength. combustion: combust planets. horary: horary chart. upagrahas: all upagrahas. arudha: Arudha padas. drishti: Vedic aspects. vishesha: special lagnas. muhurta: electional scoring. vimshopaka: Vimshopaka bala. cheshta: motion states. grahayuddha: planetary wars. upagrahas_full: all upagrahas. fullchart: complete chart JSON. ashtakavarga: Bhinna + Sarva ashtakavarga. gochara: transit analysis. bhava: house analysis. kalamana: time measurement. chinese: Chinese calendar. grahana: eclipse check. shadbala_full: complete shadbala. karakas_full: chara karakas with Rahu reflection. yogas: Vishesha yogas. nodes: lunar nodes. eclipse: eclipse details. charadasha: Chara dasha. yoginidasha: Yogini dasha. ashtottaridasha: Ashtottari dasha. (arguments: action, date, datetime, latitude, longitude, planet, sign, year, month, day, hour)
calendar_month: Show the calendar for a month (default this month), with today marked. (arguments: month, year)

convert_currency: Convert an amount of money between currencies (rupees, dollars, euros, pounds, yen, ...) at today's ECB reference rate. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off. (arguments: amount, from_currency, to_currency)
data_usage: How much internet data this computer has used today and this month, per network interface (from vnStat).

train.positives_desc: explain_command: Explain a Linux shell command (not a general topic) from the local manuals (tldr, man), e.g. 'what does tar do', 'how do I use rsync'; or find which command does something, e.g. 'which command shows disk usage'. (arguments: command, task)

negatives.desc: run_command: Run one program in the project folder and get its exit code and output - the project's tests (pytest, npm test, cargo test), its build or linter - to check that a change works. One program per call: no pipes, redirections or shell syntax. Requires the 'run-command-enabled' consent key; asks each time. (arguments: command, cwd, timeout_seconds, where, image, machine, network)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Use 'setpoints' to list built-in off-by-default proposals, 'describe-setpoint' to explain one, and 'arm-setpoint' to arm one whose own switch is already on; arming never switches one on. Listing and describing need no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds, setpoint)

backup_adapters: A small uniform view of local backup tools. list: which of restic, borg and rsync are installed; check: read a repository's own history (read-only); plan: print the exact backup command for a repository and paths, after asking. plan never runs the command. (arguments: action, backend, repository, paths, name)

find_device: Make a paired Bluetooth watch, band or tag buzz or ring so the person can find it - 'where is my watch', 'find my band'. Works on devices with the standard Immediate Alert service and on MoYoung (Da Fit) watches; anything else is refused rather than sent an unknown command. The device must be in range. Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: device)

ir_remote: Send and receive infrared remote-control codes, and build or read the pulse-space timings themselves. 'devices': is there IR hardware here (most machines have none, and that is a true answer). 'encode': turn an address and command into the NEC or RC-6 timings that would carry them. 'decode': turn timings into a code. 'send': transmit a code through an IR device. 'receive': capture a button press and decode it. Needs the 'ir-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, protocol, address, command, timings, seconds)

list_processes: List the processes running on this machine, with their pid, name, owner, CPU and memory use, sorted by CPU unless sort_by says otherwise. Use this to find what is using the machine - pass sort_by='memory' for the RAM question, which CPU order does not answer - or the pid of something you want to stop. (arguments: name_filter, sort_by, limit)

machine_capabilities: Report what this machine can actually do: which of the commands Chronoa knows how to use are really present, which Python modules import here, and which services are enabled. Asks the live machine rather than reading the shipped inventory, which describes the image it was built from and not necessarily this one. Use it before offering to convert a file, edit an image, read a document or capture audio, to find out whether that is even possible here.

train.positives_desc: set_timer: Set a countdown timer that sends a desktop notification when it finishes; list pending timers, say how much time is left, add or take off time, pause, resume, reset to the original length, and cancel. With one timer pending, 'my timer' needs no id. The countdown is owned by systemd, so it fires even if the assistant is closed. It is refused rather than silently accepted when systemd is unavailable, because a timer recorded as pending that will never fire is the same lie as a camera reported as disabled when it is not. (arguments: action, seconds, label, id)

negatives.desc: autostart_entries: Report everything on this machine that starts automatically: the autostart .desktop files in this user's home and /etc/xdg, the enabled systemd user units and timers, and the crontab. Use for 'what starts automatically', 'what runs at login', 'what is scheduled', 'why does this thing keep running', 'what did I set to start on its own'. Honours Hidden, OnlyShowIn and NotShowIn, and says 'cannot tell' rather than guessing when the desktop is unknown - which is the normal state outside a login session. Read-only; nothing is enabled, disabled or changed.

lan_phone: Find phones on the SAME Wi-Fi network, using the KDE Connect protocol directly - so it works without KDE Connect or GSConnect installed. 'devices': what announced itself on this network in the last few seconds (phones, tablets, other computers). 'announce': make this computer findable by a phone's KDE Connect app. 'status': what this computer can and cannot do on the LAN. 'pair': pair with the device 'devices' found (the phone asks its owner). Needs the 'lan-phone-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, seconds)

desktop_setting: Read or change one desktop setting from a fixed list: animations (window and menu animations); cursor_size (mouse pointer size in pixels (24 is normal; 32, 48, 64 are larger)); single_click (open files and folders with a single click); clock_24h (show the top-bar clock in 24-hour format); clock_seconds (show seconds in the top-bar clock); battery_percentage (show the battery percentage in the top bar); hot_corner (open the overview when the pointer hits the top-left corner); natural_scroll (touchpad natural (reverse) scrolling); tap_to_click (tap the touchpad to click). Changing requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: setting, value)

print_file: Print a document file on the default printer, or on a named one. Refuses directories and non-document files. Reports the job as queued, since whether it actually printed is not observable from here. (arguments: path, printer)

print_queue: Show the printers, which one is the default, the print jobs still waiting, and what this machine can print to even when nothing is configured; or cancel a waiting job by its id. Use for 'what's printing', 'why isn't my printer there', 'what can I print to', 'cancel that print'. Cancelling requires the 'print-control-enabled' consent key; listing does not. (arguments: action, job, printer, option)

todo_list: Keep a list of tasks that survives between turns and restarts: add an item, change its status, mark what it is blocked by, or list what is outstanding. Use this to track a multi-step job rather than holding it in the conversation. Requires the 'todo-list-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, id, content, status, blocked_by)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

train.say: Installed fonts, and which one is used.
train.positives_desc: list_fonts: List the font families installed on this machine (optionally only those whose name contains some text), and which real font the generic names - sans-serif, serif, monospace, emoji - or a font you name actually resolve to. Use for 'what fonts do I have', 'is Fira Code installed', 'which font is used for monospace'. Read-only. (arguments: query)

negatives.desc: install_app: Search Flathub for an app, or install / remove one for this user by its app ID (e.g. org.videolan.VLC, from a search). Installing and removing need the 'app-install-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, query, app_id)

install_model: Download a named model into the local Ollama. Takes an explicit model name and never picks one by itself - call recommend_model first and install only what the user agreed to. Warns rather than refuses when the model looks larger than available memory. This downloads gigabytes and needs the network. (arguments: name)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Use 'setpoints' to list built-in off-by-default proposals, 'describe-setpoint' to explain one, and 'arm-setpoint' to arm one whose own switch is already on; arming never switches one on. Listing and describing need no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds, setpoint)

read_document: Read the text of a PDF (optionally a page range) or of an image (OCR), e.g. to summarise it or read it out. For a PDF it also reports whether the document embeds its fonts, since one that does not prints wrong elsewhere. (arguments: path, first_page, last_page)

sing: Sing a line aloud: each syllable gets its own note, on one of five named contours (rising, falling, arch, level, wave) or the real tune from a 'midi_file'. It does NOT know any song, so never present its output as a particular tune unless a MIDI file was supplied. Needs soundtouch or rubberband. (arguments: text, shape, voice_style, midi_file)

translate_text: Translate text into another language, with the local model when it is running and a web service otherwise. The reply says which was used, because one sends your text to a third party. (arguments: text, to_language, from_language)

android_device: An Android phone connected with USB debugging (adb). devices: which are connected; info: model, Android version, battery, storage; screenshot: save the phone's screen as a PNG; apps: installed apps (query filters); push: copy a file to the phone (to, default /sdcard/Download); pull: copy a file from the phone; open_url: open a web link on the phone. Requires 'phone-control-enabled'. (arguments: action, serial, path, to, url, query, output)

train.say: how loud is it right now?
train.positives_desc: get_volume: Get the current volume and mute state of an audio output, or the default one. On a machine with more than one output - several monitors, headphones and a dock - 'the volume' is ambiguous, so pass the device exactly as `wpctl status` prints it to ask about a specific one. (arguments: device)

negatives.desc: set_volume: Set the system output volume to an exact percentage. (arguments: percent, device)

arrange_window: Arrange a window: tile (snap it to the left, right, top or bottom half of the screen - 'put it on the left half', side by side), minimize, maximize, unmaximize, make fullscreen, leave fullscreen, move, resize, or send it to another workspace - by window id from list_windows or by part of its title. tile takes side; move takes x and y, resize width and height (pixels), set_workspace a 0-based workspace. Nothing is closed; close_window does that. (arguments: action, window_id, title_contains, x, y, width, height, workspace, side)
click_pointer: Click a mouse button at the current pointer position. Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key (separate from the vision sense) to be enabled. (arguments: button, count)

scroll: Scroll the window under the pointer up, down, left or right by a number of wheel steps (move the pointer over it first). Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key (separate from the vision sense). (arguments: direction, amount)
read_audio: Read an audio file's basics out loud: how long it is, its codec, sample rate, channels, and bitrate. The original is never modified. (arguments: path)

read_image: Read a picture's basics out loud: width by height, format, and colour type, plus file size. For what the picture says, use read_document on it. The original is never modified. (arguments: path)

read_video: Read a video's basics out loud (for subtitles or what was said use recording): how long it is, its resolution, its video codec, whether it has audio, and its bitrate. Add keyframes=true to also save the moments the image changes. The original is never modified. (arguments: path, keyframes)

train.positives_desc: media_control: Control music and video players: play, pause, toggle, next track, previous track, stop, restart (current track from the beginning), seek (skip ahead or go back by 'seconds'; negative goes back), or 'status' to say what is playing. (arguments: action, seconds)

negatives.desc: convert_media: Convert an audio, video or image file to another format (mp3, ogg, opus, wav, flac, m4a, mp4, webm, gif, png, jpg, webp), optionally resizing to a width. Writes a new file next to the original; never overwrites. (arguments: path, to, width)

open_application: Open or launch an installed application by name or by kind, e.g. 'firefox', 'files', 'settings', 'music player', 'text editor'. Not for websites: use browse to open a site and work on it. (arguments: name)

phone_remote: Press keys on the paired phone as a Bluetooth keyboard: 'press' the camera 'shutter' (takes a photo in the camera app), play_pause, next, previous, volume_up/down, mute; or 'type' text into whatever field is focused on the phone. The phone must have paired 'Chronoa Remote'. Requires the 'phone-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, key, text)

set_timer: Set a countdown timer that sends a desktop notification when it finishes; list pending timers, say how much time is left, add or take off time, pause, resume, reset to the original length, and cancel. With one timer pending, 'my timer' needs no id. The countdown is owned by systemd, so it fires even if the assistant is closed. It is refused rather than silently accepted when systemd is unavailable, because a timer recorded as pending that will never fire is the same lie as a camera reported as disabled when it is not. (arguments: action, seconds, label, id)

recording: Make subtitles or a transcript of a video or audio file, tell speakers apart, or remove background noise. Works on the sound, on this computer. text: what was said; subtitles: save an .srt beside it; speakers: who said what, turn by turn; clean: a copy with background noise removed; sounds: what can be heard in it (music, a dog, traffic...); listen: what can be heard around the computer right now (the microphone, a few seconds); streams: which applications are carrying audio right now, and the name to capture one by (a call in a browser is one); capture: record one of those for 5-600 seconds and transcribe it - which records the room, so it needs the sound consent like the microphone does. (arguments: action, path, range, language, people, seconds)

list_shortcuts: List this machine's keyboard shortcuts, or find what one key does. Reads GNOME's two keybinding schemas, so it covers both window management and the hardware media keys, and reports that the scheme does not apply on a desktop that does not use it rather than listing defaults for a desktop that is not running. Reading a shortcut is not a change and needs no permission. (arguments: action, keys)

photo_video: Blur or pixelate faces, blur or remove the background, or find people and objects in a photo or video. Works by what is in it, on this computer. identify: find faces and everyday objects (people, cars, dogs, cups...); effect: blur_faces, pixelate_faces, blur_background or remove_background, saved as a new file (videos keep their sound); keyframes: save the moments a video changes; describe: say what happens in a video. For a look like sepia or sketch, or resizing and converting, use edit_image or convert_media. (arguments: action, path, effect, subject, labelled_copy)

train.positives_desc: set_clipboard: Write text to the system clipboard. (arguments: text)

negatives.desc: get_clipboard: Read the current contents of the system clipboard.

move_or_copy_file: Move or copy a file or directory to a new path. Moving a directory into itself is refused, and an existing destination is not overwritten unless asked. (arguments: source, destination, mode, overwrite)
find_emoji: Find an emoji or symbol by name (heart, thumbs up, rupee sign, arrow) and copy the best match to the clipboard. (arguments: name)
generate_password: Generate a strong random password, or a passphrase of random words, and copy it to the clipboard (it is never said or shown in the reply). (arguments: kind, length, symbols)

conversations: The user's saved Chronoa conversations. list: recent ones; search: find what was said in earlier conversations (query); open: continue one (which = title or id); new: start a fresh one; rename (which, title); copy: duplicate one to try another way, optionally keeping only its first keep_turns user messages; export: save one as Markdown (path); delete: remove one permanently (needs 'file-delete-enabled'). (arguments: action, which, query, title, path, keep_turns)

adb_workflow: A small Android Debug Bridge workflow. status: connected devices and their state; pair: the steps to authorise this computer; push and pull: copy one file between this computer and the phone. Needs 'phone-control-enabled' and a yes for each copy. Local paths stay inside your home; remote paths must be under /sdcard/. (arguments: action, serial, local, remote)

android_device: An Android phone connected with USB debugging (adb). devices: which are connected; info: model, Android version, battery, storage; screenshot: save the phone's screen as a PNG; apps: installed apps (query filters); push: copy a file to the phone (to, default /sdcard/Download); pull: copy a file from the phone; open_url: open a web link on the phone. Requires 'phone-control-enabled'. (arguments: action, serial, path, to, url, query, output)

train.say: Undo Chronoa's last change to a file.
train.positives_desc: undo_last_change: Put a file or a Chronoa setting back the way Chronoa last found it, by restoring the content or value recorded just before Chronoa's own last change to it. Undoes Chronoa's recent writes only - NOT git history, NOT changes you made in an editor or a shell, and only while a recorded pre-image is still held. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, list, setting, steps)

negatives.desc: office_document: Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx) and PowerPoint (.pptx) files; also reads .odt/.ods/.odp. read: text with headings, tables, one section per sheet or slide (sheet, cell_range like A1:D20, formulas=true to see formulas). create: a new file from content - for .docx Markdown-style text (# headings, - bullets, 1. lists, | tables |, **bold**); for .xlsx rows (list of lists), or sheets {name: rows}, or CSV/Markdown-table text in content, '=...' cells are formulas; for .pptx slides [{title, bullets[], subtitle}]. set_cells: values {'B12': 42, 'C1': 'Total'} in a sheet. replace_text / append: change a .docx. pdf_images: save a PDF's embedded pictures to a folder. Changing an existing file needs 'file-edit-enabled' and can be undone with undo_last_change. (arguments: action, path, content, rows, sheets, chart, slides, values, sheet, cell_range, formulas, find, replace, title, overwrite, output_dir)

get_file_info: Report one file's type, size, when it was last modified, and who can read it. Use this to answer 'when did I last edit this' or 'who else can read this file' - no other skill reports timestamps or permissions. (arguments: path)

edit_file: Replace one exact piece of text in one named file. The text to replace must appear exactly once, or nothing is written - the count and line numbers are reported instead of a guess being made. Use this to change a specific line; use find_and_replace to change a string across many files. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, old_string, new_string, preview, replace_all)

find_recently_modified: List files under a directory whose recorded modification time is within the last N days, newest first. Use this to answer 'what did I change today'. This is a timestamp, so a tool that preserves or sets times (tar, rsync, cp -p) can move an entry without the content changing. (arguments: path, within_days, pattern, limit)

delete_file: Delete a file or folder by moving it to the desktop trash, where it stays recoverable. This is how you clear something out. The whole folder goes as one item and can be restored from the trash - nothing in this project is deleted permanently, so there is no faster or 'real' delete to reach for instead. Requires the 'file-delete-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path)

download_file: Download a file from a web address and save it to disk, reporting the size and how long it took. Use for 'download that file', 'get this installer', 'save that page'. Only http and https; a site that answers with an error page reports that rather than saving the error as if it were the file. (arguments: url, destination, engine)

identify_file: Identify a file by reading its first bytes rather than trusting its name. Use for 'why won't this open', 'what is this file', 'is this really a PNG', 'this file has no extension'. Reports the detected format and whether the filename agrees with it, which is the usual cause of a file refusing to open in the program its name implies. Says plainly when a signature is unrecognised. Read-only. (arguments: path)

train.positives_desc: manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Use 'setpoints' to list built-in off-by-default proposals, 'describe-setpoint' to explain one, and 'arm-setpoint' to arm one whose own switch is already on; arming never switches one on. Listing and describing need no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds, setpoint)

negatives.desc: alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

resolve_conflict: Work out what is conflicting in a git repository and resolve it. 'show' lists every unmerged file and prints all three sides git holds - the common ancestor, your side and theirs - so there is no guessing about which is which; 'ours' and 'theirs' take a whole side of the named files and mark them resolved; 'mark' marks files you have edited by hand; 'abort' abandons the merge, rebase or cherry-pick and leaves the commits to try again. There is no automatic merge, because deciding which line is right is a judgement about the code and only you can make it. Reading needs 'git-sense-enabled'; changing the working tree needs 'git-write-enabled'. (arguments: action, path, paths)

train.positives_desc: disk_health: Health of this machine's drives (SMART/NVMe status and wear where it can be read) and whether each mounted filesystem - /, /home and the rest - sits on an encrypted (LUKS) volume. Use for 'is my SSD healthy', 'is my disk encrypted', 'how worn is my drive'. Drive health uses the 'storage-sense-enabled' switch. Read-only.

negatives.desc: ui_elements: Use another app's controls by what they are, through the accessibility tree. apps: which apps are reachable. inspect: list a window's buttons, fields, menus and labels with ids (app = its name; query narrows by text). press: activate an element by id (a button, checkbox, link, menu item). set_text: put text in a field by id. read: an element's text or value. menu: open a menu path like 'File > Export'. drive: one turn of driving - give an action and a control number and the reply is the app's new state in the same short numbered form, which is what a small model can act on. act: click, type or key an app by name or position, with a visible cursor. state: the numbered controls an app is showing. Works on a container's app and on this desktop's own apps alike. Requires 'input-control-enabled'; drive start also runs a container, so it needs 'container-control-enabled' as well. (arguments: action, app, id, text, query, path, do, how, number, image, keys, x, y)

close_window: Ask a window to close, the way its close button would - the application still gets the chance to ask about unsaved work. Requires the 'window-close-enabled' consent key. Works on X11, Plasma and GNOME (GTK4 apps, or any app with Chronoa's window control extension). (arguments: window_id, title_contains)

focus_window: Bring a window to the front and give it keyboard focus, by window id from list_windows or by matching part of its title. Works on X11 and Plasma; on GNOME it needs Chronoa's window control extension and says so. (arguments: window_id, title_contains)
disk_usage: Report how full each filesystem is, and optionally which directories under a given path use the most space. Read-only: it never deletes anything. (arguments: path)

manage_mount: Mount an unmounted filesystem or drive, or unmount one, through the desktop's own disk service so its authorisation rules apply. Verifies the result against the mount table. Requires the 'mount-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, device)

arrange_window: Arrange a window: tile (snap it to the left, right, top or bottom half of the screen - 'put it on the left half', side by side), minimize, maximize, unmaximize, make fullscreen, leave fullscreen, move, resize, or send it to another workspace - by window id from list_windows or by part of its title. tile takes side; move takes x and y, resize width and height (pixels), set_workspace a 0-based workspace. Nothing is closed; close_window does that. (arguments: action, window_id, title_contains, x, y, width, height, workspace, side)

list_windows: List the windows currently open, with their title, class and geometry. Pass title_contains to narrow the list to windows matching some text in their title or application - a desktop usually has more windows open than are worth reading. Where xdotool cannot see the session it falls back to the accessibility bus and says so, because that list is not complete. (arguments: title_contains)

train.positives_desc: get_location: Where this computer is right now - latitude, longitude and accuracy - from a GPS receiver or GNOME's location service. Use for 'where am I'. Requires the location sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off.

negatives.desc: adb_workflow: A small Android Debug Bridge workflow. status: connected devices and their state; pair: the steps to authorise this computer; push and pull: copy one file between this computer and the phone. Needs 'phone-control-enabled' and a yes for each copy. Local paths stay inside your home; remote paths must be under /sdcard/. (arguments: action, serial, local, remote)

bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)

chart: Make an SVG file from data, drawn on this computer with no install. chart: kind=bar|line|pie with data (bar/pie: [[label, number], ...]; line: [[x, y], ...], or several lines as series {name: [[x, y], ...]}), plus title, x_label, y_label. icon: a stroke icon by name (arrow-right, bell, calendar, check, clock, close, download, folder, heart, home, mail, search, settings, star, user). diagram: a top-to-bottom flow, steps=["Read", "Edit", "Test"] with optional arrows [[from, to, label], ...]. output is the .svg path, e.g. '~/Pictures/sales.svg'. (arguments: action, output, kind, data, series, steps, arrows, name, title, x_label, y_label)

dashboard: Build a dashboard as one self-contained HTML page (headline numbers, charts and tables), drawn on this computer with no install, no network and no scripts. Give any of: cards [{label, value, sub}], charts [{type: bar|line|pie, title, data: [[label, number], ...]}], tables [{title, rows: [[header...], [row...]]}], plus title and when (a 'as of ...' line). output is the .html path, e.g. '~/Documents/sales-dashboard.html'. Static: run again to refresh it. (arguments: output, title, when, cards, charts, tables)
data_usage: How much internet data this computer has used today and this month, per network interface (from vnStat).

fm_radio: FM and AM broadcast radio. Five actions: 'hardware' for whether this computer can receive anything at all (a laptop usually cannot, and that is a true answer rather than a failure - it needs an RTL2832U USB dongle), 'bands' for the coverage, 'tune' to a frequency, 'decode' to demodulate a recorded IQ capture, and 'scan' to look for carriers in one. A frequency is given in MHz, e.g. 98.6. rtl_fm is narrowband and retunes per channel, so it cannot scan - scanning needs a wideband recording. No station names are guessed: a carrier gives a frequency, and naming it would need a table for your region. Requires the 'fm-radio-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, frequency, seconds, file, centre_mhz, out, deemphasis_us)

lan_phone: Find phones on the SAME Wi-Fi network, using the KDE Connect protocol directly - so it works without KDE Connect or GSConnect installed. 'devices': what announced itself on this network in the last few seconds (phones, tablets, other computers). 'announce': make this computer findable by a phone's KDE Connect app. 'status': what this computer can and cannot do on the LAN. 'pair': pair with the device 'devices' found (the phone asks its owner). Needs the 'lan-phone-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, seconds)

landline_call: Place and answer calls on the JioFiber broadband landline over Wi-Fi, through the router - the same line the JioJoin app uses, the house's own landline number. 'status' says whether the line is connected and what call is on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+911234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' picks up a ringing call; 'hangup' ends, cancels or declines the current call. The voice is on this computer's speaker and microphone, nothing is recorded, and the landline handset keeps working. Needs this computer added to the line on the Shani Link app's Phone page and the 'landline-enabled' consent key. This is the landline, not a mobile over Bluetooth - that is 'bluetooth_call'. (arguments: action, number, name)

train.positives_desc: scan_document: Scan a page and return its text (OCR), keeping the image in ~/Documents/Scans. source: 'scanner' (default; list_only lists them), 'camera' (hold the page up to the webcam; it is found and straightened), or 'photo' (straighten and read a picture of a page at path). 'Scan this letter and read it to me.' (arguments: source, path, list_only, device)

negatives.desc: nfc: Read and write NFC tags. 'scan': is there a reader here (most laptops have none, and that is a true answer). 'read': tap a tag and be told what is written on it. 'write': put a link on an Ultralight/NTAG sticker - a bank card, transit pass or hotel key is refused, not rewritten. 'emulate': present a tag to a phone. Needs the 'nfc-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, url, text, seconds, target)

fm_radio: FM and AM broadcast radio. Five actions: 'hardware' for whether this computer can receive anything at all (a laptop usually cannot, and that is a true answer rather than a failure - it needs an RTL2832U USB dongle), 'bands' for the coverage, 'tune' to a frequency, 'decode' to demodulate a recorded IQ capture, and 'scan' to look for carriers in one. A frequency is given in MHz, e.g. 98.6. rtl_fm is narrowband and retunes per channel, so it cannot scan - scanning needs a wideband recording. No station names are guessed: a carrier gives a frequency, and naming it would need a table for your region. Requires the 'fm-radio-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, frequency, seconds, file, centre_mhz, out, deemphasis_us)

read_document: Read the text of a PDF (optionally a page range) or of an image (OCR), e.g. to summarise it or read it out. For a PDF it also reports whether the document embeds its fonts, since one that does not prints wrong elsewhere. (arguments: path, first_page, last_page)

email_read: Read a locally configured IMAP mailbox: 'list' recent messages (or 'unseen'), or 'get' one by 'uid'. Needs the 'email-read-enabled' consent key. There is no built-in account or cloud credential - the account must be configured locally. (arguments: action, uid, unseen)
read_audio: Read an audio file's basics out loud: how long it is, its codec, sample rate, channels, and bitrate. The original is never modified. (arguments: path)

read_image: Read a picture's basics out loud: width by height, format, and colour type, plus file size. For what the picture says, use read_document on it. The original is never modified. (arguments: path)

read_logs: Read recent log output from a named system service, or from the kernel when no service is named. Returns the most recent lines first-context-last, and says how much it did not show. (arguments: unit, lines, priority, since)

train.say: Open the system Settings at a page.
train.positives_desc: open_settings: Open the system Settings app at a specific page, e.g. 'wifi', 'bluetooth', 'display', 'sound', 'power', 'privacy', 'keyboard', 'mouse', 'touchpad', 'printers', 'users', 'about', 'date_time', 'region', 'notifications', 'background', 'accessibility'. GNOME and KDE Plasma. Use open_application for Settings without a page. (arguments: page)

negatives.desc: open_application: Open or launch an installed application by name or by kind, e.g. 'firefox', 'files', 'settings', 'music player', 'text editor'. Not for websites: use browse to open a site and work on it. (arguments: name)

system_info: Describe the machine Chronoa is running on: distribution, kernel, architecture, uptime, load, memory, CPU count, whether this is a desktop session or a container, and the hardware identity (make, model, board, BIOS version).

open_file: Open one specific file or folder (by its path) using the desktop's default application for it - the same thing double-clicking it would do. To launch an app such as the file manager, use open_application. (arguments: path)

watch: Your MoYoung/Da Fit smartwatch: 'summary' (steps, distance, calories for 3 days, last night's sleep stages, today's stress, workouts), 'measure' a heart rate, blood oxygen or blood pressure on the wrist (takes up to a minute), read 'settings', 'set' one (step_goal, time_format 12h/24h, units metric/imperial, raise_to_wake, sedentary_reminder, other_app_notifications, power_saving, heart_rate_auto_interval, do_not_disturb '22:00-07:00'), 'sync_time', 'find' (make the watch ring), 'notify' (show a message on the watch), or set the 'profile' (height, weight, age, gender - weight is never measured by the watch). Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, device, what, setting, value, sender, text, kind, height_cm, weight_kg, age, gender)

process_cost: What each running program is COSTING this machine right now, measured over the last second rather than as a snapshot: percent CPU split into user and system time, how much memory it holds, page faults (including the major ones that mean it is thrashing), and how many kB a second it is reading and writing. Answers 'what is using my CPU', 'what is making my computer slow', 'what is writing to my disk all the time', 'which program is swapping', 'why did everything freeze'. Use this when the machine feels slow; use list_processes to see what is running and disk_activity to see whether the disk itself is busy. Read-only; nothing is started, stopped or changed.

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

android_device: An Android phone connected with USB debugging (adb). devices: which are connected; info: model, Android version, battery, storage; screenshot: save the phone's screen as a PNG; apps: installed apps (query filters); push: copy a file to the phone (to, default /sdcard/Download); pull: copy a file from the phone; open_url: open a web link on the phone. Requires 'phone-control-enabled'. (arguments: action, serial, path, to, url, query, output)

train.say: Read a watch or band's battery, sensors and firmware.
train.positives_desc: bluetooth_gatt: Read what a paired Bluetooth Low Energy device says about itself - a watch's or headset's battery, a heart-rate strap's live reading, which services a band offers. 'list': every paired device and whether it speaks this protocol. 'services': what one exposes. 'read': one stored value. 'listen': a live reading of something the device only pushes, e.g. heart rate - 'nothing arrived' is the truthful answer when the device is not measuring. Speakers, headphones and car stereios are older Bluetooth and expose nothing here, which is a true answer, not a failure; wearables, bands, straps, smart tags and thermometers answer. Needs 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' and the device must be connected. (arguments: action, device, seconds, characteristic)

negatives.desc: watch: Your MoYoung/Da Fit smartwatch: 'summary' (steps, distance, calories for 3 days, last night's sleep stages, today's stress, workouts), 'measure' a heart rate, blood oxygen or blood pressure on the wrist (takes up to a minute), read 'settings', 'set' one (step_goal, time_format 12h/24h, units metric/imperial, raise_to_wake, sedentary_reminder, other_app_notifications, power_saving, heart_rate_auto_interval, do_not_disturb '22:00-07:00'), 'sync_time', 'find' (make the watch ring), 'notify' (show a message on the watch), or set the 'profile' (height, weight, age, gender - weight is never measured by the watch). Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, device, what, setting, value, sender, text, kind, height_cm, weight_kg, age, gender)

firmware_updates: List firmware updates fwupd knows for this machine's devices (BIOS, SSD, dock, touchpad...) and what each fixes, plus the firmware versions this machine is running. Read-only; nothing is installed.

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Use 'setpoints' to list built-in off-by-default proposals, 'describe-setpoint' to explain one, and 'arm-setpoint' to arm one whose own switch is already on; arming never switches one on. Listing and describing need no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds, setpoint)

set_power_profile: Switch the machine between its power profiles - typically power-saver, balanced and performance - and report which one is active now. The profile list is read from the machine rather than assumed, because which profiles exist depends on the CPU driver: switching to one the machine does not have is refused with the valid names listed. Changes the CPU and platform power behaviour, not a per-application setting. (arguments: profile)
