charger_info: Report what is powering this machine: on battery or plugged in, AC adapter or USB-C, whether USB Power Delivery is in use, and the charger's wattage when the firmware reports it, plus battery charge and rate.
get_battery_status: Get the current battery charge percentage and charging state.

power_action: Suspend (sleep), hibernate, restart or shut down this computer, or cancel a scheduled restart/shutdown. Restart and shutdown happen after one minute and can be cancelled. Requires the 'power-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

train.positives_desc: random_pick: Flip a coin, roll dice ('2d6'), pick a random number in a range, or choose one of a list of options. (arguments: kind, dice, low, high, options)

negatives.desc: edit_image: Edit a picture (for faces or backgrounds use photo_video) and save the result as a new file next to it: resize (width and/or height, or percent), compress (quality, or to under a size in KB), crop, upscale (2-4x), rotate, flip, grayscale, a look (sepia, vignette, sketch, paint, enhance), strip metadata (location/camera), or convert format. Several edits can be combined in one call. For effects that depend on what is in the picture (blur faces, blur the background) use photo_video. (arguments: path, width, height, percent, upscale, quality, max_kb, crop, rotate, flip, grayscale, look, strip_metadata, format)
generate_password: Generate a strong random password, or a passphrase of random words, and copy it to the clipboard (it is never said or shown in the reply). (arguments: kind, length, symbols)

train.say: Which model would fit this machine?
train.positives_desc: recommend_model: Recommend local language models that fit this machine's currently available memory, largest first, marking which support reliable tool calling. Reports available (not total) memory and the budget used. Does not download anything. (arguments: limit)

negatives.desc: install_model: Download a named model into the local Ollama. Takes an explicit model name and never picks one by itself - call recommend_model first and install only what the user agreed to. Warns rather than refuses when the model looks larger than available memory. This downloads gigabytes and needs the network. (arguments: name)

machine_capabilities: Report what this machine can actually do: which of the commands Chronoa knows how to use are really present, which Python modules import here, and which services are enabled. Asks the live machine rather than reading the shipped inventory, which describes the image it was built from and not necessarily this one. Use it before offering to convert a file, edit an image, read a document or capture audio, to find out whether that is even possible here.

notes: Keep your own notes in a plain list stored on this machine: 'add' one from 'text', 'list' them, 'search' by text or id, 'remove' one by 'id'. Never sent to a model. For what the assistant itself believes and uses in its replies, use remember_fact instead. (arguments: action, text, query, id)

speaker_id: Opt-in voice identity using the local speaker model. enrol: remember a person's voice from a 16 kHz mono WAV, with their name and the basis on which they agreed; identify: say which enrolled voice a WAV sounds like; list: names already enrolled; forget: remove one. Needs the hearing consent and an explicit yes for enrol and forget. Nothing about the voice leaves this machine. (arguments: action, name, clip, basis)

system_info: Describe the machine Chronoa is running on: distribution, kernel, architecture, uptime, load, memory, CPU count, whether this is a desktop session or a container, and the hardware identity (make, model, board, BIOS version).

run_command: Run one program in the project folder and get its exit code and output - the project's tests (pytest, npm test, cargo test), its build or linter - to check that a change works. One program per call: no pipes, redirections or shell syntax. Requires the 'run-command-enabled' consent key; asks each time. (arguments: command, cwd, timeout_seconds, where, image, machine, network)

find_device: Make a paired Bluetooth watch, band or tag buzz or ring so the person can find it - 'where is my watch', 'find my band'. Works on devices with the standard Immediate Alert service and on MoYoung (Da Fit) watches; anything else is refused rather than sent an unknown command. The device must be in range. Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: device)

train.say: What is the integral of x squared?
train.positives_desc: solve_math: Maths: derivative, series (Taylor), expansion, factor, numeric integral (definite, or numeric for indefinite), numeric limit (at a point or oo), linear and quadratic solve, numeric sum of a series, evaluation to N digits, prime_factors / is_prime. Write maths plainly: 'x^2 + 3x', 'sin(x)/x', 'x^2 - 4 = 0'. (arguments: operation, expression, variable, point, lower, upper, order, digits, other)

negatives.desc: calculate: Evaluate arithmetic and percentages ('15% of 2400'), or convert between units. Handles the four operations, powers, parentheses, factorial, permutations and combinations (perm/nPr, comb/nCr), gcd, lcm, sqrt, exp, log, ln, trig and inverse trig, and pi/e/tau - exact for whole numbers. For algebra with variables, derivatives, integrals, limits or equations, use solve_math. Converts length, mass, volume, time, data, pressure, frequency, power, energy and temperature, in the units a person actually meets - say '200 km to miles' or '70kg in lb'. Runs entirely on this machine with no network call. Refuses to guess: a percentage needs a number to apply to, and converting between quantities that measure different things is an error rather than a number. (arguments: expression)

train.positives_desc: find_emoji: Find an emoji or symbol by name (heart, thumbs up, rupee sign, arrow) and copy the best match to the clipboard. (arguments: name)

negatives.desc: find_device: Make a paired Bluetooth watch, band or tag buzz or ring so the person can find it - 'where is my watch', 'find my band'. Works on devices with the standard Immediate Alert service and on MoYoung (Da Fit) watches; anything else is refused rather than sent an unknown command. The device must be in range. Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: device)

find_and_replace: Find a string across files under a directory and optionally replace it. Reports what it would change without changing anything unless dry_run is explicitly false. Requires the 'bulk-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: find, replace, path, file_pattern, dry_run, case_sensitive)

find_files: Find files and folders by name under a directory, using a wildcard pattern such as '*.log' or 'report*'. Matches on the name only and never opens the files. To see what is in one folder, use list_directory. (arguments: pattern, path, include_hidden, max_results, details)

find_recently_modified: List files under a directory whose recorded modification time is within the last N days, newest first. Use this to answer 'what did I change today'. This is a timestamp, so a tool that preserves or sets times (tar, rsync, cp -p) can move an entry without the content changing. (arguments: path, within_days, pattern, limit)

list_shortcuts: List this machine's keyboard shortcuts, or find what one key does. Reads GNOME's two keybinding schemas, so it covers both window management and the hardware media keys, and reports that the scheme does not apply on a desktop that does not use it rather than listing defaults for a desktop that is not running. Reading a shortcut is not a change and needs no permission. (arguments: action, keys)

maps: OpenStreetMap maps: find where a place is ('find'), driving/walking/cycling directions ('directions') or just distance and time ('travel_time') between places, the nearest kind of place such as petrol pump, hotel, ATM or hospital ('nearby'), or open a place or route on the map in the browser ('open'). Times are typical, without live traffic. With no origin, 'here' is this computer's location. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off; 'here' also needs the location sense. (arguments: action, place, destination, origin, mode, what, near, limit)

watch: Your MoYoung/Da Fit smartwatch: 'summary' (steps, distance, calories for 3 days, last night's sleep stages, today's stress, workouts), 'measure' a heart rate, blood oxygen or blood pressure on the wrist (takes up to a minute), read 'settings', 'set' one (step_goal, time_format 12h/24h, units metric/imperial, raise_to_wake, sedentary_reminder, other_app_notifications, power_saving, heart_rate_auto_interval, do_not_disturb '22:00-07:00'), 'sync_time', 'find' (make the watch ring), 'notify' (show a message on the watch), or set the 'profile' (height, weight, age, gender - weight is never measured by the watch). Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, device, what, setting, value, sender, text, kind, height_cm, weight_kg, age, gender)

train.say: When, where and with what camera a photo was taken.
train.positives_desc: photo_metadata: Read a photo's embedded EXIF metadata: the camera and lens, the date and time it was taken, exposure, aperture, ISO, focal length, and the GPS location if one is recorded. Use for 'when was this photo taken', 'does this picture contain my location', 'which camera took it'. JPEG and TIFF. Read-only; the file is not changed. (arguments: path)

negatives.desc: scan_document: Scan a page and return its text (OCR), keeping the image in ~/Documents/Scans. source: 'scanner' (default; list_only lists them), 'camera' (hold the page up to the webcam; it is found and straightened), or 'photo' (straighten and read a picture of a page at path). 'Scan this letter and read it to me.' (arguments: source, path, list_only, device)

edit_image: Edit a picture (for faces or backgrounds use photo_video) and save the result as a new file next to it: resize (width and/or height, or percent), compress (quality, or to under a size in KB), crop, upscale (2-4x), rotate, flip, grayscale, a look (sepia, vignette, sketch, paint, enhance), strip metadata (location/camera), or convert format. Several edits can be combined in one call. For effects that depend on what is in the picture (blur faces, blur the background) use photo_video. (arguments: path, width, height, percent, upscale, quality, max_kb, crop, rotate, flip, grayscale, look, strip_metadata, format)

set_wallpaper: Report or change the GNOME desktop wallpaper, setting the light and dark variants together. Refuses a path that does not exist, rather than leaving a blank desktop with no error. KDE is not supported and will say so. Requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, image)

photo_video: Blur or pixelate faces, blur or remove the background, or find people and objects in a photo or video. negatives.desc: login_history: Recent logins to this machine: which user, from which terminal or remote address, when they started and how long they lasted, and recent reboots. Use for 'who logged in', 'has anyone used my computer'. Requires the 'sessions-sense-enabled' consent key, because it reports other people's presence. Read-only. (arguments: limit)

bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)

landline_call: Place and answer calls on the JioFiber broadband landline over Wi-Fi, through the router - the same line the JioJoin app uses, the house's own landline number. 'status' says whether the line is connected and what call is on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+911234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' picks up a ringing call; 'hangup' ends, cancels or declines the current call. The voice is on this computer's speaker and microphone, nothing is recorded, and the landline handset keeps working. Needs this computer added to the line on the Shani Link app's Phone page and the 'landline-enabled' consent key. This is the landline, not a mobile over Bluetooth - that is 'bluetooth_call'. (arguments: action, number, name)

phone: The user's paired phone via GSConnect/KDE Connect: status (reachable, battery), ring it to find it, ping it, share a file or link to it; read text messages ('messages': latest, from a contact, or unread only); send a text message ('send': to a contact name or number, or omit contact to reply to the latest conversation) with exactly the text given - draft it first; or 'call' a contact or number (opens the phone's dialer). The user confirms every message and call before it goes. Requires the 'phone-control-enabled' consent key; reading needs 'phone-messages-read-enabled', sending and calling 'phone-messages-send-enabled'. (arguments: action, device, target, contact, text, unread_only, limit)

watch: Your MoYoung/Da Fit smartwatch: 'summary' (steps, distance, calories for 3 days, last night's sleep stages, today's stress, workouts), 'measure' a heart rate, blood oxygen or blood pressure on the wrist (takes up to a minute), read 'settings', 'set' one (step_goal, time_format 12h/24h, units metric/imperial, raise_to_wake, sedentary_reminder, other_app_notifications, power_saving, heart_rate_auto_interval, do_not_disturb '22:00-07:00'), 'sync_time', 'find' (make the watch ring), 'notify' (show a message on the watch), or set the 'profile' (height, weight, age, gender - weight is never measured by the watch). Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, device, what, setting, value, sender, text, kind, height_cm, weight_kg, age, gender)

manage_triggers: Arm, list, or remove automatic rules that run a Chronoa action when a perception matches - for example, notify when the battery sense reports low. A rule names one already-whitelisted skill; it cannot run an arbitrary command or an LLM-authored prompt. Use 'setpoints' to list built-in off-by-default proposals, 'describe-setpoint' to explain one, and 'arm-setpoint' to arm one whose own switch is already on; arming never switches one on. Listing and describing need no permission; arming or disarming requires the 'trigger-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds, setpoint)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

train.positives_desc: set_scaling: Report or change the desktop's text scaling factor (1.0 is normal, 1.5 is 150%). Text scaling only - display-resolution and HiDPI scaling are not changed by this, because driving those black-screens sessions. Requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, factor)

negatives.desc: desktop_setting: Read or change one desktop setting from a fixed list: animations (window and menu animations); cursor_size (mouse pointer size in pixels (24 is normal; 32, 48, 64 are larger)); single_click (open files and folders with a single click); clock_24h (show the top-bar clock in 24-hour format); clock_seconds (show seconds in the top-bar clock); battery_percentage (show the battery percentage in the top bar); hot_corner (open the overview when the pointer hits the top-left corner); natural_scroll (touchpad natural (reverse) scrolling); tap_to_click (tap the touchpad to click). Changing requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: setting, value)

generate_image: Make a new picture from a text description, or change a photo the way a description says (from_photo, e.g. 'make it snowy', 'as a watercolour'), drawn locally by stable-diffusion.cpp. Describe it in English. Saves a PNG and returns its path. (arguments: prompt, avoid, size, steps, seed, output, from_photo, strength)

undo_last_change: Put a file or a Chronoa setting back the way Chronoa last found it, by restoring the content or value recorded just before Chronoa's own last change to it. Undoes Chronoa's recent writes only - NOT git history, NOT changes you made in an editor or a shell, and only while a recorded pre-image is still held. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, list, setting, steps)
encode_text: Encode or decode text: base64, url (percent-encoding), hex, binary, rot13, morse. (arguments: text, scheme, direction)
type_text: Type text at the currently focused window. Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key (separate from the vision sense) to be enabled. (arguments: text)
read_text_file: Read a text file and return its contents, optionally a range of lines. Use this to see what a file actually says. (arguments: path, start_line, max_lines)

translate_text: Translate text into another language, with the local model when it is running and a web service otherwise. The reply says which was used, because one sends your text to a third party. (arguments: text, to_language, from_language)

write_text_file: Write text to a file, creating it or replacing its contents. Refuses to replace a non-empty file unless asked to overwrite, and refuses binary data. (arguments: path, content, overwrite, append)

train.say: what did we talk about the router last week?
train.positives_desc: conversations: The user's saved Chronoa conversations. list: recent ones; search: find what was said in earlier conversations (query); open: continue one (which = title or id); new: start a fresh one; rename (which, title); copy: duplicate one to try another way, optionally keeping only its first keep_turns user messages; export: save one as Markdown (path); delete: remove one permanently (needs 'file-delete-enabled'). (arguments: action, which, query, title, path, keep_turns)

negatives.desc: search_my_files: Search your own files by their contents - documents, notes, code - either in a directory you choose with Chronoa's own index, or through the desktop's index (LocalSearch on GNOME, Baloo on Plasma). 'search' (default): what matches a few words. 'desktop': ask the desktop's index instead, needing 'document-search-enabled'. 'reindex': read the directory and build or refresh Chronoa's index (needed before the first search). 'status': what would be indexed and whether this machine can search by meaning. Needs the 'file-index-enabled' consent key for its own index. (arguments: action, query, kind, path, limit)

search_file_contents: Search inside text files under a directory for a literal string, and report which files contain it and on which lines. Skips binary files and very large files, and says how many it skipped. (arguments: text, path, file_pattern, case_sensitive, max_matches)

undo_last_change: Put a file or a Chronoa setting back the way Chronoa last found it, by restoring the content or value recorded just before Chronoa's own last change to it. Undoes Chronoa's recent writes only - NOT git history, NOT changes you made in an editor or a shell, and only while a recorded pre-image is still held. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, list, setting, steps)

web_search: Look something up on the web and return what the pages actually say: facts, prices, how-tos, anything no more specific tool covers. Give a search query, a specific URL, or both. For a scholarly question - a paper, a preprint, prior work, 'what does the research say' - set source=arxiv and it searches the arXiv preprint archive instead of the web. For news headlines use news; to click, fill in or book something on a site use browse. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: query, url, source)

calendar_events: List events on the user's calendars (GNOME calendars and online accounts): today, tomorrow, this week, or the next few hours. Requires the 'calendar-read-enabled' consent key. (arguments: range, hours)

date_math: Date arithmetic: days until a date ('how many days until 25 December'), the date N days/weeks/months from a date ('what date is 45 days from now'), days between two dates, or the weekday of a date. (arguments: operation, date, other_date, amount, unit)

review_proposals: Facts Chronoa noticed in a finished conversation and has NOT saved, listed for the user to keep or discard. Nothing here is remembered until it is kept, and a discarded fact is never offered again. Use this when the user asks what Chronoa thinks it learned, or asks to remember or forget something it noticed last night. (arguments: action, session_id, number)

train.positives_desc: get_clipboard: Read the current contents of the system clipboard.

negatives.desc: set_clipboard: Write text to the system clipboard. (arguments: text)
find_emoji: Find an emoji or symbol by name (heart, thumbs up, rupee sign, arrow) and copy the best match to the clipboard. (arguments: name)
generate_password: Generate a strong random password, or a passphrase of random words, and copy it to the clipboard (it is never said or shown in the reply). (arguments: kind, length, symbols)

train.say: Trim, normalize, change volume or speed.
train.positives_desc: edit_audio: Edit a sound file and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, raise or lower the volume, normalize loudness, change speed, or convert to an audio format. End times accept seconds or 'MM:SS'/'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, volume, normalize, speed, to)

negatives.desc: edit_video: Edit a video and save the result as a new file next to it (never overwriting the original): trim between times, resize to a width, rotate, mute or keep only the audio, or change the speed. End times accept seconds ('95'), or 'MM:SS' / 'HH:MM:SS'. (arguments: path, start, end, width, rotate, mute, audio_only, speed, output)

get_volume: Get the current volume and mute state of an audio output, or the default one. On a machine with more than one output - several monitors, headphones and a dock - 'the volume' is ambiguous, so pass the device exactly as `wpctl status` prints it to ask about a specific one. (arguments: device)
set_volume: Set the system output volume to an exact percentage. (arguments: percent, device)

undo_last_change: Put a file or a Chronoa setting back the way Chronoa last found it, by restoring the content or value recorded just before Chronoa's own last change to it. Undoes Chronoa's recent writes only - NOT git history, NOT changes you made in an editor or a shell, and only while a recorded pre-image is still held. Requires the 'file-edit-enabled' consent key. (arguments: path, list, setting, steps)

fm_radio: FM and AM broadcast radio. Five actions: 'hardware' for whether this computer can receive anything at all (a laptop usually cannot, and that is a true answer rather than a failure - it needs an RTL2832U USB dongle), 'bands' for the coverage, 'tune' to a frequency, 'decode' to demodulate a recorded IQ capture, and 'scan' to look for carriers in one. A frequency is given in MHz, e.g. 98.6. rtl_fm is narrowband and retunes per channel, so it cannot scan - scanning needs a wideband recording. No station names are guessed: a carrier gives a frequency, and naming it would need a table for your region. Requires the 'fm-radio-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, frequency, seconds, file, centre_mhz, out, deemphasis_us)

phone_remote: Press keys on the paired phone as a Bluetooth keyboard: 'press' the camera 'shutter' (takes a photo in the camera app), play_pause, next, previous, volume_up/down, mute; or 'type' text into whatever field is focused on the phone. The phone must have paired 'Chronoa Remote'. Requires the 'phone-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, key, text)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

train.positives_desc: list_percepts: Show what Chronoa is currently perceiving - every fact held about this machine and the user right now, with its age, what expires it, and whether it would be included in the next reply. Use this to check what the assistant actually knows rather than what it says. (arguments: sense_filter, include_expired)

train.say: Add, move or cancel a calendar event.
train.positives_desc: calendar_edit: Change the user's calendar: 'create' adds an event to the default calendar (title, start, optional duration or end, location); 'move' reschedules an event found by its current time and/or title to new_start; 'cancel' deletes one. Times in words: 'tomorrow 3pm', 'friday 5 pm', '2026-10-09 14:00'. Move and cancel ask the person to confirm. Ambiguous matches are refused with the candidates. Requires the 'calendar-write-enabled' consent key (move/cancel also 'calendar-read-enabled'). No invitations are sent. (arguments: action, title, start, duration, end, new_start, location, notes)

negatives.desc: calendar_events: List events on the user's calendars (GNOME calendars and online accounts): today, tomorrow, this week, or the next few hours. Requires the 'calendar-read-enabled' consent key. (arguments: range, hours)
calendar_month: Show the calendar for a month (default this month), with today marked. (arguments: month, year)

(arguments: action, name, sense, match_mode, substring, keywords, actuator, arguments, cooldown_seconds, event_type, source, params, ask_first, retry_policy, debounce_seconds, setpoint)

(arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)
move_pointer: Move the pointer to absolute screen coordinates. Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key (separate from the vision sense) to be enabled. (arguments: x, y)

move_or_copy_file: Move or copy a file or directory to a new path. Moving a directory into itself is refused, and an existing destination is not overwritten unless asked. (arguments: source, destination, mode, overwrite)

kundali: Compute Vedic Kundali (birth chart), Panchang (daily almanac), transits, aspects, dignities, BaZi (Chinese Four Pillars), and Nakshatra details. Offline, no API keys, no external dependencies. panchang: Tithi, Vara, Nakshatra, Yoga, Karana. kundali: sidereal birth chart with planets, houses, Navamsha, Dasha, aspects, dignities. transit: transit positions and cross-aspects. aspects: planetary aspects. dignity: planet dignity in a sign. bazi: Chinese Four Pillars. nakshatra: nakshatra details. timelords: profections and firdaria. arabicparts: Arabic parts (lots). temperament: elemental temperament. lunarmansion: lunar mansion. charakarakas: Jaimini karakas. shadbala: planetary strength. combustion: combust planets. horary: horary chart. upagrahas: all upagrahas. arudha: Arudha padas. drishti: Vedic aspects. vishesha: special lagnas. muhurta: electional scoring. vimshopaka: Vimshopaka bala. cheshta: motion states. grahayuddha: planetary wars. upagrahas_full: all upagrahas. fullchart: complete chart JSON. ashtakavarga: Bhinna + Sarva ashtakavarga. gochara: transit analysis. bhava: house analysis. kalamana: time measurement. chinese: Chinese calendar. grahana: eclipse check. shadbala_full: complete shadbala. karakas_full: chara karakas with Rahu reflection. yogas: Vishesha yogas. nodes: lunar nodes. eclipse: eclipse details. charadasha: Chara dasha. yoginidasha: Yogini dasha. ashtottaridasha: Ashtottari dasha. (arguments: action, date, datetime, latitude, longitude, planet, sign, year, month, day, hour)

train.say: Read a picture's dimensions, format, and colour.
train.positives_desc: read_image: Read a picture's basics out loud: width by height, format, and colour type, plus file size. For what the picture says, use read_document on it. The original is never modified. (arguments: path)

negatives.desc: screenshot: Capture the screen to a PNG file and return the path it was saved to. Refuses when there is no display.

solve_math: Maths: derivative, series (Taylor), expansion, factor, numeric integral (definite, or numeric for indefinite), numeric limit (at a point or oo), linear and quadratic solve, numeric sum of a series, evaluation to N digits, prime_factors / is_prime. Write maths plainly: 'x^2 + 3x', 'sin(x)/x', 'x^2 - 4 = 0'. (arguments: operation, expression, variable, point, lower, upper, order, digits, other)

look_at_image: Look at a picture file and say what it shows, with the local vision model: objects, scenes, charts, screenshots, UI, handwriting. Use a prompt to ask something specific about it. For the exact words printed in a picture, use read_document. Needs the vision sense. (arguments: path, prompt)

create_video: Create a video: a slideshow from a list of pictures (each shown for a few seconds), or a simple clip of a colour for a duration. Writes a new .mp4 next to the inputs; never overwrites. (arguments: images, seconds, color, duration, width)

edit_image: Edit a picture (for faces or backgrounds use photo_video) and save the result as a new file next to it: resize (width and/or height, or percent), compress (quality, or to under a size in KB), crop, upscale (2-4x), rotate, flip, grayscale, a look (sepia, vignette, sketch, paint, enhance), strip metadata (location/camera), or convert format. Several edits can be combined in one call. For effects that depend on what is in the picture (blur faces, blur the background) use photo_video. (arguments: path, width, height, percent, upscale, quality, max_kb, crop, rotate, flip, grayscale, look, strip_metadata, format)

photo_metadata: Read a photo's embedded EXIF metadata: the camera and lens, the date and time it was taken, exposure, aperture, ISO, focal length, and the GPS location if one is recorded. Use for 'when was this photo taken', 'does this picture contain my location', 'which camera took it'. JPEG and TIFF. Read-only; the file is not changed. (arguments: path)

train.positives_desc: press_key: Press a key or key combination in the focused window, e.g. 'Return', 'Escape', 'Tab' or 'ctrl+shift+t'. This sends a key, not text - use type_text to type a string. Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key. X11 only. (arguments: key, repeat)

The phone must have paired 'Chronoa Remote'. Requires the 'phone-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, key, text)

ui_elements: Use another app's controls by what they are, through the accessibility tree. apps: which apps are reachable. inspect: list a window's buttons, fields, menus and labels with ids (app = its name; query narrows by text). press: activate an element by id (a button, checkbox, link, menu item). set_text: put text in a field by id. read: an element's text or value. menu: open a menu path like 'File > Export'. drive: one turn of driving - give an action and a control number and the reply is the app's new state in the same short numbered form, which is what a small model can act on. act: click, type or key an app by name or position, with a visible cursor. state: the numbered controls an app is showing. Works on a container's app and on this desktop's own apps alike. Requires 'input-control-enabled'; drive start also runs a container, so it needs 'container-control-enabled' as well. (arguments: action, app, id, text, query, path, do, how, number, image, keys, x, y)

ir_remote: Send and receive infrared remote-control codes, and build or read the pulse-space timings themselves. 'devices': is there IR hardware here (most machines have none, and that is a true answer). 'encode': turn an address and command into the NEC or RC-6 timings that would carry them. 'decode': turn timings into a code. 'send': transmit a code through an IR device. 'receive': capture a button press and decode it. Needs the 'ir-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, protocol, address, command, timings, seconds)

accessibility: Turn an accessibility feature on or off, or report them all: screen reader, on-screen keyboard, magnifier (zoom), large text, high contrast, reduce motion (animations), sticky keys. (arguments: feature, enabled)

airplane_mode: Report which radios (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile broadband) are on, or turn airplane mode on (all radios off) or off. Changing requires the 'radio-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

maps: OpenStreetMap maps: find where a place is ('find'), driving/walking/cycling directions ('directions') or just distance and time ('travel_time') between places, the nearest kind of place such as petrol pump, hotel, ATM or hospital ('nearby'), or open a place or route on the map in the browser ('open'). (arguments: action, place, destination, origin, mode, what, near, limit)

install_app: Search Flathub for an app, or install / remove one for this user by its app ID (e.g. org.videolan.VLC, from a search). Installing and removing need the 'app-install-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, query, app_id)

cloud_files: See what is in this machine's configured cloud storage remotes - which remotes rclone knows, how many objects and bytes each holds, and what is at the top level of one. Use for 'what is in my cloud drive', 'is anything in the bucket', 'how big is my remote'. Read-only: it never copies, syncs or deletes anything. A machine with no remotes says so, because that means there is nowhere off-machine for anything to go. (arguments: remote, path)

default_apps: Show or change which application opens a kind of file - by MIME type ('application/pdf'), extension ('.pdf', 'mp4') or an example file - or the default web browser (target 'browser'). Use for 'what opens PDFs', 'make VLC open my videos', 'set Firefox as my default browser'. Changing a default requires the 'default-apps-enabled' consent key; showing one does not. (arguments: target, action, app)

train.say: What it can do right now.
train.positives_desc: list_capabilities: Report what this assistant can do right now, and which of those need a setting switched on first. Reads the live skill registry and the live consent values rather than a fixed list, so a skill that is not installed, or a permission that is off, is shown as such. Changes nothing.

negatives.desc: arrange_window: Arrange a window: tile (snap it to the left, right, top or bottom half of the screen - 'put it on the left half', side by side), minimize, maximize, unmaximize, make fullscreen, leave fullscreen, move, resize, or send it to another workspace - by window id from list_windows or by part of its title. tile takes side; move takes x and y, resize width and height (pixels), set_workspace a 0-based workspace. Nothing is closed; close_window does that. (arguments: action, window_id, title_contains, x, y, width, height, workspace, side)
click_pointer: Click a mouse button at the current pointer position. Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key (separate from the vision sense) to be enabled. (arguments: button, count)

scroll: Scroll the window under the pointer up, down, left or right by a number of wheel steps (move the pointer over it first). Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key (separate from the vision sense). (arguments: direction, amount)

ask_user: Ask the user a clarifying question and wait for their answer, with 2 to 4 short options they can pick. Use this whenever a request is genuinely ambiguous - especially when several files or devices could match. Do not guess instead, and do not ask when one option is obviously right. In a headless session there is nobody to answer and this will say so. (arguments: question, options)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

chart: Make an SVG file from data, drawn on this computer with no install. chart: kind=bar|line|pie with data (bar/pie: [[label, number], ...]; line: [[x, y], ...], or several lines as series {name: [[x, y], ...]}), plus title, x_label, y_label. icon: a stroke icon by name (arrow-right, bell, calendar, check, clock, close, download, folder, heart, home, mail, search, settings, star, user). diagram: a top-to-bottom flow, steps=["Read", "Edit", "Test"] with optional arrows [[from, to, label], ...]. output is the .svg path, e.g. '~/Pictures/sales.svg'. (arguments: action, output, kind, data, series, steps, arrows, name, title, x_label, y_label)

list_percepts: Show what Chronoa is currently perceiving - every fact held about this machine and the user right now, with its age, what expires it, and whether it would be included in the next reply. Use this to check what the assistant actually knows rather than what it says. (arguments: sense_filter, include_expired)

train.positives_desc: ask_user: Ask the user a clarifying question and wait for their answer, with 2 to 4 short options they can pick. Use this whenever a request is genuinely ambiguous - especially when several files or devices could match. Do not guess instead, and do not ask when one option is obviously right. In a headless session there is nobody to answer and this will say so. (arguments: question, options)

negatives.desc: analyze_table: Ask questions of a .csv, .tsv, .xlsx or .json (list of records) file with read-only SQLite SQL. describe: the tables, columns, types, row counts and a sample - do this first. query: run one SELECT (the table is `data`, or one table per sheet name for a workbook); save_as='~/x.csv' or .xlsx keeps the full result. chart: bar, line or pie chart saved as .svg from a SELECT returning (label, value) columns. (arguments: action, path, sql, save_as, kind, title, output)

json_query: Ask questions about the shape of a JSON document: what keys it has, what a field contains, how many entries an array has, or the sum/unique/sorted values of an array. Give either a file path or paste the document itself. (arguments: path, document, field, operation, of)

fingerprint_status: Whether fingerprint login is set up on this machine, and which fingers are enrolled. Says which of the four real states it is in: no reader attached, reader present but nothing enrolled, fingers enrolled, or the daemon not running and the question unanswerable. Reading only - it never enrolls or deletes a fingerprint, because 'which fingers are enrolled' is a question and the other two are not. Needs no permission: it reports a machine's own login configuration, and the answer is about hardware and a per-user setting rather than anything private. (arguments: user)

list_processes: List the processes running on this machine, with their pid, name, owner, CPU and memory use, sorted by CPU unless sort_by says otherwise. Use this to find what is using the machine - pass sort_by='memory' for the RAM question, which CPU order does not answer - or the pid of something you want to stop. (arguments: name_filter, sort_by, limit)

manage_goals: Save a multi-step goal as a plan of tool steps that can be run later from the Goals panel, list saved goals, answer one that is waiting for you, or remove one. Saving runs nothing. Each step names a tool, its arguments, and a name for its result; a later step can use an earlier result as $name in a string argument, and lists the names it depends_on. A depends_on name that no earlier step produces is a question for the user: the goal waits there until they answer it. Requires the 'goals-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, goal, steps, id, answer)

web_search: Look something up on the web and return what the pages actually say: facts, prices, how-tos, anything no more specific tool covers. Give a search query, a specific URL, or both. For a scholarly question - a paper, a preprint, prior work, 'what does the research say' - set source=arxiv and it searches the arXiv preprint archive instead of the web. For news headlines use news; to click, fill in or book something on a site use browse. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: query, url, source)

apply_patch: Apply a .patch or .diff file to files on this machine. Use for 'apply this diff', 'here is a patch', 'merge this change in'. Runs a dry run by default and changes nothing until asked. Reports when the patch is already applied, which is a refusal rather than a reverse-applied change, and lists the .rej files patch leaves for hunks it could not apply. Never prompts. (arguments: patch, path, strip, action)

train.say: Minimize, maximize, move or resize a window.
train.positives_desc: arrange_window: Arrange a window: tile (snap it to the left, right, top or bottom half of the screen - 'put it on the left half', side by side), minimize, maximize, unmaximize, make fullscreen, leave fullscreen, move, resize, or send it to another workspace - by window id from list_windows or by part of its title. tile takes side; move takes x and y, resize width and height (pixels), set_workspace a 0-based workspace. Nothing is closed; close_window does that. (arguments: action, window_id, title_contains, x, y, width, height, workspace, side)

negatives.desc: close_window: Ask a window to close, the way its close button would - the application still gets the chance to ask about unsaved work. Requires the 'window-close-enabled' consent key. Works on X11, Plasma and GNOME (GTK4 apps, or any app with Chronoa's window control extension). (arguments: window_id, title_contains)
move_pointer: Move the pointer to absolute screen coordinates. Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key (separate from the vision sense) to be enabled. (arguments: x, y)

focus_window: Bring a window to the front and give it keyboard focus, by window id from list_windows or by matching part of its title. Works on X11 and Plasma; on GNOME it needs Chronoa's window control extension and says so. (arguments: window_id, title_contains)

move_or_copy_file: Move or copy a file or directory to a new path. Moving a directory into itself is refused, and an existing destination is not overwritten unless asked. (arguments: source, destination, mode, overwrite)

media_control: Control music and video players: play, pause, toggle, next track, previous track, stop, restart (current track from the beginning), seek (skip ahead or go back by 'seconds'; negative goes back), or 'status' to say what is playing. (arguments: action, seconds)

drag: Drag with the left button held from one pixel position to another - to select text, move an item, or resize by its edge. Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key (separate from the vision sense). (arguments: sx, sy, ex, ey)

list_windows: List the windows currently open, with their title, class and geometry. Pass title_contains to narrow the list to windows matching some text in their title or application - a desktop usually has more windows open than are worth reading. Where xdotool cannot see the session it falls back to the accessibility bus and says so, because that list is not complete. (arguments: title_contains)

train.positives_desc: check_updates: Check whether this machine has package updates waiting, without installing anything and without needing root. Works on Arch and other pacman systems.

negatives.desc: firmware_updates: List firmware updates fwupd knows for this machine's devices (BIOS, SSD, dock, touchpad...) and what each fixes, plus the firmware versions this machine is running. Read-only; nothing is installed.

system_info: Describe the machine Chronoa is running on: distribution, kernel, architecture, uptime, load, memory, CPU count, whether this is a desktop session or a container, and the hardware identity (make, model, board, BIOS version).
get_clipboard: Read the current contents of the system clipboard.
set_clipboard: Write text to the system clipboard. (arguments: text)

control_service: Start, stop, restart, reload, enable or disable a system service, then read its state back so the reply says whether it actually came up. Requires the 'service-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: unit, action)

list_services: List system services with their load and active state, optionally filtered by name, newest state first for anything running. Reports UNKNOWN on a machine that is not systemd-managed. (arguments: name_filter, failed_only)

open_settings: Open the system Settings app at a specific page, e.g. 'wifi', 'bluetooth', 'display', 'sound', 'power', 'privacy', 'keyboard', 'mouse', 'touchpad', 'printers', 'users', 'about', 'date_time', 'region', 'notifications', 'background', 'accessibility'. GNOME and KDE Plasma. Use open_application for Settings without a page. (arguments: page)

train.say: Find, ping or send a file to your paired phone.
train.positives_desc: phone: The user's paired phone via GSConnect/KDE Connect: status (reachable, battery), ring it to find it, ping it, share a file or link to it; read text messages ('messages': latest, from a contact, or unread only); send a text message ('send': to a contact name or number, or omit contact to reply to the latest conversation) with exactly the text given - draft it first; or 'call' a contact or number (opens the phone's dialer). The user confirms every message and call before it goes. Requires the 'phone-control-enabled' consent key; reading needs 'phone-messages-read-enabled', sending and calling 'phone-messages-send-enabled'. (arguments: action, device, target, contact, text, unread_only, limit)

negatives.desc: lan_phone: Find phones on the SAME Wi-Fi network, using the KDE Connect protocol directly - so it works without KDE Connect or GSConnect installed. 'devices': what announced itself on this network in the last few seconds (phones, tablets, other computers). 'announce': make this computer findable by a phone's KDE Connect app. 'status': what this computer can and cannot do on the LAN. 'pair': pair with the device 'devices' found (the phone asks its owner). Needs the 'lan-phone-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, seconds)

phone_remote: Press keys on the paired phone as a Bluetooth keyboard: 'press' the camera 'shutter' (takes a photo in the camera app), play_pause, next, previous, volume_up/down, mute; or 'type' text into whatever field is focused on the phone. The phone must have paired 'Chronoa Remote'. Requires the 'phone-remote-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, key, text)

screen_to_phone: Show this computer's screen on a paired phone, over the Bluetooth network. 'status': could this be shared here at all, and what is missing if not. 'start': ask the desktop to share the screen and serve it to the phone - the desktop shows its own 'Share screen' dialog, which only the person can answer. 'stop': end it and close the portal session. The picture goes over Bluetooth, so it is not on Wi-Fi, but it is the whole screen - which is why this needs the 'screen-share-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

adb_workflow: A small Android Debug Bridge workflow. status: connected devices and their state; pair: the steps to authorise this computer; push and pull: copy one file between this computer and the phone. Needs 'phone-control-enabled' and a yes for each copy. Local paths stay inside your home; remote paths must be under /sdcard/. (arguments: action, serial, local, remote)

find_device: Make a paired Bluetooth watch, band or tag buzz or ring so the person can find it - 'where is my watch', 'find my band'. Works on devices with the standard Immediate Alert service and on MoYoung (Da Fit) watches; anything else is refused rather than sent an unknown command. The device must be in range. Requires the 'bluetooth-gatt-enabled' consent key. (arguments: device)

bluetooth_call: Use a paired Android phone as a Bluetooth speakerphone, with no cable and no app on the phone. 'status' says whether a phone is connected as a hands-free unit, whether a call is in progress, and which audio profile its call audio arrived on. 'dial' places a call - 'dial number="+441234567890"' - asking you to confirm first, because it rings someone. 'answer' and 'hangup' work on a call already in progress. 'audio' reports where the call's voice is going and names anything missing from that path, and 'profile' switches the card between wide-band hfp_hf and narrow-band hsp_hs. The phone stays the radio; this routes the voice to this computer's speakers and microphone. Needs the phone connected over Bluetooth, not merely paired, and the 'bluetooth-call-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action, card, profile, to, number)

email_send: Send a plain-text email through the locally configured SMTP server. Needs 'to' and 'body'; 'subject' is optional. Needs the 'email-send-enabled' consent key and asks before sending. No account or credential is built in. (arguments: to, subject, body)

train.positives_desc: control_service: Start, stop, restart, reload, enable or disable a system service, then read its state back so the reply says whether it actually came up. Requires the 'service-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: unit, action)

negatives.desc: open_application: Open or launch an installed application by name or by kind, e.g. 'firefox', 'files', 'settings', 'music player', 'text editor'. Not for websites: use browse to open a site and work on it. (arguments: name)

open_file: Open one specific file or folder (by its path) using the desktop's default application for it - the same thing double-clicking it would do. To launch an app such as the file manager, use open_application. (arguments: path)

open_settings: Open the system Settings app at a specific page, e.g. 'wifi', 'bluetooth', 'display', 'sound', 'power', 'privacy', 'keyboard', 'mouse', 'touchpad', 'printers', 'users', 'about', 'date_time', 'region', 'notifications', 'background', 'accessibility'. GNOME and KDE Plasma. Use open_application for Settings without a page. (arguments: page)

media_control: Control music and video players: play, pause, toggle, next track, previous track, stop, restart (current track from the beginning), seek (skip ahead or go back by 'seconds'; negative goes back), or 'status' to say what is playing. (arguments: action, seconds)

screen_to_phone: Show this computer's screen on a paired phone, over the Bluetooth network. 'status': could this be shared here at all, and what is missing if not. 'start': ask the desktop to share the screen and serve it to the phone - the desktop shows its own 'Share screen' dialog, which only the person can answer. 'stop': end it and close the portal session. The picture goes over Bluetooth, so it is not on Wi-Fi, but it is the whole screen - which is why this needs the 'screen-share-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)
stopwatch: A stopwatch: start, lap, read the time so far, or stop. (arguments: action)

ui_elements: Use another app's controls by what they are, through the accessibility tree. apps: which apps are reachable. inspect: list a window's buttons, fields, menus and labels with ids (app = its name; query narrows by text). press: activate an element by id (a button, checkbox, link, menu item). set_text: put text in a field by id. read: an element's text or value. menu: open a menu path like 'File > Export'. drive: one turn of driving - give an action and a control number and the reply is the app's new state in the same short numbered form, which is what a small model can act on. act: click, type or key an app by name or position, with a visible cursor. state: the numbered controls an app is showing. Works on a container's app and on this desktop's own apps alike. Requires 'input-control-enabled'; drive start also runs a container, so it needs 'container-control-enabled' as well. (arguments: action, app, id, text, query, path, do, how, number, image, keys, x, y)

train.positives_desc: click_pointer: Click a mouse button at the current pointer position. Requires the 'input-control-enabled' consent key (separate from the vision sense) to be enabled. (arguments: button, count)

negatives.desc: close_window: Ask a window to close, the way its close button would - the application still gets the chance to ask about unsaved work. Requires the 'window-close-enabled' consent key. Works on X11, Plasma and GNOME (GTK4 apps, or any app with Chronoa's window control extension). (arguments: window_id, title_contains)

desktop_setting: Read or change one desktop setting from a fixed list: animations (window and menu animations); cursor_size (mouse pointer size in pixels (24 is normal; 32, 48, 64 are larger)); single_click (open files and folders with a single click); clock_24h (show the top-bar clock in 24-hour format); clock_seconds (show seconds in the top-bar clock); battery_percentage (show the battery percentage in the top bar); hot_corner (open the overview when the pointer hits the top-left corner); natural_scroll (touchpad natural (reverse) scrolling); tap_to_click (tap the touchpad to click). Changing requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: setting, value)

Works on a container's app and on this desktop's own apps alike. Requires 'input-control-enabled'; drive start also runs a container, so it needs 'container-control-enabled' as well. (arguments: action, app, id, text, query, path, do, how, number, image, keys, x, y)

(arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

Where xdotool cannot see the session it falls back to the accessibility bus and says so, because that list is not complete. (arguments: title_contains)

train.positives_desc: set_timer: Set a countdown timer that sends a desktop notification when it finishes; list pending timers, say how much time is left, add or take off time, pause, resume, reset to the original length, and cancel. With one timer pending, 'my timer' needs no id. The countdown is owned by systemd, so it fires even if the assistant is closed. It is refused rather than silently accepted when systemd is unavailable, because a timer recorded as pending that will never fire is the same lie as a camera reported as disabled when it is not. (arguments: action, seconds, label, id)

negatives.desc: autostart_entries: Report everything on this machine that starts automatically: the autostart .desktop files in this user's home and /etc/xdg, the enabled systemd user units and timers, and the crontab. Use for 'what starts automatically', 'what runs at login', 'what is scheduled', 'why does this thing keep running', 'what did I set to start on its own'. Honours Hidden, OnlyShowIn and NotShowIn, and says 'cannot tell' rather than guessing when the desktop is unknown - which is the normal state outside a login session. Read-only; nothing is enabled, disabled or changed.

set_screensaver: Report or change how long the machine waits before the screen blanks, and whether it then demands a password. The two are reported separately, because blanking without locking leaves anyone who walks up to the machine able to use it. Requires the 'idle-timeout-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, blank_after_minutes, lock)

alarm: Alarm clock: set an alarm at a time of day (once, or repeating daily/weekdays/weekends/chosen days), list alarms, say when the next one is, change one's time or label, snooze the one that just rang, or delete one. Examples: 'set an alarm for 7am', 'alarm for 6:30 on weekdays', 'when is my next alarm?', 'change my 7am alarm to 7:30', 'snooze', 'delete the 7am alarm'. Times may be words ('7am', '7:30 pm', 'tomorrow 6:45'). It rings with a notification and the alarm sound even if the assistant is closed; it is held by systemd --user, so a reboot drops it until alarms are next listed, which re-arms it. (arguments: action, time, label, repeat, id, new_time, new_label, minutes)

print_queue: Show the printers, which one is the default, the print jobs still waiting, and what this machine can print to even when nothing is configured; or cancel a waiting job by its id. Use for 'what's printing', 'why isn't my printer there', 'what can I print to', 'cancel that print'. Cancelling requires the 'print-control-enabled' consent key; listing does not. (arguments: action, job, printer, option)

set_brightness: Get or set screen brightness as a percentage. With no level, reports the current brightness of each panel. With a level, sets it. Writing needs root - the backlight node is root-owned - and a permission failure is reported as such rather than as success. (arguments: level)
set_clipboard: Write text to the system clipboard. (arguments: text)

desktop_setting: Read or change one desktop setting from a fixed list: animations (window and menu animations); cursor_size (mouse pointer size in pixels (24 is normal; 32, 48, 64 are larger)); single_click (open files and folders with a single click); clock_24h (show the top-bar clock in 24-hour format); clock_seconds (show seconds in the top-bar clock); battery_percentage (show the battery percentage in the top bar); hot_corner (open the overview when the pointer hits the top-left corner); natural_scroll (touchpad natural (reverse) scrolling); tap_to_click (tap the touchpad to click). Changing requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: setting, value)

train.positives_desc: set_theme: Report or change whether the desktop uses a light or dark appearance, on GNOME or KDE. Reports the applied theme separately from the preference, because setting the preference does not make every application follow it. Requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action)

negatives.desc: airplane_mode: Report which radios (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile broadband) are on, or turn airplane mode on (all radios off) or off. Changing requires the 'radio-control-enabled' consent key. (arguments: action)

browse: Open a website and do things on it for the person: find information, fill in forms, click through. Drive a web browser: navigate, read the page's text (get_text), click, type, select options, scroll, move through history, take screenshots and wait for conditions. While Chronoa's window is open this is the in-app browser the user can watch: there it opens only http(s) pages the egress policy allows, and key, hover, drag, upload_file, tabs and evaluate are not available. Otherwise it is a headless Chromium with all actions. Requires the web sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off. (arguments: action, url, selector, text, key, value, label, files, x, y, to_x, to_y, to_selector, delta_x, delta_y, steps, repeat, tab_id, path, wait_for, timeout, settle)

toggle_wifi: Turn the Wi-Fi radio on or off (only Wi-Fi - airplane_mode switches every radio, connect_wifi joins a network), or report whether Wi-Fi is on. Changing requires the 'radio-control-enabled' consent key; status needs no permission. (arguments: action)

set_wallpaper: Report or change the GNOME desktop wallpaper, setting the light and dark variants together. Refuses a path that does not exist, rather than leaving a blank desktop with no error. KDE is not supported and will say so. Requires the 'appearance-control-enabled' consent key; reporting needs no such permission. (arguments: action, image)

convert_currency: Convert an amount of money between currencies (rupees, dollars, euros, pounds, yen, ...) at today's ECB reference rate. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off. (arguments: amount, from_currency, to_currency)

get_location: Where this computer is right now - latitude, longitude and accuracy - from a GPS receiver or GNOME's location service. Use for 'where am I'. Requires the location sense to be enabled and privacy mode to be off.
lookup_wikipedia: Who or what something is - a person, place, thing or event - from Wikipedia's summary. Requires the web sense and privacy mode off. (arguments: topic)
